# Changelog Archive

Detailed, per-phase write-ups live here — not in CLAUDE.md. This file is read by
Claude Code only when a phase touches a file, module, or pattern already logged
under one of the headings below. It is not read by default at session start.

When a project has been stable in real use for a while, tell Claude Code to
compress that project's section down to just the reusable lessons (move those
lessons into CLAUDE.md's Conventions section) and delete the rest.

## Revised Cross-check pending plan — 2026-09-02

The Cross-check matrix, field selection, persistence, and Verification result functionality are
complete. Their development phases are retired from `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`; only acceptance,
correctness review, performance, safety, regression, and closeout phases remain active there.

The revised plan adds a configurable Verification Data Field policy before performance optimization.
Vendor, Item, Unit of Measurement, Quantity, Rate, and Amount are the core fields; Audit Rules may
add optional active Master Columns by Low/Medium/High risk level and order, with unavailable fields
shown explicitly. The backend must derive the allowed projection and targeted search fields rather
than accepting arbitrary browser requests.

This file was assembled on 2026-07-25 from the previous single-file CLAUDE.md's
Conventions and Status log sections, split out project-by-project so CLAUDE.md
itself could go back to being lean. Entries below are the original, unedited
write-ups — nothing was reworded, only relocated and grouped.

---

## Cross-Check Matrix Redesign

**Requirement:** Rebuild the Audit Rules Cross-Check feature as a document × field matrix —
Documents are columns, user-added field rows have no stored label (row ID + order only), and each
cell holds a column name picked from that Document's linked template (empty cell = not applicable).
Also removes the duplicate cross-check-eligible fields section from the Documents tab. Old
cross-check data is discarded/rebuilt, not migrated. 5 phases: (1) DB storage, (2) backend CRUD +
template column-list lookup, (3) remove Documents-tab fields section, (4) build matrix UI,
(5) wire UI to backend.

### Phase 1 of 5 — DB storage

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `database.py` (committed). Schema test class
`CrossCheckMatrixSchemaTests` written and passing but **held out of this commit** — it shares
`tests/test_audit_rulebook.py` with an in-flight Phase 4 of the earlier per-document-field
requirement; it lands with a later commit. Backup:
`scratchpad/test_audit_rulebook_with_matrix.py`.

Additive schema change — two new tables in both `init_db()` (SQLite) and `init_db_postgres()`:

- `audit_rule_cross_check_fields` — the row axis. `id`, `cross_check_id` (FK → `audit_rule_cross_checks`,
  `ON DELETE CASCADE`), `sort_order`. No label column; a row is identified by its id, order by
  `sort_order`.
- `audit_rule_cross_check_cells` — one row per (field row × Document) cell. `id`,
  `field_id` (FK → `audit_rule_cross_check_fields`, CASCADE), `document_id` (FK →
  `audit_rule_documents`, CASCADE), `column_name TEXT` nullable (`NULL`/missing cell = not
  applicable), `UNIQUE(field_id, document_id)`. `column_name` is free text, not FK'd — validity
  against the Document's linked template is a Phase 2 backend concern, matching how the existing
  `compare_field` columns are already free text.

Indexes: `idx_audit_rule_cross_check_fields_crosscheck`, `idx_audit_rule_cross_check_cells_field`.

The document column axis reuses the existing `audit_rule_cross_check_documents` junction unchanged.

**Deliberately deferred to Phase 2:** the old `compare_field` columns on `audit_rule_cross_checks`
and `audit_rule_cross_check_documents` are left in place this phase so `routers/audit_rules.py`
(untouched here) and the current tests keep working. No data migration/purge code — old rows are
discarded as a separate cleanup later. Confirmed with Aadil: additive, keep old columns.

`CrossCheckMatrixSchemaTests` covers table shapes, `column_name` NULL, the
`UNIQUE(field_id, document_id)` constraint, and cell CASCADE on field-row delete (the CASCADE
test enables `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` locally since the app never does).

### Phase 2 of 5 — matrix CRUD + column lookup

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/templates.py`,
`tests/test_audit_rulebook.py` (the held-back schema tests land here too).

**Scope change from the brief, confirmed with Aadil:** the brief assumed the old `compare_field`
columns get dropped this phase. They don't — they're still consumed by the flat Cross-check CRUD,
`compile_verification_rulebook()`, the `verification.py` cross-check evaluation engine, guidance
emission, the frontend editor, and tests, and no phase in the 5-phase plan rewires the engine to
the matrix. The column drop is deferred to a later phase (after the matrix UI lands and a phase
migrates the engine). This phase is purely additive.

Also: the superseded in-flight "per-document field names Phase 4" WIP
(`routers/audit_rules.py` + `verification.py` + two test files) was **discarded** (`git restore`)
— the matrix generalises that concept, so finishing the old approach is wasted work.

New endpoints (all in `routers/audit_rules.py` unless noted; mutations gated by
`ensure_no_active_verification_sessions` + `invalidate_audit_rules_cache`, cross-checks are
global so no `client_id`):

- `GET /api/audit-rules/cross-checks/{id}/matrix` — one call returns ordered document columns
  (`document_id`, `name`, `template_id`, `sort_order`) + ordered field rows, each row's `cells`
  as `{ "<document_id>": "<column_name|null>" }`. Read-through the `cache_get`/`cache_set` layer,
  key `cross_checks:matrix:{id}`.
- `POST /api/audit-rules/cross-checks/{id}/fields` — append a label-less field row
  (`sort_order` = current max + 1). Returns `{field_id}`.
- `DELETE /api/audit-rules/cross-check-fields/{field_id}` — deletes the row; clears its cells
  explicitly first (FKs aren't enforced on this app's connections; Postgres would cascade anyway).
- `PUT /api/audit-rules/cross-checks/{id}/field-order` — body `{field_ids: [...]}`, must be an
  exact permutation of the cross-check's current field-row ids (400 otherwise); rewrites
  `sort_order` = list index.
- `PUT /api/audit-rules/cross-check-fields/{field_id}/cells/{document_id}` — body
  `{column_name}`. 404 unknown field row; 400 if the document isn't a column of that cross-check;
  400 if a non-empty `column_name` isn't a real column on the document's linked template. Non-empty
  → `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (field_id, document_id) DO UPDATE`; empty/None → `DELETE` the cell
  (= not applicable).
- `GET /api/templates/{template_id}/columns` (`routers/templates.py`) — thin wrapper over the
  existing `get_cached_template_columns()` (shared TTL-cached column source); returns
  `[{column_id, column_name, data_type, sort_order}]`, 404 on inactive/missing template. The
  reusable "column-list by template" the matrix UI (Phase 4) calls per distinct `template_id`.

Helpers: `get_document_template_columns(document_id)` (resolves `template_id`, reuses
`get_cached_template_columns` via a local import to keep the router import graph acyclic),
`validate_cross_check_cell()`, `get_cross_check_matrix()`. Models: `CrossCheckFieldOrder`,
`CrossCheckCellUpdate`. Full suite: 83 passed.

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `static/audit_rules.html`, `static/audit_rules.js`,
`static/style.css`. **UI-only.**

The Documents detail form's "Cross-Checks" section — a single read-only "Cross-check-eligible
Fields (automatic mirror)" chip list of every active Master Column — is removed. It duplicated
what the Cross-Check tab now derives per-document from the linked template, and it isn't what the
matrix reads.

Removed from `audit_rules.js`: `fieldsState`, `renderFieldChips()`, `fetchActiveMasterColumns()`,
`refreshFieldsMirror()`, the three element refs, two already-commented-out legacy blocks, the
`cross_check_fields` key from `saveDocument()`'s payload, and the "losing its mirrored
cross-check-eligible fields" clause from the physical-bill switch confirm (the linked-template
clause stays). `updateDocumentTypeVisibility()` and the type-change listener no longer touch the
removed section. From `style.css`: the orphaned `.ar-chip-warning` rule (`.ar-chip*` base classes
stay — shared with Authorisation Roles / Category Cross-checks). `audit_rules.js?v=8 → ?v=9`.

**Left in place (confirmed with Aadil):** the Document `cross_check_fields` backend storage and
the `audit_rule_document_fields` table — a later cleanup phase retires them. `DocumentCreate` /
`DocumentUpdate` default `cross_check_fields` to `[]`, so omitting the payload key is safe;

**Side effect:** each Document save now writes an empty `audit_rule_document_fields` list through

Verification: 83 tests pass (no backend change); `node --check` clean; no orphaned references to

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `static/audit_rules.html`, `static/audit_rules.js`,
`static/style.css`. **UI-only, mock state — no save/load (Phase 5).**

`static/audit_rules.js` — new: `matrixState {columns:[{documentId,name}], rows:[{id,cells:{}}]}`,

`static/style.css` — `.ar-matrix-wrap` (`overflow-x:auto`), `.ar-matrix-table` + th/td borders,

Verification: 83 tests pass; `node --check` clean. Playwright against the dev server confirmed:

### Phase 5 of 5 — wire the matrix UI to the backend (COMPLETE)

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `routers/audit_rules.py`, `static/audit_rules.js`,
`static/audit_rules.html`, `tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`.

The matrix now loads from and saves to real endpoints; every edit persists immediately.
Save/Delete/Restore restored, preview banner and stopgap `saveCrossCheck()` gone.

**Confirmed with Aadil:** all-immediate persistence; create-first for a new cross-check (matrix
disabled with `#arMatrixNeedsSaveHint` until Name + Comparison Type are saved); two lean new
backend endpoints (the brief assumed JS-only, but the old flat CRUD can't set the column axis or
save Name/Type without the deferred `compare_field` model).

**Backend** — `routers/audit_rules.py`:
- `PUT /api/audit-rules/cross-checks/{id}/documents` (`CrossCheckDocuments {document_ids}`) —
  `save_cross_check_column_axis()` replaces the `audit_rule_cross_check_documents` junction
  (`compare_field` NULL) and deletes any `audit_rule_cross_check_cells` row left pointing at a
  dropped document. 404 missing cc, 400 unknown document id.
- `PUT /api/audit-rules/cross-checks/{id}/meta` (`CrossCheckMeta {name, comparison_type,
  compare_to_voucher_line}`) — scalar `UPDATE` only, leaves `compare_field` untouched. 404, 400
  on a bad `comparison_type`.
- Create still uses `POST /api/audit-rules/cross-checks`; the frontend sends
  `compare_field: "(matrix)"` + `document_ids: []` so the deferred flat-model validation passes.

**Frontend** — `static/audit_rules.js`:
- `selectCrossCheck` fetches `GET .../{id}/matrix`; `loadMatrixFromServer()` populates
  `matrixState` (row `id` is now the backend `field_id`; `matrixRowSeq` removed).
- `renderMatrix()` early-returns a disabled state when `!editingCrossCheckId`.
- Optimistic `matrixPersist(doRequest, undo)` wrapper: `addMatrixColumn`/`removeMatrixColumn` →
  `PUT .../documents`; `addMatrixRow` → `POST .../fields`; `removeMatrixRow` →
  `DELETE .../cross-check-fields/{id}`; `moveMatrixRow` → `PUT .../field-order`; cell `<select>`
  change → `PUT .../cross-check-fields/{id}/cells/{documentId}` with `{column_name: value||null}`.
  Any failure rolls the local change back and shows the error.
- `saveCrossCheck(triggerBtn)`: new → POST (filler) → `selectCrossCheck(newId)`; existing →
  `PUT .../meta` + `loadCrossChecks()`.

`static/audit_rules.html`: `#arMatrixPreviewBanner` → `#arMatrixNeedsSaveHint`;
`audit_rules.js?v=10 → ?v=11`.

**Verification:** `node --check` clean; 88 pytest pass (5 new endpoint tests). Full Playwright
end-to-end against a **local** server instance (booted on :5057 with `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` since
the persistent :5000 server predates Phase 2): new-cc gate → Save creates + enables the matrix →
add 2 columns / 2 rows / set a real template-column cell → **reload + reselect shows columns,
rows and the cell value all persisted**; reorder rows persists (`field-order`); remove a column
persists and its orphaned cell is cleaned; Save renames via `/meta` and the list relabels;
Delete/Restore work. No console or page errors. (Earlier "failures" during the pass were test
timing — checking server state before a cold-Postgres PUT committed; adding `expect_response`
waits resolved them.)

**Requirement COMPLETE.** Remaining deferred work (own future phases): drop the
`audit_rule_cross_checks.compare_field` / junction `compare_field` columns once the
`verification.py` cross-check evaluation engine + rulebook compiler + guidance are migrated to
read the matrix; retire the now-unused Document `cross_check_fields` storage +
`audit_rule_document_fields` table.

## Cross-check per-document field names

**Superseded 2026-09-01 by the Cross-Check Matrix Redesign (above).** Phases 1–3 shipped
(commits `ffe8b12`, `e87d586`, `a52a615`); Phase 4 (engine/guidance wiring) was in progress,
never committed, and discarded — the matrix generalises per-document field names, so the flat
`compare_field` model is on its way out entirely.

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `database.py`, `tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`.

Confirmed 4-phase requirement. Cross-checks currently force one shared `compare_field` name
across every Document in the chain. Quantity fields are now named differently per stage
("Quantity" for PO / Purchase Demand vs "Quantity Received" for Store Receiving / Vendor Bill),
so a Cross-check must support a different field name per Document, matched by chain
position / comparison intent rather than by identical name.

**Phase 1 of 4 — schema only (this entry).** Added a nullable `compare_field TEXT` column to the
`audit_rule_cross_check_documents` junction table (both SQLite `init_db()` and Postgres
`init_db_postgres()`), plus an idempotent backfill that copies each parent Cross-check's shared
`audit_rule_cross_checks.compare_field` onto its junction rows where the new column is still NULL.
A NULL junction value therefore means "fall back to the parent's shared field", and every existing
Cross-check is backfilled on the next startup so nothing breaks or needs re-saving. SQLite upgrade
uses the established PRAGMA-gated `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` + `UPDATE ... WHERE compare_field IS NULL`
pattern (runs every startup, cheap no-op once populated); Postgres uses
`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` + an `UPDATE ... FROM` backfill. New-DB CREATE TABLE statements carry the
column directly. Two tests added (`CrossCheckPerDocumentFieldSchemaTests`): column presence, and
backfill of a NULL junction row from the parent's shared field after a re-run of `init_db()`.

Locked assumptions: eligible-fields sourcing (global active-Master-Columns mirror) unchanged and
out of scope; `comparison_type` logic unaffected; `compare_to_voucher_line` stays a single anchor
field; UI (Phase 3) shows one field-picker per Document row, not a matrix.

**Phase 2 of 4 — backend validation / save / response (`routers/audit_rules.py`,
`tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`, `tests/test_verification_performance_metrics.py`).** Both
Cross-check request models (`CrossCheckCreate` / `CrossCheckUpdate`) gain
`document_fields: Dict[int, Optional[str]] = {}` — an optional `document_id -> own compare_field`
map. `normalize_compare_field()` (new helper) trims a value and treats blank as `None`.
`save_cross_check_documents()` now writes the junction `compare_field` column per row from that
map (absent / blank -> NULL). `validate_cross_check_payload()` no longer does a single-name
intersection across every Document: per Document it resolves the *effective* field
(`own override or shared compare_field`) and checks that against that Document's own
`get_document_cross_check_fields()`; the 400 message names the effective field.
`get_cross_check_documents()` takes the shared field as a second arg and each returned document
dict now carries `compare_field` (own, nullable) and `effective_compare_field` (own or shared);
`row_to_cross_check()` passes `row["compare_field"]` through. Top-level `compare_field` on
`audit_rule_cross_checks` untouched (still the fallback). Backward compatible: a client sending
only `document_ids` writes all-NULL junction rows -> every Document uses the shared field, exactly
as before. Five unit tests added (patched pg helpers, existing pattern in the file).

**Phase 3 of 4 — per-Document field-picker UI (`static/audit_rules.html`,
`static/audit_rules.js`; frontend only, no backend touched).** The Cross-check editor's
Documents list (`renderCrossCheckDocsList()`) now renders an inline `<select>` per row,
scoped to that Document's own eligible fields (new `eligibleFieldsForDoc(docId)` =
`getDocumentById(docId).cross_check_fields`, no intersection — mirrors Phase 2's
per-Document server check). New page state `crossCheckDocFields = {docId: field}` holds
explicit overrides only (keyed by docId so it survives reorder; pruned on remove; reset in
`startNewCrossCheck()`; hydrated in `selectCrossCheck()` from each `cc.documents[].compare_field`
— the raw override, not `effective_compare_field`). A blank row's first option reads
`(use default: <field>)` and is omitted from the save payload so the backend stores NULL.
The old shared `#arCompareFieldSelect` is relabelled "Default field to compare" and its
options are now the **union** of all selected Documents' eligible fields
(`computeEligibleFields()` changed from intersection); still required on save as the
fallback. Amber `.ar-field-warning` now renders per-row: when a saved override is no longer
eligible on that Document (stale value kept visible as a `⚠️` option), or when a blank
row's fallback default isn't eligible there. Save payload adds
`document_fields: {docId: field}` for explicit picks only, per Phase 2's contract.
`updateCompareToVoucherLineHint()` now shows the anchor's *effective* field
(`crossCheckDocFields[anchorId] || shared`). Default-dropdown render reordered before the
docs-list render so `(use default: …)` labels are correct on first open; the shared
dropdown's `change` re-renders the docs list. Inline `<select>` sizing only (margin/maxWidth/
fontSize set in JS) — no `style.css` change, no stylesheet `?v=` bump; `audit_rules.js?v=7 -> ?v=8`.
Full backend suite (66) still green; `node --check` passes.

Deferred to Phase 4 (validation engine): `compile_verification_rulebook()` and
`get_category_guidance_cross_checks()` still emit only the shared `compare_field`.

Later phase: 4 — validation engine (`routers/verification.py`) compares using each
document's own field name.

## Cross-check-eligible field mirror

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `routers/audit_rules.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`,
`static/audit_rules.js`, `tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`, `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`.

The Audit Rules Documents field was changed from a template-scoped, manually persisted list to a
read-only mirror of the active Master Columns registry. Every non-Physical-Bill Document now
receives all active client-data fields, including fields added later, without editing each
Document. The Cross-check document picker receives the same field data in its list response, so
the Field to Compare selector can calculate the common field set correctly. Physical Bills retain
their fixed evidence-field behavior and remain outside the Data Bank field mirror.

The legacy `audit_rule_document_fields` rows remain for compatibility but no longer control field
display, Cross-check validation, or compiled Verification Rulebooks. Focused Audit Rulebook tests
passed 15 tests; JavaScript syntax, Python compilation, and scoped diff checks also passed. Manual
browser testing remains required before Git staging, commit, or push.

## Prominent Rulebook change alert

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`,
`routers/verification.py`, `static/verification.js`, `static/audit_workbook.js`,
`static/style.css`, `tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`, `tests/test_verification_dirty_saves.py`,
`DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`.

The Rulebook mismatch investigation showed that an older Audit Workbook session displayed only a
generic failure while the browser's network panel exposed the HTTP 409. A durable
`audit_rules_config_changes` history now records the Rulebook version, entity type, item name,
action, user, and timestamp whenever stable Audit Rules configuration is invalidated. The
session Rulebook mismatch response includes the changes newer than the session's captured version,
with a safe generic fallback when historical records are unavailable.

Verification and Audit Workbook now display a prominent blocking alert listing the changed factory
settings and the session/current versions. The user can leave the session unchanged or explicitly
rebase it; the rebase continues to preserve saved verification work. No silent Rulebook change or
automatic recovery was added.

Focused Rulebook, alert, and dirty-save tests passed 25 tests. Aadil manually confirmed that Audit
Rules changes are not silently applied while a session is in progress and that the prominent alert
identifies the changed factory setting. The approved Git closeout is now complete; Phase 3 is the
next active implementation stage after the Phase 2 persistence closeout.

## Phase 2 closeout - host-specific voucher-check persistence

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `routers/verification.py`, `static/procedure_modal.js`,
`static/verification.js`, `static/audit_workbook.js`, `tests/test_verification_dirty_saves.py`,
`DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`.

Phase 2 was closed against the implementation already included in commit `a94759b`. Verification
keeps voucher-check changes local until its grouped Save -> Verify or save-only bundle request,
while Audit Workbook retains direct individual and batch persistence through the shared modal host
adapter. Optimistic state, rollback on failure, cache invalidation, Verify, and Verify & Next are
preserved.

The focused dirty-save suite passed 12 tests, and JavaScript syntax checks passed for all three
affected frontend files. Aadil manually confirmed the Audit Workbook check persistence and Verify
flows. Phase 3, Verification guidance normalization, is now the active stage.

## Phase 3 - Verification guidance normalization

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `static/verification.js`, `tests/test_audit_rulebook.py`,
`DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`.

The session Rulebook stores cross-check document references as stable `document_ids`, while the
Verification guidance renderer expects display-ready document names. A new adapter-boundary
normalizer now maps those IDs through the Rulebook's document metadata, preserves comparison
field/type and original metadata, and shows a safe `Document <id>` placeholder for an unknown
reference. The legacy live guidance endpoint, public response shape, and status/gate logic remain
unchanged.

The focused Rulebook and dirty-save suites passed 26 tests; JavaScript syntax validation, Python
compilation, and scoped diff checks passed. Manual browser validation remains required before Phase
3 Git closeout.

## Phase 3A - Edit Template close/save regression

**Date:** 2026-09-01 | **Files:** `static/templates.html`, `static/templates.js`, `tests/test_templates.py`,
`File_Map.md`, `DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`.

The Edit Template modal no longer closes from a backdrop click or the Escape key. Dynamically
rendered column Select/Remove controls and the search clear control are explicitly non-submit
buttons, preventing an accidental form submission when a column is selected. Column changes now
remain in the modal draft until the user clicks Save Template; the existing explicit Cancel and
top-right close controls remain available.

A disposable-template Playwright regression confirmed that selecting `Quantity` makes no PUT request,
backdrop clicks and Escape leave the modal open, the close icon closes it, reopening with the persisted
column payload shows the column, and explicit Save Template makes exactly one PUT request. The focused
Rulebook, dirty-save, and template
suites passed 27 tests. JavaScript syntax validation, Python compilation, and scoped diff checks
passed. Manual browser validation remains required before Git closeout.

Claude's six reported findings were independently compared with the current source and commit
history. Finding 1 is superseded rather than current: `a09258a` used the overly broad
`verification_sessions.status = 'In Progress'` guard, but `d7a7c6f` replaced it with the current
`verification_presence` lease query requiring an unended heartbeat within 90 seconds. Therefore
old In Progress sessions do not currently create the reported permanent Audit Rules lock. The
missing terminal session lifecycle remains a separate design pendency for cleanup and reporting.

Finding 2 is confirmed and high risk. `_audit_rules_config_version` is process-local and starts at 1
after a restart, while existing sessions retain their captured version. Template/master-column
invalidation also increments the same version. `load_verification_rulebook_for_session()` rejects
any mismatch with HTTP 409 and is used by session activation, line saves, grouped Save/Verify,
voucher-check verification, and status-reason reads. A controlled restart-safe compatibility or
recovery design is required before treating the Rulebook lock as complete.

Finding 3 is confirmed as a shared-host contract regression. The voucher-level check controls in
`procedure_modal.js` currently issue immediate individual/batch writes for both hosts, while the
Verification close/grouped path also submits the state. The Audit Workbook requirement for direct
persistence and Verification's local-first/grouped requirement must be separated explicitly; the
current behavior can perform duplicate idempotent writes and undermines the intended network-saving
design.

Finding 4 is confirmed as a display-only Rulebook adapter defect. Verification maps Rulebook
documents and roles but passes cross-checks through without converting `document_ids` to document
names or exposing document-level `cross_check_fields`. Audit Workbook's
`awRulebookCategoryToGuidance()` already contains the proven normalization pattern. No status gate
or audit conclusion is changed, but the Verification guidance popover can omit the visible chain.

Findings 5 and 6 are valid deferred hardening items. The sibling-ID memo is held in a ContextVar and
is not automatically available in ThreadPoolExecutor workers, so concurrent modal helpers can repeat
the resolution. Audit Workbook's observation and no-match-note flushes occur before its `try`, so a
flush failure can bypass the adapter's `{ok, data/error}` contract. Neither changes current audit
conclusions; both should be addressed only after the correctness fixes.

Additional unique pendencies recorded in the plan are explicit terminal Verification-session
lifecycle design, targeted regression tests for version drift/restart recovery and host-specific
voucher-check behavior, and reconciliation of stale historical Markdown status lines. The full
current test suite passes 49 tests with four non-blocking warnings; earlier Postgres-cutover failure
notes are stale and should not be treated as active failures.

The final stabilization order is: Rulebook recovery, shared-modal host gating, Verification guidance
normalization, Safety Phase A/B acceptance, targeted regression coverage, deferred hardening only if
still justified, documentation/Git closeout, then real product development. Further Supabase/free-tier
performance tuning remains deferred because the measured variability is infrastructure/connection
wait dominated and no safe additional rewrite is proven.

Audit Workbook's adapter supplied ordinary line saving but not Verification's optional grouped
`saveAndVerifyVoucher()` method. The shared modal close handler called that method unconditionally,
so its `×` button raised `hostAdapter.saveAndVerifyVoucher is not a function` and left the modal
open. Audit Workbook's `awSaveLineItems()` also returned no result after a successful save, so the
shared Verify fallback treated the save as failed and did not call `verify_voucher_checks`.

host's ordinary line save. `awSaveLineItems()` now returns the shared `{ok, data/error}` contract;
its database payload, status patch, cache invalidation, and table refresh are unchanged.

`save_line_items` and `verify_voucher_checks` with HTTP 200 and closes, and `✅ Verify & Next Line`
calls both endpoints with HTTP 200 and begins the next-line transition. No page errors were
observed. Both changed JavaScript files passed `node --check`; the focused dirty-save suite passed
9 tests. Aadil manually confirmed the target behavior; this phase is ready for Git commit/push.

## Audit Workbook batched voucher-support fetch

Frontend-only (`static/audit_workbook.js` + `?v=6` bump in `static/audit_workbook.html`), no
backend change. Brings Audit Workbook in line with the Verification-side `voucherSupportCache`
fix and resolves the 2026-08-28 KNOWN_ISSUES row for the AW physical_bill completion drift.

**Phase 2a (discovery, no code change):** confirmed the existing
`GET /api/verification/voucher_support_data/{anchor}` endpoint (already used by Verification's
`loadVoucherSupportData()`) covers all four of Audit Workbook's per-line data needs — linked
documents, procedure checks, observations, physical bills — with byte-identical field shapes
(`voucher_line_documents`/`procedure_checks` share the same SQL columns; physical bills go
through the same `_shape_physical_bill()` helper) and equivalent sibling-session resolution.
No endpoint param/response tweak needed; `routers/verification.py` stayed off the file list.

**Phase 2b (implementation):**

- **New voucher-level cache** (`awVoucherSupportCache` / `awVoucherSupportLoading` /
  `awVoucherSupportLoadingAnchor`) + `awLoadVoucherSupportData(anchorUid)` +
  `awInvalidateVoucherSupportCache()` — the direct analog of verification.js's
  `voucherSupportCache` / `loadVoucherSupportData()` / `invalidateVoucherSupportCache()`. One
  `window.ApiUtils.apiFetch('/api/verification/voucher_support_data/{anchor}')` call per voucher
  group (anchor = `voucher.lines[0].detail_id`), result indexed by each line's own `detail_id`.
  The in-flight guard only reuses a pending promise when it's for the **same anchor** — unlike
  verification.js (one voucher on screen at a time), Audit Workbook can refresh lines from
  different vouchers, so a blind reuse could hand back another voucher's data. Fail-soft to `{}`.

- **`awRefreshLineProcedures()` / `awRefreshLineObservations()`** repointed: replaced the
  `Promise.all` of `awFetchAssignedDocumentRecords` / `awFetchProcedureChecksForLine` /
  `awFetchPhysicalBillsForLine` (and, in the observations function, `awFetchLineObservationEntries`)
  with reads off `supportLines[String(uid)].{linked_documents.documents, procedure_checks.checks,
  physical_bills.bills, observations.entries}`. The `needsPhysicalBills` gate is gone — the
  batched fetch returns bills unconditionally (one request regardless). `ensureVoucherChecksLoaded()`
  still runs in parallel, gated on `needsVoucherChecks`, unchanged.

- **`isDocDone` physical_bill branch** ported verbatim from verification.js's
  `updateProceduresCellForLine()`: `physicalBills.filter(b => b.document_id === doc.id)`,
  `docBills.length > 0 && docBills.every(bill => bill_no/bill_date/vendor_name trimmed &&
  bill.bill_total != null)`, `Math.abs(sum of bill_total - voucherLineAmount) <= 0.005`. The old
  code used `physicalBills.find(...)` + `bill.amount` — but the shaped bill has no `amount` field
  (it's `bill_total` + nested `items` since the Multi-Bill/Multi-Line work), so `bill.amount` was
  always `undefined` and **a physical_bill document never counted toward done/total in the AW
  Procedures cell**. Pre-existing bug, fixed here as part of the same file's work.

  its success path (after the `cleared_status` patch). Single chokepoint — covers the adapter's
  `saveLineItems` / `saveAllVoucherLines` and `performVerifyVoucherChecksImpl()`'s fallback save

  Without this, `hideProcedureModalOnly()`'s fire-and-forget badge refresh serves the pre-save
  copy and badges show stale done/total until the page reloads — the exact bug the
  Verification-side fix addressed.

- **Dead code removed:** all four `awFetch*` helpers (`awFetchAssignedDocumentRecords`,
  `awFetchProcedureChecksForLine`, `awFetchPhysicalBillsForLine`, `awFetchLineObservationEntries`)
  plus the `fetchPhysicalBillsForLine: awFetchPhysicalBillsForLine` entry in
  `buildAuditWorkbookAdapter()`. Confirmed the only callers were the code replaced above —
  `procedure_modal.js` never calls these adapter methods (it reads its own `procedure_modal_data`

**Untouched:** `awFindLineByDetailId`, `awFetchAuditGuidanceData`, the gating logic, and
`applyFilterAndRender()` are all fetch-agnostic — they operate on already-fetched data and
needed no change. `pytest` → 36 passed (frontend-only change; confirms nothing broke on import).

## Procedure modal cache invalidation after bundle save

`procedureModalDataCache` (`static/procedure_modal.js`, keyed per voucher-line uid) feeds
`openProcedureModal()`, which rebuilds `tabState.checklist` from that payload verbatim on every
open — so a stale entry silently un-ticked procedures that were correctly saved in the DB, on
reopening a line after a save.

Two call sites were leaving the cache stale, same root cause (missing/skipped
`invalidateProcedureModalData()` call):

1. The `save_and_verify_voucher_bundle` path (`hostAdapter.saveAndVerifyVoucher()`) never
   invalidated. The bundle persists **every** line in `currentVoucherLines`, so all those uids
   go stale, not just the open one. Fixed with a new helper
   `invalidateProcedureModalDataForVoucher()` (loops `hostAdapter.currentVoucherLines`, the same
   array `verification.js`'s `saveAndVerifyVoucher()` builds its `lines` payload from), called
   after the success check in `performVerifyVoucherChecksImpl()` (covers the bundle branch and
   the legacy `saveLineItems + verify_voucher_checks` fallback) and in `closeProcedureModal()`
   after the grouped-save success check.
2. `toggleAllProcedureChecks()` — the local-first refactor added an early `return;` that jumped
   over its own `invalidateProcedureModalData(uid)` call. Restored by adding the call immediately
   before the early return (the in-memory checklist has diverged from the cache, so the entry is
   definitively stale; a later reopen re-fetches once the background per-line save has run). The
   now-dead post-`return` copy at the old line was left as-is (other post-`return` dead code in
   this file is a separate cleanup).

No backend / DB-write / gate-logic changes. Cache-bust `procedure_modal.js?v=8→9` on
`verification.html` and `audit_workbook.html`. 33 backend tests pass (frontend-only change).

## Verification Speed Optimization — Phase 3

**Date:** 2026-08-27
**Full investigation/timing log:** `INVESTIGATION_VERIFICATION_PERF_PHASE3.md` (repo root).
**Scope so far:** Phase 3a (reconcile + map, no code) and Phase 3c (modal-open fetch fix).
Phases 3d/3e (Verify sequence) and 3f (Render test + docs) not yet done.

### Phase 3a — reconciliation + call-pattern map (no code changes)

Confirmed the ~7.9s procedure-modal open and ~21.7s Verify sequence are specific instances of
`PERFORMANCE_INVESTIGATION.md`'s Finding #1 (cross-region round-trip tax, Render Singapore ↔
Supabase Mumbai) multiplied by Finding #2 (sequential, non-batched round-trips) — no new
root-cause class. Corrected one stale note: the 2026-08-25 `Promise.all` fix covered page/session
load, not `openProcedureModal()` or the Verify sequence (both built later, 2026-08-26, still
sequential). Mapped the exact modal-open call sequence and Verify-sequence steps — see the
investigation doc. Confirmed the `audit_rules.py get_required_documents_with_authority()`
auth-role N+1 is reached only from the save/Verify path, never from `get_procedure_modal_data()`'s
fan-out — so it is not entangled with 3c and stays tracked separately (KNOWN_ISSUES 2026-08-25).

### Phase 3c — modal-open fetch fix

**Backend — per-request memo for `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids()` (`routers/verification.py`):**
`get_procedure_modal_data()` is a thin sequential fan-out to 5 read sub-functions
(`get_voucher_line_documents` / `get_procedure_checks` / `get_line_observations` /
`get_voucher_line_physical_bills` / `get_cross_check_results`), each of which independently
called `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids()` (2 cross-region queries) for the same id.
Added `import contextvars` and a module-level `_sibling_ids_request_memo` ContextVar
(default `None`). `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids()` now checks the memo first and stores its
result (including `None` for a missing line). `get_procedure_modal_data()` sets a fresh `{}` on
the ContextVar as its first `try` statement and `reset()`s it in `finally`. Opt-in only — every
other caller (Verify path, standalone endpoints, Audit Workbook) is byte-for-byte unchanged
because the memo defaults to `None`. Chosen per-request rather than the `audit_rules.py` TTL
`cache_get/cache_set`: the `client_data_id → sibling verification_details ids` mapping changes
whenever a new verification session is created for the cashbook, which cannot happen mid-request,
so a process-lifetime/TTL cache would risk a stale sibling set.

**Frontend — parallelize `openProcedureModal()` (`static/procedure_modal.js`):**
Previously awaited 4 things in series: guidance (usually cached), template-columns `Promise.all`,
`procedure_modal_data`, `fetchLatestTbAccounts`. Steps 3–4 are independent of 1–2 and of each
other. Now the `procedure_modal_data` fetch is started (in a timed IIFE, own try/catch,
fail-soft to `null`) **before** the guidance await, and template-columns + modal-data are awaited
together via `Promise.all`. `modal_data_ms` is still measured truthfully inside the IIFE;
`template_columns_ms` now covers whichever of the two overlapping fetches finishes last.

**Frontend — `fetchLatestTbAccounts()` cache + lazy load (`static/procedure_modal.js`):**
Had no cache-hit guard despite its name, so it re-fetched `/api/trial-balance/latest-accounts`
on every modal open even though only the "Voucher Line" tab's Account-Head search uses it.
Now cached per client (`latestTbAccountsCacheClientId`) with in-flight dedup
(`latestTbAccountsInFlight`), removed from `openProcedureModal()`, and warmed lazily
fire-and-forget from `renderAccountHeadCard()` the first time that tab renders — safe because the
match-mode markup reads nothing from the cache; only the keystroke dropdown / Suggest / "Use"
handlers do, all strictly later. Result: 0 cost on the common modal open, at most one fetch per
client per page session.

**Cache-bust:** `procedure_modal.js?v=4→5` on `verification.html` and `audit_workbook.html`
(the only two pages that load it).

### Verification

- **Baseline script** (`scratchpad/bench_modal_data.py`, throwaway, read-only): calls

- **Live UI check (Playwright, dev server, session #749 / voucher CPV-0826-442 / detail_id

## Verification Save Performance — Phase 2

**Date:** 2026-08-27

### Developed

- Added a monotonically increasing dirty revision per loaded voucher line. New vouchers begin
  clean; line-specific evidence, procedure, observation, account-head, signature, and Physical
  Bill changes dirty only their line, while voucher-level check changes dirty every line.
- `saveAllVoucherLines()` now sends only dirty lines and reports saved, failed, and skipped counts
  under `?perf=1`. Writes remain sequential pending the later atomic voucher-save backend.
- A successful response clears a line only when its revision did not change while the request was
  in flight. Failed saves and newer edits remain dirty for retry.
- Verify forces the current line through the existing server-side status engine, then navigation
  recognizes that successful revision as clean instead of submitting it again. Voucher-level
  changes remain dirty on the other affected lines until safely recomputed.
- Physical Bills now have their own dirty flag, so opening/closing an unchanged manual Vendor Bill
  no longer rewrites it. Bills flush before the line status save so Cleared/Query sees current bill
  data; a failed bill write leaves the line dirty.
- Cache versions: `procedure_modal.js?v=3→4` in Verification/Audit Workbook and
  `verification.js?v=16→17` in Verification.

## Client Data Availability Loading Popup

**Date:** 2026-08-27 | **Files:** `static/databank.html`, `static/databank.js`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`.

**Why:** On entering Client Data, the temporary “Fetching availability data” ribbon disappeared
before the template table became visible, leaving an apparently idle page during the remaining
wait. The page needed prominent feedback that stayed until its template list was actually ready.

**Implementation:** Added a centered, page-specific loading card backed by the shared
`LoadingUI` progress primitive. It starts in indeterminate mode while availability and database-size
requests run. Once availability arrives, it switches to determinate mode and renders template rows
one browser frame at a time, updating the exact count and percentage. It reaches 100% only after the
last row is inserted, remains briefly so completion is visible, then closes. Empty results finalize
as 100%; failures close the overlay and retain the existing error display. Data Bank JS cache-bust
advanced from `v=5` to `v=6`. No shared Loading UI or global stylesheet change was required.

**Verification:** `node --check static/databank.js` and `git diff --check` passed. A hermetic
Playwright test served the real Data Bank page with stubbed endpoints and verified: delayed success
showed the overlay at 0%, reached 100% with all three template rows present, then closed; an empty
response reached 100% with zero rows; and a forced 500 closed the overlay while preserving the
server error message. The test used no live database or credentials.

## Row-Exclusion Requirement (7 entries)


- **Known pre-existing bug, not yet fixed (found 2026-07-16 while verifying the row-exclusion phase)**: `compare_transactions()`'s existing-rows query (`routers/import_export.py`) does a `LEFT JOIN verification_details` that can return multiple rows per `client_data_id` when more than one `verification_details` row references the same `client_data_id` — this inflates `existing_docs`/the "missing" list with duplicate `client_data_id`s (harmless duplication on its own, since re-`UPDATE`ing the same id is idempotent) but also means `total_existing_before_import`/`missing_count` in API responses can overcount real rows. Caught the hard way: testing `/api/upload/import` against the *real* ACME client (client_id=1) with a small unrelated test file caused every real document not present in that test file to be correctly-by-design-but-dangerously flagged `change_detection_status='deleted'` (~1200 rows momentarily mis-flagged; reverted using `data_audit_log` history to confirm each row's true prior status, no data loss). **Lesson for future testing**: never call `/api/upload/import` (or anything that reaches `compare_transactions()`) against a client that has real/live data unless the incoming file is a genuine full re-upload of that client's data — use a disposable test client (create via `POST /api/clients`, delete afterward) for any import-path testing instead.

- 2026-07-16: Row-exclusion Phase 1 of 4 (backend, routers/import_export.py only) done — `ImportRequest` gained `excluded_rows: Optional[List[int]] = None` (row numbers match `validation_errors[].row_number`: header=1, first data row=2; `None`/absent = exclude nothing, identical to today's behavior); new `filter_excluded_rows(rows, excluded_rows)` is called immediately after `rows = df.to_dict('records')` in both `validate_only()` and `validate_and_import()`, before any validation, counting, or `compare_transactions()`/`get_document_group_id()` grouping — so excluded rows are invisible to validation, import, and change-detection grouping, per the brief. `check-duplicates` intentionally left untouched (brief scoped to validate/import only). No UI changes this phase. Verified end-to-end against the live app: a baseline `/api/upload/validate` call (43-row real file, no `excluded_rows`) was unchanged; excluding a row that would otherwise fail validation (blank required fields + bad date) removed it from `validation_errors` and dropped `total_rows`/`valid_rows` accordingly; a full `/api/upload/import` run (using a disposable throwaway test client created and deleted for this purpose, see the "known bug" note below) confirmed the excluded row produced no `client_data` row and was absent from `document_group_id` grouping. **Incident during this session's verification, since corrected — see the "known pre-existing bug" Convention note above**: an initial `/api/upload/import` test call against the *real* ACME client (client_id=1) with a small unrelated test file triggered a pre-existing, unrelated bug in `compare_transactions()` that flagged ~12 real rows `change_detection_status='deleted'` (the raw response claimed ~3989 due to a duplicate-join artifact in that same pre-existing query, not 3989 real rows). Fully reverted using `data_audit_log` history to confirm and restore each affected row's true prior status (`active`), with before/after status-distribution counts cross-checked to reconcile exactly (verified no net data loss); all test artifacts (client, rows, uploaded_files entries, physical files) removed afterward. Root cause is a separate, unfixed bug (documented as a Convention note above) — out of scope for this phase.

- 2026-07-18: Cashbook discovery bug fix, expanded to a 5-way voucher-prefix category scheme (database.py, routers/clients.py, routers/verification.py, static/client_settings.html, static/client_settings.js) done. Started as a narrow brief: `GET /api/verification/cashbooks` (`extract_cashbook_name()`) was surfacing expense/vendor accounts as cashbook candidates because it accepted a Cash/Bank-category row with *either* debit or credit > 0. Investigation found the root cause was structural: the earlier per-client-prefix migration had collapsed the old type-specific `CPV`/`CV`→Payment vs `CRV`/`CR`→Receipt prefix lists into a flat 3-way `Cash`/`Bank`/`Journal` scheme with no Payment/Receipt distinction at all — `extract_cashbook_name()` runs before any cashbook name is known, so it structurally couldn't recover which side was correct from category alone, which is why the "accept either side" fallback existed. Presented two fix options (an internal letter-heuristic kept inside verification.py, vs. storing Payment/Receipt explicitly); **user chose to store it explicitly**, expanding scope to a 5-way category scheme: `Cash Payment`/`Cash Receipt`/`Bank Payment`/`Bank Receipt`/`Journal` (defaults CPV/CRV/BPV/BRV/JV). See the new Conventions note above for the full design (`VOUCHER_PREFIX_CATEGORIES`/`DEFAULT_VOUCHER_PREFIXES`, `CATEGORY_FIELD_MAP`, the `init_db()` migration, `voucher_type_label()`'s simplified signature). `extract_cashbook_name()` is now directly type-specific (`category in ('Cash Payment','Bank Payment') and credit>0`, or Receipt+debit) with no side-guessing; `start_verification_session()`/`preview_cashbook()` simplified to read `vtype` straight from category instead of re-deriving it from the cashbook row's debit/credit sign (that lookup is now only a sanity check, not a type-derivation step) — their actual per-row filtering logic was left untouched, as the original brief required. ## Audit Rules Module (27 entries)


- **Modal Caching Phase 3, sub-phase 3 of 3, FINAL (verify, no code changes — this completes the 3-sub-phase Modal Caching Phase 3 track)**: confirmed the cache built in sub-phase 1 and wired in sub-phase 2 behaves correctly end-to-end via real HTTP requests against the actually-running dev server, not another repeat of the in-process function-call smoke test. **A real blocker surfaced first**: the dev server already listening on port 5000 pre-dated both sub-phases' code (`main.py` has no `--reload` flag; the process's start time was `12:58 PM`, `routers/audit_rules.py`'s last edit was `2:34 PM`) — every initial curl against it silently exercised the old, pre-caching code, producing a flat ~3s latency with zero difference between a guaranteed miss and a guaranteed hit. Per this file's own standing convention (never kill a port-5000 process without checking whose it is first), stopped and asked before touching it — confirmed with the user to restart it, then re-ran every check against the fresh process (PID confirmed new, `Application startup complete` logged). **Four checks, all passed live**: (1) cache-hit latency — a guaranteed miss (immediately after an invalidating write) costs ~3-4.6s per `GET /api/audit-rules/documents/{id}`, a guaranteed hit costs ~0.2s via `curl` (a Python `urllib`-based repeat of the same check initially showed a flatter ~2s "hit" cost — traced to per-call client-side connection overhead in that script, not a server-side effect, and confirmed as a red herring once `curl`'s numbers came back sharply different and consistent across 3 repeated rounds); (2) a paginated list (`GET /api/audit-rules/documents?limit=5&offset=0`) sets `X-Total-Count` identically on both a fresh call and a repeat cache-hit call (`18` both times); (3) no stale reads — `PUT`ing a new `kb_note` onto a live Document and immediately re-`GET`ting it returns the new value right away, not a cached stale one; (4) cross-file invalidation — created a disposable test Category, hit `GET /api/verification/audit_guidance?transaction_type=<name>` twice (confirming a real cache hit via identical `kb_overview` on both calls), then `PUT` a `kb_overview` change to that Category through `routers/audit_rules.py`'s own endpoint, and the very next `audit_guidance` call reflected the new text immediately — proving `verification.py`'s guidance cache correctly shares and is correctly busted by `audit_rules.py`'s own invalidation hooks, exactly as designed in sub-phase 2. All disposable test data (the temporarily-modified Document's `kb_note`, the test Category) was reverted/soft-deleted afterward. No bug found — nothing to report as a blocker beyond the stale-server false start above, which was an environment/process issue, not a defect in the cache logic itself. This completes the confirmed 3-sub-phase Modal Caching Phase 3 requirement: mechanism + write invalidation (sub-phase 1) → read-side wiring (sub-phase 2) → live end-to-end verification (this entry).

- **Modal Caching Phase 3, sub-phase 2 of 3 (read-side wiring, `routers/audit_rules.py` + `routers/verification.py`)**: wires the cache mechanism built in sub-phase 1 into every GET path it covers. **Two design decisions confirmed with the user before implementation, both departures from the original brief's literal wording**: (1) cache keys are **global, not per-client** — sub-phase 1 already confirmed `audit_rule_documents`/`audit_rule_cross_checks`/`audit_rule_categories` have no `client_id` column, so partitioning by client would just build N redundant copies of identical data; every key wired this phase omits client_id. (2) `GET /api/verification/category-for-account` was deliberately **left uncached** — it's genuinely client-scoped (client_id + account_code → category), but its data comes from `routers/trial_balance.py` (TB uploads, Assign Categories), a file with zero invalidation hooks into this cache; caching it now would risk serving a stale category mapping for up to the 10-min TTL after a TB re-upload with no way to invalidate sooner, so it stays uncached until (if ever) `trial_balance.py` gets its own hooks. Wired in `routers/audit_rules.py`: `get_documents`/`get_document`, `get_cross_checks`/`get_cross_check`, `get_categories`/`get_category`, and `get_category_cleared_requirements` — each checks `cache_get(key)` first, computes and `cache_set()`s on a miss. `fetch_paginated_rows()` (the shared helper behind the three list endpoints) was restructured to return `(rows, total)` instead of writing `response.headers["X-Total-Count"]` itself, since a cache **hit** now needs to set that same header from a cached total without re-querying `COUNT(*)` — each list endpoint stores `(result, total)` as its cached value and sets the header identically on both the hit and miss paths. Wired in `routers/verification.py`: `get_audit_guidance` (the only qualifying call site — `category-for-account` is the other endpoint in this file and was excluded per decision #2 above), keyed on `transaction_type` (the Category name) since guidance content doesn't vary by client; imports `cache_get`/`cache_set` from `routers.audit_rules` alongside the file's existing cross-router imports from that same module (`get_category_guidance_documents` etc.), no new import pattern introduced. No changes to `invalidate_audit_rules_cache()` or any write endpoint — sub-phase 1's 14 hooks already cover every write that can affect what's cached here. Verified: `py_compile` clean on both files; `pytest` shows the same 2 pre-existing failures as sub-phase 1's baseline (confirmed unrelated, both in Postgres-backed routers outside this change), no new failures. Direct smoke test against the live Postgres/Supabase database (disposable `SmokeTestDoc`/`SmokeTestCategory` rows, soft-deleted at the end — same create-then-soft-delete verification convention used throughout this module's build history) confirmed: a single-item GET makes real DB calls on a miss and zero on a hit with an identical result; an `update_document` call immediately invalidates that cached read (next GET reflects the new name, not stale data); a paginated list GET is a cache hit on the second call and still sets `X-Total-Count` identically to the miss path; `verification.py`'s `get_audit_guidance` hits the same shared cache (miss then hit, zero DB calls on the hit) and is correctly invalidated by an `update_category` write made through `audit_rules.py`, proving the cross-file reuse works end-to-end. No new files, no schema changes.

- **Modal Caching Phase 3, sub-phase 1 of 3 (TTL cache mechanism + write-side invalidation, `routers/audit_rules.py` only)**: adds an in-memory, process-level TTL cache in front of Categories/Documents/Cross-checks reads — server-side, separate from and complementary to the existing client-side session cache (matrix_version-based, from the original caching feature's Phase 2). Render is single-instance, so no Redis. New module-level `_audit_rules_cache: Dict[str, tuple]` (key → `(expires_at, value)`) guarded by a `threading.Lock()` (endpoints are sync `def`s, run in FastAPI's threadpool, so concurrent access is possible), with `cache_get(key)`/`cache_set(key, value, ttl=AUDIT_RULES_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)`/`invalidate_audit_rules_cache()` — `AUDIT_RULES_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS = 600` (10 min) is a safety net only; TTL is not the primary invalidation mechanism. **Read-only finding that shaped the design**: none of `audit_rule_documents`/`audit_rule_cross_checks`/`audit_rule_categories` have a `client_id` column — they're firm-wide entities, not per-client (confirmed against the schema) — so a write from any one client's session invalidates the same data for every client equally, meaning `invalidate_audit_rules_cache()` always clears the whole cache rather than attempting a per-client scoped clear, regardless of whatever key scheme the read-side wiring (sub-phase 2) ends up using. Also checked the brief's question about `bump_category_matrix_version()`: confirmed it fires on only two triggers (Category document-membership change in `update_category`, and the `is_required` toggle in `update_category_document_required`) — it does **not** fire on Document field edits (`update_document`), Document soft-delete/restore, the `transaction_level_approval` toggle, or any Cross-check write, all of which can change a cached Categories/Documents/guidance read. Since `matrix_version` is a narrower, different concept (staleness of an already-persisted per-voucher classification, not API-response freshness), cache invalidation was wired as its own explicit `invalidate_audit_rules_cache()` call in each affected write endpoint rather than folded into `bump_category_matrix_version()` itself — 14 call sites total: Documents' `create_document`/`update_document`/`delete_document`/`restore_document`/`update_document_transaction_level_approval`; Cross-checks' `create_cross_check`/`update_cross_check`/`delete_cross_check`/`restore_cross_check`; Categories' `create_category`/`update_category`/`delete_category`/`restore_category`/`update_category_document_required`. Voucher-level Checks and Signature Specimens endpoints deliberately untouched — out of this brief's stated cache scope (Categories/Documents/guidance only). No GET endpoint reads the cache yet (`cache_get`/`cache_set` defined but not yet called from any read path) — that's sub-phase 2's job, along with wiring `verification.py`'s `get_audit_guidance`/`category-for-account` lookups. No schema changes, no new files. Verified: existing `pytest` suite run before and after (via `git stash`) shows the same 2 pre-existing failures both times, both in Postgres-backed routers unrelated to this file — confirmed not a regression. Direct smoke test (`python -c`, `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` to work around this repo's known cp1252-console `print()`-emoji issue in `database.py`) confirmed `cache_set`/`cache_get` round-trip correctly, `invalidate_audit_rules_cache()` clears all keys, and a short-TTL entry correctly evicts as expired after sleeping past it. No browser/UI verification possible or needed this phase — nothing user-visible changed yet.

- **Audit Rules Phase 9 of 9, FINAL — verification module wired to Categories (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/verification.js`)**: this completes the 9-phase Audit Rules module. **Design decision, confirmed with the user**: the per-account-code/name linking mentioned in the original brief is explicit *future* work (a separate financial-statements module, not this phase); for now, Categories are matched using the same per-line "Transaction Type" dropdown that already existed in `verification.js` — its value now *is* a Category name (fetched live from `GET /api/audit-rules/categories?include_inactive=false`, cached in module-level `auditCategories`), not one of 7 hardcoded strings matched against the old `audit_procedure_library` table. Categories remain **global** entities with no client scoping (confirmed: no `client_id` anywhere in the `audit_rule_*` schema) — there is no separate per-client mapping table. `GET /api/verification/audit_guidance` (routers/verification.py) keeps its original URL and `transaction_type` query param (now holding a Category name, not a literal transaction type) for frontend-contract stability, and now returns `{transaction_type, category_id, kb_overview, documents[], cross_checks[]}` sourced from `audit_rule_categories`/`get_category_guidance_documents()`/`get_category_guidance_cross_checks()` (new, additive helpers in `routers/audit_rules.py` — distinct from `get_category_documents()`/`get_category_cross_checks()`, which stay unchanged and keep serving the Categories CRUD response's lighter id/name-only shape). **Cross-checks are read-only guidance text only this phase** (rendered as "Check: {compare_field} — {comparison_type} across {doc1 → doc2 → ...}") — no automated comparison against real voucher data; that's explicitly deferred as its own future requirement. The old `audit_procedure_library` table and its 7-row seed data are left in place, unused (same deprecation pattern as the old `voucher_patterns` app_settings row) — not dropped. **One-time idempotent migration** (in `init_db()`, `database.py`): the 7 legacy transaction types (Material Purchased, Repair & Maintenance (In-house), Fuel Expense, Short Term Advance against Salary, Payment to Contractors, Fixed Asset Purchased, Kitchen Expenses) were copied into real `audit_rule_categories` rows, `kb_overview` = their old `management_controls`/`audit_risks`/`audit_procedures` text combined into one block — Documents/Cross-checks were deliberately left unattached (no structured document list existed in the old data), for manual setup via the Audit Rules UI. Checked by name before insert, so reruns are a no-op. **`audit_rule_documents` gained `template_id`** (nullable, `REFERENCES templates(id)`, same `CREATE TABLE` + `ALTER TABLE` upgrade-block pattern used 3x already for `is_active`) — a real gap found while tracing the Supporting column: `openProcedureModal(procKey, label, templateId, uid)` needs a Data Bank template to search evidence against, and the old fixed 5 procedures had this hardcoded in a JS constant (`VOUCHER_LINE_PROCEDURES`, now deleted) with no equivalent on `audit_rule_documents`. `routers/audit_rules.py`'s `DocumentCreate`/`DocumentUpdate`/`row_to_document()` and the Documents CRUD endpoints now carry `template_id`, validated by new `validate_document_template_id()` (400 if it doesn't reference an active `templates` row) — same validate-then-write pattern as the module's existing `document_ids`/`cross_check_ids` checks. `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js` gained a "Template" `<select>` (`#arTemplateSelect`) on the Documents detail form, populated once at init by new `loadTemplatesForDocuments()` (mirrors `templates.js`'s own `GET /api/templates` fetch). In `static/verification.js`: `VOUCHER_LINE_PROCEDURES` is gone; the Supporting column is now built by new async `updateSupportingCellForLine(uid, type)` from the selected Category's `documents[]` (a Document with no `template_id` renders as plain muted, non-clickable text via an inline style override — not a new CSS class, since `static/style.css` was out of scope for this phase) — called both when a line's seeded type is synced on render and from the Type dropdown's `change` listener, so switching Category live-refreshes Supporting. A new shared `fetchAuditGuidanceData(type)`/`auditGuidanceCache` (keyed by Category name, not per-line) backs both the "Guide" popover (`showAuditGuidancePopover()`) and `updateSupportingCellForLine()`, so selecting the same Category from two different lines doesn't double-fetch; a 404 caches as `null`, a transient error does not cache (so a retry can succeed). `buildAuditGuidanceTable()` was rewritten for the new response shape (kb_overview block + Documents list with auth roles + Cross-checks list as read-only guidance lines), same function name/signature/caller so `showAuditGuidancePopover()` needed no structural change beyond swapping its own inline fetch for the shared `fetchAuditGuidanceData()`. Verified end-to-end against the live dev server: `init_db()` migration correctly added `template_id` and seeded all 7 Categories with non-empty `kb_overview` and no auto-attached Documents/Cross-checks, and was confirmed idempotent on a second run; created two test Documents (one with a bad `template_id` correctly rejected 400) and a Cross-check via the live API, attached them to the migrated "Fuel Expense" Category (confirming the pre-existing containment validation from Phase 4 still fires correctly), and confirmed `GET /api/verification/audit_guidance?transaction_type=Fuel%20Expense` returned the full `kb_overview`/`documents[]`/`cross_checks[]` shape correctly; a nonexistent category name still 404s. All test rows reverted/soft-deleted afterward. **Known gap from this session, worth noting**: an attempted "isolated copy" test of the `init_db()` migration (copying `test.db` to a scratch directory and pointing a fresh `database` module import at it) did not actually stay isolated — `database.py` connects via a module-level `DB_NAME` constant read at import time, not the `DB_PATH` attribute that was reassigned after import, so the migration ran directly against the live project `test.db` instead. The change itself was safe (additive nullable column, idempotent name-checked inserts, same migration that would have run on the next real app startup regardless), but this is a real gap in how to safely sandbox a `database.py`-dependent test in this codebase — worth fixing properly (e.g. a `DATABASE_URL`-style env var read at call time) before relying on an "isolated" test again. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session (same recurring gap as most phases in this log) — the live Type dropdown listing Categories, Guide popover, and Supporting column rendering in an actual browser were not visually confirmed, only via direct API calls mirroring exactly what the JS sends. **This completes the entire 9-phase Audit Rules module requirement.**

- **Audit Rules frontend shell, Categories (Phase 7 of 9, final entity view)**: followed the Phase 6 full-duplication pattern exactly as instructed above — `#arCategoriesListSection`/`#arCategoriesDetailSection`, `editingCategoryId`/`categoryDocIds`/`categoryCrossCheckIds` state, `showCategoryDetailStatus()`, own render functions (`renderCategoryDocChips()`/`renderCategoryCrossCheckChips()`) — not a generalization of Documents' `renderChipList()` or Cross-checks' ordered-list renderer, even though Category's Documents/Cross-checks lists are conceptually similar to both. One deliberate difference from Cross-checks' Documents list: Category's Documents/Cross-checks lists are **flat tag lists with no reorder** (`.ar-chip-list`/`.ar-chip`, reused as-is, no new CSS needed) rather than Cross-checks' *ordered* list with ▲/▼ — per the confirmed brief, a Category's document/cross-check order has no meaning. `switchEntityType()` (`static/audit_rules.js`) gained its anticipated third `'categories'` branch — the one necessary edit to shared Phase 6 code, explicitly pre-authorized by this note's own prior entry — toggling `#arRailCategories`/the two new section divs and refreshing both `allDocuments` (reused from Phase 6 as-is) and a new `allCrossChecks` cache (`loadAllCrossChecksForCategories()`, mirrors `loadAllDocumentsForCrossChecks()`'s shape) whenever the view opens. **Cross-check picker eligibility is enforced proactively, not just reactively**: `renderCategoryCrossCheckChips()` rebuilds the "add cross-check" `<select>` on every change to `categoryDocIds` (not only `categoryCrossCheckIds`, same coupling convention Phase 6 established for its own doc-list/compare-field pair) and disables any cross-check option whose own documents aren't all yet in `categoryDocIds`, appending a `"(needs: X, Y)"` hint naming the missing document(s) rather than hiding the option outright — this directly satisfies the brief's "adding a Document... makes it available for selection when attaching Cross-checks" line and means a user can no longer construct the invalid state client-side, though the server's `validate_category_payload()` (routers/audit_rules.py) remains the authoritative backstop (confirmed still fires correctly and returns its already-specific "Cross-check 'X' (ID n) references Document ID(s) [n] that are not included..." message when tested directly against the API bypassing the UI's own guard). **Removal warning**: `removeCategoryDocument(docId)` calls `computeAffectedCrossChecks(docId)` (checks `allCrossChecks` cache) and shows a `confirm()` naming any already-attached Cross-check(s) that reference the document being removed — a soft warning the user can still proceed past (not a hard block), since the server validation is the final authority at Save time regardless. The server error message is surfaced completely unparsed (`result.detail` straight into `showCategoryDetailStatus()`) — no client-side regex/formatting was needed to satisfy the brief's "clear inline error naming which Cross-check/Document conflicts" requirement, since the server already names both by their actual name/ID. `used_by_vouchers_count` is displayed as "Used by N vouchers" (not "categories" — the wording used by Documents/Cross-checks' own analogous field) and will read 0 for every Category until Phase 9 replaces the backend's hardcoded placeholder with a real query. **This completes all three entity views (Documents, Cross-checks, Categories) — the Audit Rules module's frontend shell is now fully functional end-to-end**; Phase 9 (not yet started) is the confirmed remaining voucher↔Category wiring — Phase 8's scope hasn't been confirmed yet at time of writing.

- **Audit Rules frontend shell, Cross-checks (Phase 6 of 9)**: the actual pattern landed on is **full duplication per entity type**, not a generalized `switchEntityType()` that reuses Documents' own list/detail elements/functions — each entity type gets its own list-section div (`#arDocumentsListSection`/`#arCrossChecksListSection`), its own detail-section div (`#arDocumentsDetailSection`/`#arCrossChecksDetailSection`), its own state vars (`editingId`/`editingCrossCheckId`), and its own status helper (`showDetailStatus`/`showCrossCheckDetailStatus`) — chosen specifically so this addition never has to touch a single existing Documents function or call site, at the cost of some duplication (same tradeoff Phase 5 made copying columns.js/client_settings.js patterns rather than importing them). `switchEntityType(type)` (`static/audit_rules.js`) is a thin toggle: swaps `.active` on the two rail buttons and `display` on the four section divs, nothing more — it does not own any entity-specific rendering logic. **Phase 7 (Categories) should follow this same full-duplication pattern** — a third `#arCategoriesListSection`/`#arCategoriesDetailSection` pair, its own state/status helper, one more branch in `switchEntityType()` — not attempt to generalize Documents/Cross-checks into shared code as part of adding Categories. The only two touches made to Phase 5's existing Documents markup were pure structural wraps (nesting the existing list-panel and detail-panel content each inside a new named div, zero id/attribute/text changes inside), plus one new `click` listener added to the pre-existing `#arRailDocuments` button (Phase 5 didn't need one since Documents was the only view) — no Documents CRUD function was edited. Cross-checks' Compare Field dropdown (`#arCompareFieldSelect`) is the interesting new piece: `computeEligibleFields()`/`renderCompareFieldDropdown()` compute the intersection of `cross_check_fields` across every document currently in `crossCheckDocIds` (client-side mirror of `validate_cross_check_payload()`'s server-side rule in `routers/audit_rules.py`, confirmed by testing the same add/remove/reorder sequence directly against the live API), and must be recalculated on every add/remove/reorder of that document list — `renderCrossCheckDocsList()` and `renderCompareFieldDropdown()` are always called together for this reason, never independently. A `let allDocuments = []` cache (from `GET /api/audit-rules/documents?include_inactive=false`) backs both the eligible-fields computation and the "add document" picker's available options; it's refreshed every time `switchEntityType('cross-checks')` fires, not cached indefinitely, so a Document's fields edited elsewhere are picked up on next visit to this view.

- **Audit Rules frontend shell (Phase 5 of 9, `static/audit_rules.html` + `static/audit_rules.js`)**: a single reusable three-pane layout (`.ar-rail` entity-type selector / `.ar-list-panel` / `.ar-detail-panel`, all new classes in `static/style.css`'s new "AUDIT RULES MODULE" section at the end of the file) wired end-to-end for Documents only — Cross-checks/Categories rail items exist (`.ar-rail-item.coming-soon`, reusing the app's existing coming-soon dimming convention) but have no click listener yet. Phases 6-7 should extend this same shell (add a `currentEntityType` state var + a `switchEntityType()` function that swaps which list/detail logic is active) rather than building a second three-pane layout — no prior three-pane/rail+list+detail pattern existed anywhere else in this app before this phase, so this is now the reference implementation. Follows `static/columns.js`'s `editingId`/`openModal`-`closeModal`-`saveColumn` shape (here: `editingId`/`selectDocument`-`startNewDocument`-`saveDocument`, modal-free — the detail panel is an inline form, not a popup) and `static/client_settings.js`'s chip-editor pattern (`addPrefix`/`removePrefix`/`renderPrefixList` → here: `addRole`/`removeRole`/`renderRoleChips` and `addField`/`removeField`/`renderFieldChips`, generalized into a shared `renderChipList(container, items, onRemove)` helper since Documents has two independent flat-string-array fields, not `client_settings.js`'s 5-keyed-category structure). `client_settings.html`'s `.prefix-chip*` CSS is scoped inside that page's own inline `<style>` block and unreachable from other pages — redefined here as `.ar-chip*` in `style.css` rather than introduced as a cross-page dependency; if either chip-editor's visual styling changes, check whether the other should too, since they're currently identical by design but are two separate rule sets, not shared classes. `data-nav-module="Audit Rules" data-nav-parent="index.html"` — placed under the dashboard's Administration group (not Setup), matching where the inert dashboard card already sits from the earlier 2-phase placeholder work; that dashboard card is still not linked to this page (it's an inert `.coming-soon` card with no id, per the earlier 2-phase placeholder project, out of this 9-phase build's scope) — a later phase should give it an id and wire it to `/static/audit_rules.html` once the module is further along.

- **Audit Rules module (new, confirmed 9-phase requirement — distinct from the earlier 2-phase dashboard-card/row-icon placeholders)**: schema lives in `database.py`'s `init_db()` under the `audit_rule_` table prefix (kept distinct from the pre-existing, unrelated `audit_log`/`audit_procedure_library` tables). Three reusable entities assembled *by reference*, not duplicated: `audit_rule_documents` (name, one `kb_note`, `is_active` — added Phase 2 for soft-delete/restore, plus child tables `audit_rule_document_fields` — the fields on that document available for cross-checks, e.g. Quantity/Amount/Date — and `audit_rule_document_auth_roles` — a list of authorisation roles, e.g. "Approved by", modelled as a list from day one); `audit_rule_cross_checks` (name, `compare_field` free text, `comparison_type` CHECK-constrained to `'All equal'`/`'Sequential increasing'`/`'Sequential decreasing'`/`'Within tolerance %'`, `is_active` — added Phase 3, plus ordered junction `audit_rule_cross_check_documents`); `audit_rule_categories` (name, one `kb_overview`, `is_active` — added Phase 4, plus junctions `audit_rule_category_documents`/`audit_rule_category_cross_checks`). A Category is the entity a voucher will eventually reference (Phase 9 — no voucher/client_data schema change yet). This module is intended to **replace**, not run parallel to, the hardcoded `audit_procedure_library` lookup currently used by the verification module (confirmed migration target, Phase 9). Phase 1 was schema only; Phases 2-4 (all in `routers/audit_rules.py`) added full CRUD for all three entity types in order (Documents → Cross-checks → Categories) — do not wire anything into verification.py against these tables until Phase 9 confirms the migration. **Recurring pattern, now closed out across all three entity tables**: Phase 1's original `CREATE TABLE` for each entity never anticipated CRUD semantics, so each of Phases 2/3/4 had to add `is_active` both to the `CREATE TABLE` statement *and* a matching `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` upgrade block (the table already exists on any database that ran Phase 1's `init_db()`, so the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` addition alone is a no-op there) — this happened identically for `audit_rule_documents`, `audit_rule_cross_checks`, and `audit_rule_categories`; any *new* `audit_rule_*` table added in a future phase should be checked against this same gap before assuming `is_active` exists. All three CRUD surfaces (Documents/Cross-checks/Categories — `GET/POST/PUT /api/audit-rules/{documents,cross-checks,categories}`, `DELETE`+`POST .../restore`) follow `routers/clients.py`'s soft-delete/restore convention exactly (`is_active` flag, not a hard delete) and `routers/templates.py`'s delete-then-reinsert pattern for replacing an ordered child/junction list on create/update (`save_document_auth_roles()`/`save_document_cross_check_fields()`/`save_cross_check_documents()`/`save_category_documents()`/`save_category_cross_checks()`) — plain `execute_write()` calls in a loop, no new transactional pattern introduced anywhere in this module. Reuse-count fields are now fully live end-to-end: Documents' and Cross-checks' `used_by_categories_count` (`COUNT(*)` against `audit_rule_category_documents`/`audit_rule_category_cross_checks`) needed zero code changes in Phase 4 and now correctly return non-zero as soon as a Category references them (confirmed live: creating then editing a test Category moved a referenced Document's/Cross-check's count `0 → 1 → 0`) — this is what "the counts were already querying the junction tables" in the Phase 4 brief meant, and it held up exactly as predicted. Categories' own `used_by_vouchers_count` is different: `get_category_used_by_vouchers_count()` is a **hardcoded 0 placeholder**, not a live query — no voucher/client_data column references a Category yet, so there's nothing to count against until Phase 9 adds that link; the field exists now purely so the frontend (Phase 7) doesn't need a later API contract change, and this function is the one place to swap in a real query once Phase 9 lands. SQLite foreign keys are **not enforced** on this app's connections (`get_db()` never sets `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`), so every `audit_rule_*` junction-table write in this module validates referenced-row existence explicitly at the API layer rather than trusting the schema's `FOREIGN KEY` clauses — `validate_cross_check_payload()` (Phase 3, checks `document_ids`) and `validate_category_payload()` (Phase 4, checks both `document_ids` and `cross_check_ids`) both do this. Cross-checks additionally validate `comparison_type` against the fixed set client-side (mirroring the DB's own CHECK constraint, so a bad value returns a clean 400 not a raw 500) and that `compare_field` is cross-check-eligible on every selected Document (reuses `get_document_cross_check_fields()` directly). Categories additionally enforce the brief's locked containment rule: every Cross-check attached to a Category may only reference Documents that are *also* in that Category's own `document_ids` list — `validate_category_payload()` rejects (400, naming both the Cross-check and the missing Document id(s)) any Category payload that violates this, checked by reading each selected Cross-check's own `audit_rule_cross_check_documents` rows and confirming they're a subset of the Category's document-id set. None of `audit_rule_documents.name`, `audit_rule_cross_checks.name`, or `audit_rule_categories.name` has a uniqueness constraint/check — not introduced in any of the three phases since the brief never asked for one; don't assume names are unique when building later phases (frontend, Phase 9 voucher wiring) against these tables.
