- 2026-07-23: **Trial Balance — Periodic dates & overwrite warning, Section 2, Phase 5 of 6 (backend: accept period + detect overwrite — `routers/trial_balance.py` only)** done. **Confirmed with the user first**: since `trial_balance_uploads` has no `UNIQUE(client_id, as_of_date)` (every upload is deliberately its own row), "overwrite" needed a clarified meaning before writing any conflict logic — user chose **true delete-then-insert**, not just a soft "latest wins" convention: confirming the overwrite genuinely deletes the prior exact-period upload and its accounts before the new one is created. New shared `find_conflicting_uploads(client_id, period_start, period_end)` is the single source of truth for "does an exact-period upload already exist" — exact match only on `period_start`+`period_end` for the same client (never an overlap check: a monthly TB inside an already-uploaded quarterly one is never flagged, confirmed live), matches regardless of the existing row's `status` (parsed/error/pending — the schema draws no distinction, so a simple "does one exist" rule was used rather than special-casing failed attempts), returns the raw row list (most recent first) since more than one conflicting row can exist. Two new shared helpers sit next to it: `_validate_period_dates()` (ISO format + `period_end >= period_start`, same `strptime` pattern `as_of_date` already uses) and `_serialize_conflicting_upload()` (one response shape reused by both the check endpoint's `existing_upload` and the upload endpoint's 409 `detail`, so the frontend, Phase 6, can render both with one function). New read-only `GET /api/trial-balance/check-period-conflict?client_id=&period_start=&period_end=` is the two-step flow's "step 1" — touches no data, returns `{"conflict": false, "existing_upload": null}` or `{"conflict": true, "existing_upload": {...}, "conflicting_upload_count": N}`. `POST /api/trial-balance/upload` gained 4 new optional Form fields (`period_start`/`period_end`/`period_type`/`confirm_overwrite`, all backward-compatible — omitting `period_start`/`period_end` entirely skips all new logic and reproduces the endpoint's exact pre-Phase-5 behavior, confirmed live below) and a new validation/gate block inserted before the pending-upload-row INSERT: rejects if only one of `period_start`/`period_end` is given (400), validates both if given, then on a conflict either 409s with the same shape `check-period-conflict` returns (when `confirm_overwrite` is false — this is what protects against Phase 6's UI being skipped or a stray API call, per the brief) or deletes every conflicting upload's accounts then its own row (`DELETE FROM trial_balance_accounts WHERE upload_id = ?` before `DELETE FROM trial_balance_uploads WHERE id = ?`, for **all** matches, not just the latest) and logs the deletion via `log_audit()` before proceeding. The explicit two-step child-then-parent delete is deliberate, not relying on `ON DELETE CASCADE` — this app's connections don't enable `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` (already documented in this same Conventions section for Audit Rules/Trial Balance Phase 1), so a bare parent-row delete would silently leave orphaned account rows. The pending-row INSERT and final row now carry `period_start`/`period_end`/`period_type` (`None` when omitted, matching the columns' nullable Phase-4 schema). No schema/migration changes this phase (Phase 4 already added the 3 columns); `classify_accounts()`, mapping/suggestion logic, `list_trial_balance_accounts()`, `get_trial_balance_summary()`, `override_account_classification()`, and `download_trial_balance_template()` are all untouched. New `compute_preview_document_group_id(row_data, extract_date, doc_key_column, row_id)` mirrors `get_document_group_id()`'s logic, appending `||{extract_date}`; falls back to a per-row-unique `__row_{id}` when the key is blank, so blank-key rows are never silently merged together. `GET /api/data/preview` now returns `document_key_column`/`date_column`/`amount_columns` at the top level (both the empty-result early return and the main return) and a `document_group_id` on every row. Frontend (`static/databank.js`): `fetchPreviewData()` stores the three new top-level fields into module state (`previewDocumentKeyColumn`/`previewDateColumn`/`previewAmountColumns`); `renderPreviewRows()` does a single pass over the already-paginated `rows` array (**grouping is per-page only — a voucher split across a page boundary is not stitched back together**, per the confirmed brief), comparing each row's `document_group_id` against its immediate neighbors to determine `isFirstInGroup`/`isLastInGroup` — no restructuring into nested arrays. Serial-number text and the Document-key/Date **cells** are blanked on every row after the first in a group (history/quality-flag icons still render per-row regardless, since they're facts about that specific `client_data` row, not the group); every other column, including every Amount column, still shows each line's own value. A running `groupSums` accumulator (reset on `isFirstInGroup`) sums each Amount column across the group; on `isLastInGroup` (and only if the template has at least one Amount column), a `<tr class="preview-subtotal-row">` is appended with all cells blank except the Amount column(s), which show the group's sum via the existing `formatCellValue()`. A single-line "group" still gets its own subtotal row for visual consistency (equal to that one line's amount) — this was a judgment call, not explicitly stated either way in the brief. CSS (`static/databank.html`, next to `.availability-table`): new `.preview-subtotal-row td` rule gives the row a 2px top+bottom border and a light background, "boxing" each document's block off from the next, per the brief. No other row/table styling, pagination, filters, or endpoint was touched. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using real ACME data: a multi-line voucher (CPV-0726-222, client 1, Transaction Report) correctly returned 6 consecutive rows sharing one `document_group_id`; a single-line-only template (Gate Pass, June 2026 data) correctly returned 9 distinct `document_group_id`s, one per document; `document_key_column`/`date_column`/`amount_columns` all resolved correctly for both templates (`Voucher ID`/`Transaction Date`/`['Debit Amount','Credit Amount']` and `GP no`/`Transaction Date`/`['Quantity']` respectively); confirmed `/api/clients` unaffected (regression spot-check). `python -m py_compile routers/data.py` and `node --check static/databank.js` both pass. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session (same recurring gap as most phases on this page), so the actual rendered blank cells/subtotal-row borders in a browser were not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass.

## Save Column Mapping (3 entries)


- **Save Column Mapping feature (new, confirmed 3-phase requirement)**: `saved_column_mappings` (database.py, added right after the `client_voucher_prefixes` seeding block) stores one row per mapped template column (`client_id`, `template_id`, `template_column_id`, `excel_column`), `UNIQUE(client_id, template_id, template_column_id)`, upserted via delete-then-reinsert on save — mirrors `template_column_mappings`' own one-row-per-column storage and the delete-then-reinsert pattern already used by `update_template()`/`save_document_auth_roles()`. Keyed by client+template (not template alone) since different clients export the same template with differently worded Excel headers. `POST /api/upload/save-mapping` (routers/import_export.py) validates client/template are active (404 otherwise), skips any mapping entry with a blank `excel_column` (nothing meaningful to save for an unmatched column), and fully replaces whatever was previously saved for that client+template. `GET /api/upload/saved-mapping?client_id=&template_id=` deliberately returns `{"has_saved_mapping": false, "mappings": []}` rather than 404 when nothing is saved — keeps the auto-apply-on-load logic (Phase A2) a simple flag check with no special-case error handling. This completes all 3 phases of the Save Column Mapping requirement. **Phase A2 (frontend save action + auto-apply on load, `static/upload.html` + `static/upload.js` only)**: a "💾 Save Mapping" button sits inside `#mappingPanel`'s `.section-title` row (next to `#mappingCount`, not the `#modeActions` action-bar below it — this is a mapping-table-scoped action, not an import action), styled via new `.btn-save-mapping` (upload.html's own `<style>` block, same small icon-button language as `.btn-download-icon`). Its click handler filters `currentMappings` to matched entries only (`SavedMappingEntry.excel_column` is a required `str` server-side, so an unmatched/`null` entry must be dropped client-side before sending, not left to the endpoint's own blank-skip) and POSTs `{client_id, template_id, mappings: [{template_column_id, excel_column}]}` — always a full overwrite, matching the backend's own upsert. New shared `getCurrentClientId()` (upload.js, next to `formatDate()`) factors out the `isClientSelected()`/`getSelectedClientId()`/`localStorage` fallback already used inline in the `importBtn` handler (left untouched, not part of this phase) so this and the auto-apply function below don't duplicate it. New `applySavedMapping()` is called from `autoMapColumns()`'s success path, right after `clearRestorePreview()` and before `renderMapping()` — the single injection point every path that reaches the mapping table (template select, sheet change, file (re)load) already funnels through. It `GET`s the saved mapping for the current client+template and, for each saved `{template_column_id, excel_column}`, overrides the matching `currentMappings` entry's `excel_column`/`is_matched` **only if that exact excel_column string is still present in the current sheet's `excelHeaders`** — the "never force a mismatch" rule is implemented as an exact-header-presence check (the backend stores the literal header text, so this is the closest safe interpretation of "matches closely"); anything not present keeps whatever `autoMapColumns()`'s own backend call already guessed, untouched. A fetch failure or `has_saved_mapping: false` both resolve to "apply nothing" (console.warn only on a genuine fetch error, matching `refreshDateFormatPreview()`'s existing non-fatal-error convention) — never blocks or delays the normal auto-map flow. The success status message gets an appended note when anything was auto-applied (`✅ Auto‑mapped X/Y columns (N from your saved mapping)`). The mapping table's own dropdowns/edit behavior needed zero changes — a saved-mapping override is just a different starting value for `currentMappings`, still fully editable afterward, same as any auto-mapped value. Verified directly against the live `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) by calling `POST`/`GET /api/upload/save-mapping`/`saved-mapping` exactly as the new JS does (client 1, template 4 "Gate Pass"): confirmed `has_saved_mapping` goes `false → true` after saving 2 columns and the GET response shape exactly matches what `applySavedMapping()` expects; cleared the test row afterward via an empty-mappings save (`saved_count: 0`, confirmed `has_saved_mapping: false` again). `node --check static/upload.js` passes. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session (same recurring gap as most phases in this log), so the actual button click, live table pre-fill on reload, and the "fall back on a differently-worded header" case were not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass before Phase A3. **Phase A3, FINAL (clear a saved mapping, `routers/import_export.py` + `static/upload.html` + `static/upload.js` only)**: "edit" needed no new UI — Phase A2's Save Mapping button already overwrites on click (delete-then-reinsert), so the one real gap was an explicit way to remove a saved mapping entirely. New `DELETE /api/upload/saved-mapping?client_id=&template_id=` (routers/import_export.py, directly after `get_saved_column_mapping()`) deletes the matching `saved_column_mappings` rows and returns `{"message", "deleted_count"}` — deliberately as lenient as the existing `GET` (no client/template existence checks; "nothing was saved" is a normal outcome, not a 404). Since `execute_write()` returns `cursor.lastrowid` (meaningless for a `DELETE`), `deleted_count` is read via a `SELECT COUNT(*)` immediately before the delete, same "count in Python, not off the write call" pattern `save_column_mapping()`'s own `saved_count` already uses. Frontend: a "🗑️ Clear Saved Mapping" button sits right next to `#saveMappingBtn` in the same `.section-title` row, styled via new `.btn-clear-mapping` (upload.html, same small icon-button sizing as `.btn-save-mapping` but with a red hover treatment matching this app's existing destructive-action color, `.file-detail .clear`'s `#dc2626`) — signals it removes the *persisted* mapping, not the on-screen table. Its click handler (upload.js, right after the Save Mapping handler) reuses `getCurrentClientId()` unchanged, gates on `selectedTemplateId`, shows a plain native `window.confirm()` before calling the new endpoint (chosen over a custom modal since this is a single flat destructive action with no follow-on state, unlike verification.js's multi-step navigation-confirm modals), and reports `deleted_count` back via `showStatus()` — a "cleared" success message when `> 0`, a neutral "nothing was saved" info message when `0` (both are valid outcomes, not errors). Deliberately does not touch the currently-displayed mapping table/`currentMappings` — only the saved copy is removed, so a later reload/re-select for this client+template simply stops auto-applying anything, falling back to ordinary `autoMapColumns()` exactly as if nothing had ever been saved. Verified directly against the live `--reload` dev server (port 5000, same already-running process, `netstat`-confirmed unchanged PID after the edit — reload picked up the change with no restart): saved a 2-column test mapping (client 1, template 4), `DELETE`d it (`deleted_count: 2`), confirmed a follow-up `GET` returned `has_saved_mapping: false`, then called `DELETE` again on the now-empty pair and confirmed it's idempotent (`deleted_count: 0`, no error). `python -m py_compile routers/import_export.py` and `node --check static/upload.js` both pass. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so the actual button click and native confirm-dialog flow were not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass. **This completes the entire 3-phase Save Column Mapping requirement** (Phase A1: backend storage + save/load API; Phase A2: frontend save action + auto-apply; Phase A3: this clear action).

- 2026-07-21: Save Column Mapping Phase A2 of 3 (frontend save action + auto-apply on load, `static/upload.html` + `static/upload.js` only) done — added a "💾 Save Mapping" button in the Column Mapping panel wired to Phase A1's `POST /api/upload/save-mapping`, and a new `applySavedMapping()` called from `autoMapColumns()`'s success path that auto-fills a previously saved mapping for the current client+template whenever the saved Excel header is still present on the current sheet (falls back to auto-mapping's own guess otherwise, never forcing a mismatch). Table stays fully editable either way. No backend changes — reused Phase A1's endpoints as-is. Phase A3 (edit/delete a saved mapping) remains. See full entry in the Conventions section above.

- 2026-07-21: Save Column Mapping Phase A3 of 3, FINAL (clear a saved mapping, `routers/import_export.py` + `static/upload.html` + `static/upload.js`) done — this completes the entire 3-phase Save Column Mapping requirement. New "🗑️ Clear Saved Mapping" button next to Save Mapping calls a new `DELETE /api/upload/saved-mapping?client_id=&template_id=` endpoint (behind a native `confirm()`) that removes the persisted mapping for the current client+template, reporting `deleted_count` back via the status bar. "Edit" needed no new UI — Save Mapping's existing overwrite-on-save already covers it. After clearing, the next upload for that client+template falls back to ordinary auto-mapping, same as if nothing had ever been saved. See full entry in the Conventions section above.

## Trial Balance Module (21 entries)


- **Trial Balance — Column mapping & standard template, Section 1, Phase 2 of 3 (mapping window UI, `static/trial_balance.html` + `static/trial_balance.js` only — no backend changes, Phase 1 already complete)**: once a file is selected, `loadColumnMappingForFile(file)` runs `suggestColumnMapping(file)` (POSTs the raw file to Phase 1's `/api/trial-balance/suggest-mapping`) and `readFileRowsForPreview(file)` (client-side SheetJS parse — `trial_balance.html` gained the same CDN `<script>` tag `upload.html` already uses, since this page never loaded SheetJS before) in parallel via `Promise.all`, guarded by a `mappingRequestToken` stale-response counter (same convention as Verification's audit guidance panel) so a fast re-select of a different file can't let a slower response overwrite the newer file's state. Surfaces only the 4 fields the brief lists (`TB_MAPPING_FIELDS`: Account Code/Name/Debit/Credit) — Phase 1's backend also supports optional Type/Opening Balance/Closing Balance roles, but this UI never shows or sends them (omitting an `Optional[str] = Form(None)` field is a no-op server-side, not an error). **Header list authority**: both the mapping dropdowns' options and the preview table's column labels are sourced from `suggest-mapping`'s own `headers` array (not a separate client-side header parse) — guarantees the dropdown options are always exactly what the upload endpoint will validate against; the preview's row *values* come from the client-side SheetJS parse (`sheet_to_json(sheet, {header:1})`, rows sliced to the first 5 data rows) and are matched to the backend header list purely by column **index**, not by re-matching header text, since both read the same file's first sheet top-to-bottom in the same order. `renderMappingDropdowns()` mirrors `static/upload.js`'s `renderMapping()` interaction pattern exactly (per the brief's explicit instruction to match it): each field's `<select>` excludes whatever header another field has already claimed, and any `change` triggers a full table re-render so every row's exclusion list and ✅/❌ status stay in sync — `upload.js` itself was only read for reference, not edited. `checkMappingComplete()` is a frontend mirror of Phase 1's backend `validate_column_mapping()` — checks all 4 required fields (not only Account Code), reusing the existing `.status-bar`/`.status-bar.error` CSS classes for its inline message (`#mappingValidationMessage`) rather than inventing new styling, and names every still-missing field by label (e.g. "Please map the following required field(s) before uploading: Account Code, Credit."); it gates a new `hasMapping` condition in `updateClientDependentUI()` (ANDed alongside the existing client/file/date checks) and is re-checked defensively inside `uploadTrialBalance()` before building the `FormData`, which now also appends all 4 mapping fields alongside the existing `client_id`/`as_of_date`/`file`. `#uploadTrialBalanceBtn` was relocated (moved, not duplicated) from the top Upload form-group to the bottom of the new `#mappingSection` (hidden until a file is selected), so the page's natural top-to-bottom flow now reads: pick file → review/correct the suggested mapping → click Upload & Classify. The mapping table and preview table both reuse the existing `.tb-review-table`/`.tb-review-table-wrapper` CSS classes as-is (visual consistency with the page's Review Classifications table below); the only new CSS is a `.tb-review-table select` rule, since that class never previously held a `<select>`. `resetColumnMapping()` (shared by the Clear-file button and `loadColumnMappingForFile()`'s own error path) clears all 3 mapping state vars and hides the section, so a failed `suggest-mapping` call (unreadable file, network error) never leaves stale mapping state visible for the wrong file. Verified end-to-end against the live `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted): re-confirmed `POST /api/trial-balance/suggest-mapping`'s response shape (`{headers, suggestions}`) against a fresh 4-column test file matches exactly what the new JS reads (`suggestResult.headers`/`suggestResult.suggestions.<role>`); confirmed both served files contain the new markers with no drift; grepped both files and confirmed zero inline event handlers and no `<script>` blocks inside the HTML body. `node --check static/trial_balance.js` passes. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session (same recurring gap as nearly every phase in this module's history), so the actual dropdown pre-fill, preview table rendering, inline validation message, and a full upload-with-mapping click-through were not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass before Phase 3. Phase 3 (downloadable standard template) not started.

- **Trial Balance — Column mapping & standard template (new, confirmed 3-phase Section 1 requirement, distinct from the original 5-phase build above) — Section 1, Phase 1 of 3 (backend mapping support, `routers/trial_balance.py` only)**: replaces the original build's hardcoded header-name synonym matching (`identify_columns()`, now removed) with an explicit column-mapping payload the caller supplies on upload — 4 required roles (`account_code_column`/`account_name_column`/`debit_column`/`credit_column`, all `Optional[str] = Form(None)` at the FastAPI layer so validation produces one combined clear 400 rather than a generic 422) plus 3 optional roles (`type_column`/`opening_balance_column`/`closing_balance_column`). New `validate_column_mapping(mapping, headers)` raises `ValueError` (caught by the endpoint's existing outer except block, same `status='error'`+400 shape as before) naming every problem at once if a required role is missing/blank or any *provided* mapped column name doesn't exactly match a real header in the file — this is what makes an unmapped Account Code reject cleanly instead of failing deeper in `classify_accounts()`. The old synonym sets (`CODE_SYNONYMS` etc., now joined by new `OPENING_BALANCE_SYNONYMS`/`CLOSING_BALANCE_SYNONYMS`) and `clean_header()` are kept and reused only by new `suggest_column_mapping(headers)` — an exact-normalized-match pass followed by a bidirectional-substring fallback pass (mirroring `templates.py`'s `get_close_matches()` `"typed in x or x in typed"` logic, not a fuzzy-matching library), exposed via a new stateless `POST /api/trial-balance/suggest-mapping` endpoint (multipart, re-accepts the raw file, reads headers via a new shared `read_trial_balance_excel()` helper — extracted out of `upload_trial_balance()` so both endpoints read a sheet identically — and returns `{headers, suggestions}`, nothing stored). Opening/Closing Balance are validated-if-provided but not parsed into any new DB column this phase (no schema change was in scope) — their raw values are already captured in each account's existing `raw_row_data` JSON, so nothing is lost; a future phase can wire real storage if needed. `classify_accounts()`/the parent-child hierarchy logic and every response shape (`upload`/`accounts`/`summary`/`override`) are completely unchanged — only how the 4-7 columns are identified changed. No frontend changes yet (mapping window UI is Section 1/Phase 2; downloadable standard template is Phase 3); Section 2 (periodic dates + overwrite-warning) will touch this same upload endpoint again shortly, expected as an additive follow-up, not a redesign. Verified end-to-end against the live `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using a disposable test client (soft-deleted afterward) and a 5-row test hierarchy: `suggest-mapping` returned sensible Code/Name/Debit/Credit suggestions (Type correctly returned `null` for an abbreviation, "Mstr/Sub", that doesn't match any synonym — no false-positive substring match); a full valid mapping uploaded and classified correctly (2 parent/3 leaf, matching the known-hierarchy baseline used in earlier phases); omitting `account_code_column` alone, omitting all 4 required fields at once, and mapping a nonexistent column name each returned a clean single 400 naming the exact problem(s); a valid `type_column` mapping correctly populated `source_account_type` per row. `python -m py_compile routers/trial_balance.py` passes.

- **Trial Balance module Phase 3 of 5 (store + retrieve classified accounts, `routers/trial_balance.py` only — no schema/`main.py` changes needed, both already in place from Phases 1-2)**: two read-only `GET` endpoints added right after the existing upload endpoint. `GET /api/trial-balance/accounts?upload_id=&is_leaf=` lists one upload's accounts in original file order (`ORDER BY sort_order`), with an optional `is_leaf` filter (`true`→`classification='leaf'`, `false`→`'parent'`, omitted→both) — confirmed with the user to include, beyond the brief's explicitly-listed fields (code/name/parent_code/level/is_leaf/balances), the row's own `id` (Phase 5 needs a row identifier to target a specific account for a future override) and `manually_overridden` (always `false` today, but part of the same future-proofed shape) and `source_account_type` (the source file's raw cross-check "Type" value, so a reviewer can visually compare it against `is_leaf`) — all three purely additive, nothing from the brief's list was dropped. `classification`'s raw `'leaf'`/`'parent'` TEXT is translated into a boolean `is_leaf` in the response, matching the brief's exact field name rather than exposing the DB's internal string. `GET /api/trial-balance/summary?upload_id=` returns strictly `{total_count, leaf_count, parent_count}` — deliberately no upload metadata (file name/date/status) and no ambiguity-detection logic, per the brief's explicit "counts only" scope (the classification engine doesn't flag any row as ambiguous; that would need to be raised as a separate scope addition, not assumed here). Both endpoints share a new `_require_upload(upload_id)` helper (404 "Trial balance upload not found" if the upload row itself doesn't exist) — an upload that exists but has zero accounts (e.g. it errored during Phase 2's parsing) is **not** an error case for these two endpoints, it's a legitimate state that just returns an empty `accounts` list / all-zero counts. Still scoped to a single upload_id at a time, matching the classification engine's own scope (no cross-period comparison, already deferred in Phase 1). Verified end-to-end against an isolated `test.db` copy (same direct function-call approach as Phase 2, `starlette.testclient` still unavailable here): a 5-account test hierarchy (`1`/`1-100` parent, `1-100-001`/`1-200`/`2` leaf) listed correctly in file order with every field (`id`, `is_leaf`, `level`, `parent_account_code`, `debit_amount`/`credit_amount`, `source_account_type`, `manually_overridden`) correct; `is_leaf=true`/`is_leaf=false` each returned the exact expected subset; the summary's counts matched the list's own split exactly (`total_count:5, leaf_count:3, parent_count:2`); an unknown `upload_id` 404'd on both endpoints; an upload that errored during Phase 2 (no Code column) correctly returned an empty list and all-zero summary rather than a 404 or crash. Confirmed via the built OpenAPI schema that all three trial-balance routes (`/upload`, `/accounts`, `/summary`) are registered, and that `clients`/`client_data` row counts were unaffected. `python -m py_compile routers/trial_balance.py` passes.

- **Trial Balance module Phase 2 of 5 (parsing & classification engine, new `routers/trial_balance.py` + `main.py` two-line mount + `requirements.txt`)**: one endpoint, `POST /api/trial-balance/upload` (multipart: `file`, `client_id` Form, `as_of_date` Form) — upload + classify + store in one pass, per the confirmed scope (no retrieval endpoint (Phase 3) or review UI (Phase 5) yet). **Column identification**: since TB has no column-mapping UI (deliberately, unlike `import_export.py`/`templates.py`), columns are identified by new `identify_columns()`/`clean_header()` — headers are normalized (lowercased, all non-alphanumeric characters stripped) and matched *exactly* (not substring) against a per-role synonym set, processed Code→Name→Type→Debit→Credit in priority order so one header can never satisfy two roles. Only Code is required (`CODE_SYNONYMS = {"code","accountcode","ledgercode","accode","glcode","accountno","acno"}`) — `identify_columns()` raises `ValueError` if no Code-like header is found, which the endpoint turns into a 400 + an `'error'`-status upload row (not a raw crash). Name/Type/Debit/Credit synonym sets are in the same file, right below. **The core anti-corruption mechanism**: `pd.read_excel(..., dtype=str, keep_default_na=False, engine=...)` forces the *entire* sheet to raw strings at the pandas layer itself, not just the code column — confirmed via a direct side-by-side test that without `dtype=str`, a column containing `"001"` silently becomes the integer `1` (leading zero lost) under pandas' default type inference, while `dtype=str` preserves it exactly; this is the mechanism that prevents the Leather Crop-style code corruption. `engine` is picked by extension (`xlrd` for `.xls`, `openpyxl` for `.xlsx` — the `.xls` branch needed adding the `xlrd` package to `requirements.txt` and installing it, since pandas' `openpyxl` engine can't read legacy `.xls` at all; confirmed with the user before touching `requirements.txt`, outside the originally-confirmed file list). Blank Account Code rows are skipped silently (not stored, not an error, confirmed with the user — e.g. a spacer/section-title row); a duplicate Account Code within the same file is also skipped (keeping the first occurrence) and counted, both counts surfacing in the upload row's `notes` and the response, never blocking the rest of the file. **Classification** (`classify_accounts()`): implements the exact locked rule ("leaf unless some other code starts with `this code + '-'`") by walking every code's own dash-delimited proper prefixes and marking any prefix that is itself a real code in the file as `'parent'` — provably equivalent to an O(n²) any-other-code scan (a full explanation is in the function's own docstring) but runs in O(n · depth) instead. Debit/Credit are best-effort parsed via new `parse_amount()` (strips thousands-commas, honors the accounting parenthesis-negative convention e.g. `"(1,234.56)"` → `-1234.56`; never raises — an unparsable value just becomes `None`, since amounts are secondary to classification this phase); if neither a Debit nor Credit column is found, both fields are simply left null (no single signed "Balance" column fallback, confirmed with the user). The upload row is inserted immediately as `status='pending'` *before* parsing begins, so a failure at any later step updates it to `status='error'` with the exception message in `notes` rather than leaving no trace at all; on success it's updated to `status='parsed'` with the real `row_count` and a `notes` summary of any skipped/duplicate rows. Bulk insert into `trial_balance_accounts` reuses `templates.py`'s `import_backup()` transaction shape exactly (`get_raw_conn()` → `BEGIN TRANSACTION` → loop inserts → `commit()` / `except: rollback()` / `finally: close()`). Verified end-to-end against an isolated copy of `test.db` (not the live one) by calling the endpoint function directly (bypassing the HTTP layer, since `starlette.testclient` needed an `httpx2` package this environment doesn't have) with hand-built `.xlsx`/`.xls` test files: the tricky code `10-10-25-10` round-tripped exactly with correct `level`/`parent_account_code`/`classification`; a small known hierarchy (`1`, `1-100`, `1-100-001`, `1-200`, `2`) classified correctly (`1`/`1-100` parent, the rest leaf); a "Type" column's values landed in `source_account_type` without affecting `classification`; one blank-code row and one duplicate-code row were each correctly skipped and counted; a legacy `.xls` file (no Type column, testing the optional-role gap) parsed correctly; a file with no Code-like header was correctly rejected with `status='error'` and the exact message in `notes`; an unknown `client_id` correctly 404'd and a malformed `as_of_date` correctly 400'd, neither leaving a stray upload row. Confirmed `main.py` mounts the router correctly (`/api/trial-balance/upload` present in the built OpenAPI schema) and that `clients`/`client_data`/`audit_rule_categories` row counts were unaffected by any of this. `python -m py_compile routers/trial_balance.py main.py` passes. - **Trial Balance module (new, confirmed 5-phase requirement) — Phase 1 of 5 (database schema, `database.py` only)**: new, dedicated feature — deliberately not an extension of `import_export.py`/`templates.py` (those handle generic template-mapped imports; TB needs hierarchy-aware parent/leaf classification derived from the account code structure, not client-specific text markers like "+"/"»"). ## Verification ↔ Assign Categories Link (11 entries)


- **Verification page hard-refresh view persistence (confirmed fix, `static/verification.js` + `static/verification.html`)**: the page's three JS-driven views (dashboard/cashbook/session) are now reflected in the URL via `state`/`id` query params, distinct from the pre-existing **entry-only** `type`/`view` params (`?type=cash`, `?view=cashbook`/`?view=bankbook` — those only mean "open the Start-Verification popup" and are read once by `window.onload`; never reuse those two values for anything else). New scheme: `?state=cashbook&id=<cashbook name>&type=cash|bank` and `?state=session&id=<session id>&type=cash|bank`; dashboard = no `state`/`id` at all. `setVerificationUrl(view, id)` is the single place that writes this, via `history.replaceState` (never `pushState` — this page manages its own "back" behavior through `setBackOverride()`/the global navbar arrow, not the browser's native back button, so no new history entries should ever be introduced here). Two existing functions were split into a thin guard/POST half plus a shared "activate this view" core, so both the normal click-driven path and the hard-refresh restore path go through identical code: `openCashbook()` → `activateCashbookView(cashbook)`; `startSessionFromCashbook()` → `activateSessionView(sessionId)`. New `restoreCashbookView(cashbookName)`/`restoreSessionView(sessionId)` (called only from `window.onload`, checked ahead of the existing `type`/`view` popup-trigger logic, which is otherwise untouched) always re-fetch fresh from the server rather than restoring any cached state — `restoreSessionView()` uses the existing `GET /api/verification/audited_cashbook/{id}` (routers/verification.py) as its existence+data check, since it already 404s cleanly on a missing/cancelled session; **note its response nests session fields under `data.session`, not top-level** (e.g. `data.session.cashbook_name`, not `data.cashbook_name` — a real bug caught during this session's own verification, before it shipped). On a 404/failure, `showDashboardWithMessage(message)` switches back to the dashboard, resets the URL to plain, and shows a new `#dashboardFallbackMessage` div (static/verification.html, inside `#dashboardContent`, reuses the existing `.upload-status`/`.error` classes already used by `#verificationStatus` elsewhere on this page — no new CSS) instead of leaving a broken session screen. `exitCashbookView()`/`exitSession()` each gained one line to keep the URL in sync when leaving a view (`setVerificationUrl('dashboard')` / `setVerificationUrl('cashbook', selectedCashbook)`). The Transaction Report view is intentionally not covered by this scheme (out of the confirmed brief). Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using real ACME data (client 1, session 364): confirmed `GET /api/verification/audited_cashbook/364` returns the nested `{session: {...}, transactions: [...]}` shape (caught and fixed the `data.cashbook_name` bug this way, before it could ship); confirmed a nonexistent session id (`999999`) 404s cleanly with `"Verification session not found or cancelled."`, exercising the fallback path; confirmed `GET /api/verification/cashbooks` (used by `restoreCashbookView()`'s `loadCashbooks()` call) is unaffected. `node --check static/verification.js` passes; grepped the HTML addition and confirmed no inline event handlers were introduced. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session (same recurring gap as most phases in this app's history), so the actual hard-refresh click-through in a real browser (URL updating live, session/cashbook view re-populating on reload, the fallback message rendering for a genuinely-gone session) was not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass. **Follow-up fix, same day**: this visual gap in verification meant a real bug shipped — `activateSessionView()` never explicitly hid `dashboardContent` (unlike `activateCashbookView()`, which already did), so hard-refreshing straight into `?state=session&id=...` rendered the dashboard stacked underneath the session view. Fixed by adding the same `dashboardContent.style.display = 'none';` line `activateCashbookView()` already had. **Lesson**: when adding a new entry path into an existing "activate this view" function (here, calling `activateSessionView()` directly from a URL restore instead of only via `startSessionFromCashbook()`, which happened to always run after the dashboard was already hidden by a prior step), audit that function's own display-toggle completeness independently — don't assume it's correct just because every previous call site happened to reach it in a state where the omission was invisible. **Second follow-up fix, same day**: the same blind spot existed on the way *out* of a session — `exitSession()` manually re-implemented a subset of `activateCashbookView()`'s job (display toggling, back-override, URL, `fetchCashbookData()`) instead of calling it, so it inherited none of `activateCashbookView()`'s/`loadCashbooks()`'s actual population of the cashbook selector/date range, which only mattered once a session became reachable without ever passing through `openCashbook()` first (i.e. via `restoreSessionView()`). Fixed by having `exitSession()` call `restoreCashbookView(selectedCashbook)` directly instead of hand-rolling a partial copy of what it does. **General rule this keeps surfacing**: once a view can be entered from more than one path (normal click-through vs. URL restore), every function that *transitions into or out of* that view must go through the one shared "activate"/"restore" function for it, never a hand-rolled subset — the subset is exactly what silently drifts out of sync when a new entry path is added later. **Third follow-up fix, same day (confirmed fix, `static/verification.js` only)**: a hard refresh correctly restored the right session but always landed on the session's earliest-Pending voucher (`loadNextTransaction()`'s default), not the voucher the auditor was actually on — e.g. after navigating without validating every voucher in strict order. Extended the same scheme with a new `voucher` URL param (the voucher_id string) kept in sync by new `setVerificationUrlVoucher(voucherId)` (a dedicated writer, separate from `setVerificationUrl()` since it fires on every voucher-to-voucher move and shouldn't re-touch `state`/`id`/`type`; no-op outside `state=session`) — called, per explicit confirmation, at all three places `currentVoucherId` is actually assigned, not just Prev/Next: `loadNextTransaction()`, `moveToAdjacentVoucher()` (Prev/Next arrows), and `navigateToTransaction()` (the 🔍 search-popover row click) — `completeTransaction()`'s auto-advance-after-verifying needed no separate wiring since it just calls `loadNextTransaction()` internally, already covered. `setVerificationUrl()` itself now also unconditionally clears the `voucher` param on every view transition, so a stale voucher id from a previous session/cashbook is never carried over. `activateSessionView(sessionId, targetVoucherId = null)` gained the optional second parameter: if given and a matching entry exists in the already-loaded `sessionTransactions`, it calls the existing `navigateToTransaction(matchingDetailId)` directly (reusing its synchronous full-voucher render, zero new fetches) instead of the default `loadNextTransaction()`; falls back to that default if no target was given or the target voucher no longer exists in the session — `startSessionFromCashbook()`'s call (a freshly-started session) omits the param and is completely unaffected. `restoreSessionView()` reads the `voucher` param from the URL and passes it through. No backend/schema changes. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using real ACME data (session 364, 311 transactions across many distinct vouchers): confirmed `GET /api/verification/audited_cashbook/364`'s per-line `detail_id`/`voucher_id` fields match exactly what the new matching logic in `activateSessionView()` reads; regression-confirmed `GET /api/verification/next/364` and `GET /api/clients` unaffected. `node --check static/verification.js` passes; grepped and confirmed all three `currentVoucherId = ...` assignment sites now call `setVerificationUrlVoucher`. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so the actual click-through (navigate to voucher 3 of 7, hard-refresh, land back on voucher 3; same after a popover jump and after completing a voucher) was not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass.

Harmless for a session reached the normal way (dashboard → popup → `openCashbook()` → session, which had already populated the cashbook date range/selector before the session started), but a session reached via the `?state=session&id=...` hard-refresh restore never runs `openCashbook()`/`activateCashbookView()` at all — so exiting it called `fetchCashbookData()` with an empty date range, which silently bails out, rendering a blank cashbook. `exitSession()` now calls `await restoreCashbookView(selectedCashbook)` (made `async` for this) — the exact same fresh load/render path (`loadCashbooks()` + `activateCashbookView()`) a hard refresh into `?state=cashbook` already uses, which is why a refresh at that same point always "fixed" it. This also removed `exitSession()`'s now-redundant manual display-toggle/`setBackOverride()`/`setVerificationUrl()` calls, since `activateCashbookView()` already does all of that. See the Conventions note below.

## Voucher Supporting-Document Linking (incl. follow-up fixes) (33 entries)


- **Observation roll-up should replace-per-procedure, not append-forever (confirmed fix, `routers/verification.py` only) — supersedes the append-based design of every earlier observation-sync fix above.** Reported directly against the screenshots from the previous fix's own live testing: repeatedly editing the *same* procedure's observation box ("Hello World 1" → "2" → "3") kept stacking up separate lines for that one box instead of replacing its own line — the `last_synced_text` duplicate-suppression column (added two fixes ago) only ever stopped an *unchanged* re-save from duplicating; it did nothing for a genuine edit, which is exactly what was happening. Required behaviour: the voucher's Observation field holds **exactly one labelled line per document/procedure at all times** — saving that procedure's box again replaces its own line in place, every other procedure's line stays untouched. **`sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` was rewritten from incremental-append to a full rebuild on every call**, rather than a find/replace on the stored text (considered and rejected as more fragile — opaque string-splicing on an already-assembled blob, vs. deriving the whole field fresh from the one table that's the actual source of truth). Every call now: reads **every** `voucher_line_observations` row across all sibling lines (not filtered to `synced = 0` anymore — this is the key correctness point, since only considering "pending" rows would silently drop an untouched procedure's line from the rebuilt text); dedupes to one row per `document_id`, keeping whichever sibling's entry has the latest `updated_at` (same tie-break `get_line_observations()` already uses for the identical cross-session scenario); drops any document whose current text is blank (so clearing a box removes its line entirely, not leaves a stale one); builds one block per remaining document ordered by `document_id` ascending for a stable order; and **overwrites** `verification_details.observations` with the result (or `NULL` if nothing remains) instead of appending. Confirmed via grep before implementing that this column has exactly one writer in the entire codebase — this same function — and no manual-entry UI exists anywhere that types into it directly, so a full overwrite can't clobber anything else. **`synced`/`last_synced_text` are now bookkeeping-only, not gating logic** — every entry is considered on every rebuild regardless of its synced state, since omitting an already-synced entry would silently drop its line; the two fields are still written per entry (for consistency/audit visibility) but nothing reads them to decide whether to include a block anymore. This makes the two fixes immediately above (orphaned-session sync, immediate-sync-on-save) still fully valid — sibling resolution and the "sync on every explicit save" trigger are both unchanged and still correct — only *how the field is assembled* changed, from append to rebuild. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using the exact real repro line (voucher CPV-0726-222, "LOCAL PURCHASE (CASH)", client_data_id 5055, detail_id 84644): confirmed the pre-existing 3-line duplicate ("Hello World 1/2/3", all under Purchase Demand); re-saving Purchase Demand's box with new text correctly collapsed this to exactly one line (and, as a genuine side effect of now reading *all* entries not just pending ones, correctly also picked up a previously-orphaned "Purchase Order: hello" line from an *earlier sibling session* — 84333 — that the old append-only/synced-filtered logic had never surfaced at all, itself another small instance of the same class of bug these fixes have been closing); saving a fresh Vendor Bill observation correctly appeared as its own new line with Purchase Demand/Purchase Order untouched; editing Vendor Bill again correctly changed only its own line; clearing Vendor Bill correctly removed its line entirely while the other two lines were untouched. All test-induced state reverted afterward, confirmed via a follow-up query matching the exact pre-test row values. `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py` passes. No frontend changes were needed — `static/verification.js`'s `saveLineObservation()`/`renderVoucherLines()` (wired in the fix directly above) already display whatever `verification_details.observations` currently holds, so the corrected rebuild logic is reflected automatically with no JS changes.

- **Wire up the OBSERVATIONS column + suppress duplicate roll-up blocks (confirmed fix, `database.py` + `routers/verification.py` + `static/verification.js`) — two findings surfaced re-verifying the fix directly above in the browser, not by either fix itself being wrong.** Finding 1: the backend sync was (and is) genuinely correct, but the voucher table's "OBSERVATIONS" column has never displayed anything — it's the `<span class="voucher-line-observations-cell"></span>` placeholder added on 2026-07-15, explicitly logged then as "a future addition, not yet wired to any state/backend field," and nothing since (including the two sync fixes above) ever wired it. Fixed: `_fetch_session_details_grouped()` (routers/verification.py) now also selects `vd.observations`; `_build_verification_line()` returns it as an additive `"observations"` field, so `/next`, `/voucher_nav`, and every other caller of these shared helpers now carry it with no new endpoint. `save_line_observation()`'s response gained an additive `voucher_observations` field (the line's current, just-synced `verification_details.observations` text). `renderVoucherLines()` (static/verification.js) now fills `.voucher-line-observations-cell` from `line.observations` (via the existing `escapeHtml()` helper); `saveLineObservation()` additionally writes the fresh value into `currentVoucherLines` (so a later full re-render stays correct) and directly into the live DOM cell (`` .voucher-line-row[data-detail-id="${uid}"] .voucher-line-observations-cell ``, same "target by data-detail-id" convention `validateTransaction()` already uses for the status cell) — the auditor now sees the update the moment Save is clicked, no navigation needed. **No CSS added** — multi-block text (`\n`-separated in storage) currently collapses to one line in the cell (default `white-space: normal`, no wrap/line-break styling); a future pass could style this, out of scope for this phase's approved file list. Finding 2: because sync now fires on every individual "Save Observation" click (the fix above) rather than once per navigation, saving the *same* text twice in a row now appended two identical blocks instead of the old harmless no-op. Fixed by adding a nullable `last_synced_text` column to `voucher_line_observations` (database.py, standard idempotent `CREATE TABLE` + `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` upgrade-block pattern, since the table already has live data) recording what text was last actually rolled up for that `(voucher_line_id, document_id)` — distinct from `observation_text`, which always holds the current saved value even before syncing. `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` now only appends a block when a pending entry's `observation_text` (stripped) differs from `last_synced_text` (stripped) *and* is non-blank; every processed entry gets `last_synced_text` set to its own `observation_text` alongside `synced = 1` (now a per-row `UPDATE` in a loop, not the previous single bulk `IN (...)` statement, since the value differs per row). A genuine edit still appends its own distinct block — only exact repeats are suppressed. Verified end-to-end against the live `--reload` dev server (auto-reloaded on the edits, not restarted): migration confirmed via an isolated `test.db` copy (added via the `ALTER TABLE` path since the table pre-existed, a second `init_db()` run a clean no-op) and re-confirmed on the real `test.db`; against the real line from this session's trace (voucher CPV-0726-119, "Kitchen Expense CHS Residence", Vendor Bill document) — re-saving identical text a second time correctly produced no new block, while editing and re-saving with different text correctly appended a distinct new block; confirmed `voucher_observations` appears in the save response and `observations` now appears on every line from `GET /api/verification/voucher_nav`. All test-induced state reverted afterward, confirmed via a follow-up query matching the exact pre-test row values. `python -m py_compile database.py routers/verification.py` and `node --check static/verification.js` both pass. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so the actual on-screen column rendering and live cell update after clicking Save Observation were not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass.

- **Observation roll-up doesn't fire until an unrelated later action (confirmed fix, `routers/verification.py` only) — a different, narrower gap than the one directly above.** Live-tracing a brand-new observation save (not a pre-existing orphaned record) proved the fix above works correctly — a comment saved under an earlier session's line rolled up the moment `save_line_items()` next ran for it. But the *newest* comment (same voucher/line, current session) was still sitting `synced=0`, simply because **nothing had called `save_line_items()` for that specific line since it was typed** — `POST /api/verification/save_line_observation` (`save_line_observation()`) has always only written the entry and left the roll-up entirely dependent on some later, unrelated action (Next/Prev/Validate/Complete/Exit). From the auditor's side, clicking "💾 Save Observation" reads as a complete action, so waiting on an unrelated later click is a real gap, confirmed with the user. Fixed by having `save_line_observation()` call the existing `sync_line_observations_to_voucher(voucher_line_id)` **immediately** after the upsert, before the response is built (so the response's own `synced` field is truthful right away too) — no changes to `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` itself, which was already safe to call here as-is: idempotent (no-op if nothing pending) and marks entries synced as it goes, so `save_line_items()`'s own pre-existing call to the same helper (kept, unchanged, as a safety net) correctly finds nothing left to do on a later Next/Prev — no double-append. **Confirmed acceptable side effect**: `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` has no line-status gate (only `save_line_items()`'s "must be Pending" check does), so an observation can now roll up even after the line has already been validated/completed — this only ever touches the `observations` field, not validation state, so it's a genuine improvement, not a regression. Verified live end-to-end against the exact pending entry from this trace (`voucher_line_id` 84022, document 15, "Hello World"): the very next `save_line_observation` call returned `synced: true` immediately (no `save_line_items` call in between) and `verification_details.observations` picked up the appended block right away; a second edit-and-resave with different text correctly appended a second distinct block (append-only preserved, no overwrite); a follow-up `save_line_items` call for the same line correctly found nothing pending and added nothing further (no double-append). All test-induced state reverted afterward, confirmed via a follow-up query matching the exact pre-test row values. `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py` passes. No frontend changes were needed — the immediate sync happens transparently server-side within the same request `saveLineObservation()` (`static/verification.js`) already makes.

- **Observation sync doesn't roll up across orphaned sessions (confirmed fix, `routers/verification.py` only) — supersedes the Phase 3 entry directly above's claim that `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` "is untouched — it still only ever rolls an entry into its *own* `voucher_line_id`'s ... field, since that's inherently a per-session concern."** That claim turned out to be the actual bug: diagnosed directly against live `test.db` (not re-derived from code) — every one of the 4 existing `voucher_line_observations` rows was `synced=0` despite belonging to `Pending` lines (ruling out the "line already verified" gate in `save_line_items()` as the cause). Tracing `audit_log`+`verification_sessions` showed the real pattern: each time an observation was saved, a *new* verification session started (same root cause as the Phase 3 entry above — `start_verification_session()` has no resume logic) before that exact `voucher_line_id` ever got another `save_line_items()` call — so the observation's own session-specific id was orphaned before the sync could ever run for it, and `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()`'s `WHERE vlo.voucher_line_id = ?` (literal id only, no sibling resolution) could never find it again from a later session. Fixed by having `sync_line_observations_to_voucher(voucher_line_id)` call the existing `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids()` (same helper the Phase 3 fix already uses for every *read* path) first, then querying/marking-synced across that whole sibling set (`WHERE voucher_line_id IN (...)`) instead of the single literal id — still rolling the collected text into the *current* (active) line's own `observations` field, still append-only, still never raising. Verified against live data: called `save_line_items` for the most recent of 3 sibling lines sharing one `client_data_id` (5055) — all 3 previously-orphaned entries (spanning 3 different sessions) were correctly picked up, their two non-blank texts both appended in one combined block with no duplication, all 3 flipped to `synced=1`, and a 4th, unrelated row (different `client_data_id`) was correctly left untouched, confirming sibling resolution stays scoped per accounting line. Test-induced state fully reverted afterward, confirmed via a follow-up query matching the exact pre-test row values. `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py` passes. No frontend changes were needed — `static/verification.js`'s `saveLineObservation()` already saves correctly against whatever `uid` is open; the gap was entirely in the backend roll-up's read scope.

- **Voucher Supporting-Document Linking follow-up, Phase 3 of 4 — the real (deeper) Browse/Linked Evidence cross-session sync bug (confirmed fix, `routers/verification.py` + `routers/data.py` + `static/verification.js`)**: the fix immediately above solved a real but narrower same-session/different-document-tab disagreement; it did **not** fix the reported "Browse shows Assigned but Linked Evidence doesn't show it" symptom for CPV-0726-222/Purchase Demand, diagnosed this phase directly against `test.db`. **Root cause, confirmed with real data, not re-guessed from code**: `start_verification_session()` (routers/verification.py) has no "resume an existing session" logic — every time a cashbook is opened and verification is (re)started, a brand-new `verification_sessions` row and a brand-new set of `verification_details` rows are inserted for every voucher/line, even ones already worked on before (`test.db` had 393 such sessions for one cashbook at time of diagnosis). `voucher_line_documents` (Phase 1), `voucher_line_procedure_checks` (Phase 5), and `voucher_line_observations` (Phase 6) all key their data off `voucher_line_id` = `verification_details.id` — a **per-session, ephemeral id**, not a stable identity for "this voucher line." Proof: the real "LOCAL PURCHASE (CASH)" line of CPV-0726-222 is `client_data.id = 5055` (stable); in session 382 it was `verification_details.id = 78735` (Purchase Demand evidence linked there); in session 393 (the latest session) the *same* line is `verification_details.id = 82156` — Linked Evidence, filtered by `voucher_line_id = 82156`, could never see the assignment made under 78735, while Browse still correctly (if misleadingly) reported it "Assigned to CPV-0726-222" since it just resolves the assignment's own stored `voucher_line_id` back to a still-valid `transaction_ref` from the *old* session, with no check of whether that belongs to the currently-open one. **Fix (confirmed with the user: read-time resolution only, no schema migration, no change to session-start behavior, writes untouched)**: new `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids(voucher_line_id)` (routers/verification.py, next to `assign_supporting_document`) returns every `verification_details.id` across *all* sessions that shares the same underlying `client_data_id` as the given line — i.e. every past/present copy of that exact accounting line. `get_voucher_line_documents()`, `get_procedure_checks()`, and `get_line_observations()` all now query `WHERE voucher_line_id IN (...)` (the resolved sibling set) instead of `= ?`; `get_procedure_checks()`/`get_line_observations()` additionally dedup in Python by `(document_id, role_name)`/`document_id` respectively, keeping whichever sibling's row has the latest `checked_at`/`updated_at`, since two different sessions could each carry their own tick/observation for the same document — `get_voucher_line_documents()` needs no dedup (the partial unique index on `client_data_id` already guarantees one evidence row is never actively linked under more than one sibling). `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` (called from `save_line_items()`) is untouched — it still only ever rolls an entry into its *own* `voucher_line_id`'s `verification_details.observations` field, since that's inherently a per-session concern. For Browse's own "is this the same line" check (previously `String(row.assigned_to_voucher_line) === String(uid)`, broken for the same cross-session reason), `get_assignment_status_map()` gained an additive `voucher_line_client_data_id` field (the assigned row's own `vd.client_data_id`), threaded through `routers/data.py`'s `attach_assignment_flags()` as a new additive `assigned_to_line_client_data_id` field on `GET /api/data/preview`. Frontend: new shared `isSameUnderlyingLine(uid, row)` (static/verification.js, next to `formatAssignedVoucherLabel()`) looks up the current line's own `client_data_id` via `currentVoucherLines` (already carries it — confirmed via `_fetch_session_details_grouped()`'s response shape) and compares it against `row.assigned_to_line_client_data_id`, replacing the raw `voucher_line_id === uid` comparison in both `buildProcedureResultRowHtml()`'s `isSameLine` and `buildProcedureBrowseTableHtml()`'s `isOtherDocSameLine`. **Any future new query against `voucher_line_documents`/`voucher_line_procedure_checks`/`voucher_line_observations` that filters by a single `voucher_line_id` should go through `_resolve_sibling_voucher_line_ids()` first** (for reads) — a bare `WHERE voucher_line_id = ?` will silently miss history from any earlier session, exactly as this bug did. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using the exact known-broken case: `GET /api/verification/voucher_line_documents/82156` now correctly returns the Purchase Demand assignments originally made under session 382's `voucher_line_id=78735` (client_data_id 5662/5663) alongside session 393's own; `GET /api/data/preview` for client_data_id 5662 correctly returns `assigned_to_line_client_data_id: 5055`, matching the current line's own `client_data_id`; `get_procedure_checks`/`get_line_observations` for the same line return correctly (no dedup collisions in the live data); a nonexistent `voucher_line_id` still 404s on all three endpoints; a voucher line with no cross-session history still returns cleanly (single-row `IN (x)` behaves identically to `= x`). `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py routers/data.py` and `node --check static/verification.js` all pass. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so the actual browser click-through (Browse showing "Already linked here" and the item appearing in Linked Evidence for the exact same reopened line) was not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass. Phase 4 (confirmatory tick shortcut) not started.

- **Browse-Status vs Linked-Evidence disagreement fix (confirmed fix, `routers/verification.py` + `routers/data.py` + `static/verification.js` + `static/style.css`)**: `get_assignment_status_map(client_data_ids)` (routers/verification.py) previously returned only `voucher_line_id`/`voucher_id` per assigned client_data row — enough to say "this row is assigned to voucher line X" but not "under which Document slot." Since a voucher line's Supporting Documents modal has one tab per Document, and two Documents in the same Category can share the same `template_id`, a row assigned to line X under Document A would still show as `assigned_to_voucher_line === X` when browsing/searching from Document B's own tab on that same line — Browse's Status column (`buildProcedureResultRowHtml()`/`buildProcedureBrowseTableHtml()`) read this as "Already linked here," while the Linked Evidence table (`openProcedureModal()`, filters `voucher_line_documents` by BOTH `voucher_line_id` AND `document_id`) correctly never lists it there, since it belongs to a different tab. Fixed by having `get_assignment_status_map()` also return `document_id`/`document_name` (joined to `audit_rule_documents`), threaded through `routers/data.py`'s `attach_assignment_flags()` as two new additive `GET /api/data/preview` response fields (`assigned_to_document_id`/`assigned_to_document_name`) alongside the pre-existing `is_assigned`/`assigned_to_voucher_line`/`assigned_to_voucher_id`. Frontend: `buildProcedureResultRowHtml()` now takes an `activeDocId` param and only shows "Already linked here" when `assigned_to_document_id` matches the tab actually open; a same-line-different-document match instead shows `Linked to this voucher under "{document name}"` (new distinct wording, not the generic "Assigned to voucher X" used for a genuinely different voucher). `buildProcedureBrowseTableHtml()` similarly appends a muted `(under "{document name}")` note to the Voucher No. cell for the same same-line-different-document case (new `.procedure-browse-other-doc-note` CSS). `GET /api/verification/document_assignment_status` (the other consumer of `get_assignment_status_map()`) was left unchanged — it only reads the specific keys it already used, unaffected by the additive fields. Verified: `node --check static/verification.js` and `python -m py_compile routers/verification.py routers/data.py` all pass; confirmed `static/databank.js` (the other consumer of `GET /api/data/preview`) does not read `is_assigned`/`assigned_to_*` fields at all, so the additive fields are safe there. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session, so the actual Browse/search-dropdown wording for the same-line-different-document case was not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass.

- **Unassign supporting document lines (new, confirmed single-phase requirement) — `database.py` + `routers/verification.py` + `static/verification.js` + `static/style.css`**: **supersedes** the Phase 1 note above's claim that `UNIQUE(client_data_id)` is the enforcement mechanism and that a future unassign endpoint would just `DELETE` the row — that plan was replaced once it became clear a blanket table-level `UNIQUE(client_data_id)` would permanently block reassignment even after a soft-delete flag was added, since the old (now-inactive) row would still occupy the unique slot on that column. `voucher_line_documents` gained `status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active','unassigned'))` and `unassigned_at TIMESTAMP`; the table-level `UNIQUE(client_data_id)` was replaced by a **partial unique index** — `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_voucher_line_documents_active_client_data ON voucher_line_documents (client_data_id) WHERE status = 'active'` — so "once linked, never assignable again elsewhere" is still enforced at the DB level, but only while the link is active; an unassigned row can coexist with a fresh active link on the same `client_data_id`. **Required a real schema migration**, since SQLite can't drop/alter a table constraint in place and the live `test.db` already had 7 rows on the old shape — followed the exact rename → recreate-with-new-shape → copy rows across (as `status='active'`) → drop-old-table pattern already established by the `client_voucher_prefixes` 5-way category migration (same file, same `.bak-premigrate-<timestamp>` backup convention), gated on detecting the old shape (`PRAGMA table_info` has no `status` column) so it's a no-op on every subsequent startup. **Index-creation ordering gotcha, worth remembering for any future partial-index migration in this file**: the partial unique index's `CREATE INDEX` calls must run *after* the migration block resolves (whether it actually ran or the table was already on the new shape) — placing them directly after the initial `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (which is a no-op against an old-shape existing table) fails with `no such column: status` on any database still mid-upgrade, since that CREATE TABLE never touches the real existing table. New `POST /api/verification/unassign_document` (body `{assignment_id}` — the `voucher_line_documents.id`, already available client-side as `sel.id`) flips `status`/`unassigned_at`, never deletes the row (`linked_by`/`linked_at` stay intact as a provenance trail); 404s on an unknown id or one already unassigned. **Every existing query reading this table needed a `status = 'active'` filter added** — `assign_supporting_document`'s duplicate-link check, `get_voucher_line_documents` (list-by-line), and `get_assignment_status_map` (the shared helper both this router's `document_assignment_status` endpoint and `routers/data.py`'s `GET /api/data/preview` per-row assignment flags call) — an unassigned row must never be treated as a live link by any of them; a future new query against `voucher_line_documents` must apply the same filter. Frontend: `buildSelectedLinesTable()` (`static/verification.js`) gained a trailing icon-only column with a `.procedure-unlink-btn` ✕ button per row (`data-assignment-id`), wired in `renderProcedureModalPanel()` alongside the existing per-render checklist-checkbox wiring; `unassignSupportingDocument(uid, docId, assignmentId)` gates on a native `confirm()` (matching this app's established single-flat-destructive-action convention), POSTs the new endpoint, then removes the entry from `tabState.selections` and — if that was the tab's last selection — clears `docId` from `lineState.assignedDocIds` (un-filling the tab dot) before re-rendering the tab bar and panel; re-rendering reuses the exact same `getSelectedLinesSummary()`/`buildSelectedLinesTable()` code Phase 4 already built, so the running total and Matches/mismatch badge recalculate with no new logic. Observation text for the tab is deliberately left untouched by this action, per the confirmed brief. No changes to the search/browse assignment flow — a freed row becomes selectable again automatically, since it reads `is_assigned` sourced from the now-active-only `get_assignment_status_map()`. Verified end-to-end against the user's already-running `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted — the server's own auto-reload picked up the `database.py` edit and ran the migration against the real `test.db` automatically, preserving all 7 pre-existing rows as `status='active'`, confirmed via direct query before and after): unassigned a real link, confirmed it disappeared from `GET /voucher_line_documents/{id}` and `GET /document_assignment_status` reported the row free again, confirmed a duplicate-unassign attempt and an unknown `assignment_id` both 404 with distinct messages, then — the core scenario this migration exists to enable — reassigned the freed `client_data_id` to a *different* voucher line and confirmed it succeeded (`HTTP 200`, new row, old inactive row untouched). All test state reverted afterward (original row restored to `status='active'`, the transient reassignment row deleted) — confirmed via a follow-up `GET` that `test.db` matches its pre-test 7-row state exactly. `python -m py_compile database.py routers/verification.py` and `node --check static/verification.js` both pass; grepped and confirmed zero inline event handlers introduced. No Playwright/browser tool was available this session (same recurring gap as most phases in this app's history), so the actual ✕ click / confirm dialog / table-and-badge refresh in a real browser were not visually confirmed — worth a manual pass.

- **Voucher Supporting-Document Linking, Phase 6 of 6, FINAL (observation flow, `database.py` + `routers/verification.py` + `static/verification.js` + `static/style.css`)**: `voucher_line_observations` (one row per `voucher_line_id`+`document_id`, `UNIQUE` constraint, upserted in place — not an append-only history log) is the persistence layer for each Document tab's own observation text; its `synced` flag is what separates "saved on this tab" from "already rolled into the voucher line's own text field." **The actual roll-up chokepoint is `save_line_items()`** (`routers/verification.py`) — every Save/Next/Prev/Validate/Complete/Exit path in `static/verification.js` already funnels through it once per line (see `saveAllVoucherLines()`), so `sync_line_observations_to_voucher()` was hooked there rather than into `validate_transaction()`/`complete_transaction()` separately; a future phase adding a new "save this line" path must call `save_line_items()` (or explicitly re-invoke the sync helper) rather than bypassing it, or newly-saved observations will silently never reach `verification_details.observations`. **Append-only is enforced by construction, not by a flag check**: the sync helper always reads the field's current value first and concatenates onto it — a manually-typed prior note (if any auditor ever types directly into that column via some other future UI) is never at risk of being clobbered by this feature. **Every explicit save via `POST /api/verification/save_line_observation` unconditionally resets `synced=0`**, regardless of whether the text actually changed — this is deliberate (simpler and always-correct vs. diffing old/new text), so re-clicking Save with identical text is a harmless no-op re-append-preventing operation once synced, but re-triggers a real (if redundant) sync cycle. The auto-suggestion (`buildObservationSuggestion()`) is a **one-shot fill** gated by a client-only `suggestionApplied` flag on each tab's state (never persisted) — it fills an empty box at most once per modal-open lifetime and is never reapplied over auditor-edited or auditor-cleared text, including after an explicit Save (which also sets `suggestionApplied = true`, since a save is a final decision on that tab's text). `getSelectedLinesSummary()` was factored out of `buildSelectedLinesTable()` specifically so the mismatch computation backing both the Phase 4 badge and this phase's suggestion text can never drift apart — extend that one function, not two, if the mismatch rule ever changes.

- **Voucher Supporting-Document Linking, Phase 2 of 6 (search filter on Data Bank preview, `routers/data.py` + `routers/verification.py`)**: backend/query only, no UI. **Two of the brief's three "locked assumptions" turned out to already be satisfied by existing code, not new work**: `GET /api/data/preview`'s existing `search: Optional[str]` param already matches against any column value via `json_each(cd.row_data)` — exactly the "generic filter, not hardcoded to specific field names" requirement — so no new filter param was added; this is the first time `routers/data.py` imports from another router module, so if a future phase adds a reverse dependency (`routers/verification.py` needing something from `routers/data.py`), re-check for a cycle before adding it. `get_dataset_rows()` (the other, upload-scoped preview endpoint in the same file) was deliberately left untouched — a different browsing context with no client+template+date-range scoping, not what Phase 4's search UI will call. - **Voucher Supporting-Document Linking (new, confirmed 6-phase requirement) — Phase 1 of 6 (locking data model + assignment endpoints, `database.py` + `routers/verification.py`)**: backend/schema only, no UI changes. - 2026-07-24: **Voucher Supporting-Document Linking Phase 5 of 6 (audit procedures checklist, `database.py` + `routers/verification.py` + `static/verification.js` + `static/verification.html` + `static/style.css`)** done — renders each Document's already-configured auth roles (`audit_rule_document_auth_roles`, already flowing through `doc.auth_roles` on every document in `procedureModalState[uid].documents` via the shared `fetchAuditGuidanceData()` cache — no new fetch for the role list itself) as a tickable checklist beneath the Linked Evidence table in each tab, with no validation logic behind ticking (rules explicitly deferred to a future phase, per the confirmed brief). **New persistence, since nothing in Phase 1's schema could store this**: new `voucher_line_procedure_checks` table (`database.py`, added right after `voucher_line_documents`) — `UNIQUE(voucher_line_id, document_id, role_name)`, storing by `role_name` string (not a role id) to match how `get_document_auth_roles()` already exposes roles as plain strings with no id surfaced anywhere in this app; a role with no row is simply unchecked, same "missing = not set" convention already used elsewhere in this feature. Deliberately scoped to `(voucher_line_id, document_id, role_name)` rather than living on `voucher_line_documents` itself, since a checklist needs to exist even before any evidence row has been linked for that document (a document can have configured roles but zero linked evidence, and `voucher_line_documents` has no row until the first evidence assignment). Brand-new table, no prior data, plain `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, no `ALTER TABLE` upgrade block needed (same reasoning as `voucher_line_documents`); no `PRAGMA foreign_keys` enforcement, so the new endpoints validate every referenced id explicitly. ON CONFLICT(voucher_line_id, document_id, role_name) DO UPDATE SET is_checked=excluded.is_checked, checked_by=excluded.checked_by, checked_at=CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` so re-ticking the same role updates in place rather than duplicating a row; logs via the existing `log_audit()` helper. Frontend (`static/verification.js`): `getProcedureTabState()`'s default per-tab shape gained a `checklist: {}` field (keyed by `role_name` → `{is_checked, checked_by, checked_at}`); `openProcedureModal()` now also fetches `GET /api/verification/procedure_checks/{uid}` alongside the existing `voucher_line_documents/{uid}` fetch, same fail-soft-to-empty-array pattern (a fetch hiccup never blocks the modal opening), and seeds each tab's `checklist` from it in the same `documents.forEach(...)` loop that already seeds `selections` — re-synced fresh on every open, never just seeded once, so reopening the modal always reflects true server state. New `buildProcedureChecklist(uid, docId)` renders one checkbox per `doc.auth_roles` entry (checked per `tabState.checklist`), or a muted "No audit procedures configured for this document." message when a document has zero auth roles — same empty-state convention already used elsewhere in this modal. `renderProcedureModalPanel()` appends a new `.procedure-checklist-section` (heading "Audit Procedures" + `buildProcedureChecklist()` output) as a sibling directly after the existing `.procedure-selected-section`, and wires a `change` listener on each new checkbox the same "render → `querySelectorAll` → `addEventListener`" way the search input/browse button already are.
