## Row-level Blank-Field Rejection (8 entries)


- **Row-level blank-field rejection, Phase 4 of 4, FINAL (`static/upload.js`, `routers/import_export.py`, `database.py`)**: this completes the 4-phase requirement. `rejectedRowOverrides` (Phase 3) is now folded into the shared validate/import `payload` object as `force_include_rows: Array.from(rejectedRowOverrides)`, right next to the existing `excluded_rows` line in the `importBtn` click handler — rebuilt fresh on every click, so ticking an override either before or after the Validate call is picked up correctly on the actual Upload click; `performImport()` needed no change since it reuses that same payload object by reference. **Backend design decision**: rather than threading a "this row was force-included" marker through `compare_transactions()`'s own row_data reconstruction, the new `compute_data_quality_flag(row_data, critical_cols)` helper (routers/import_export.py, next to `find_critical_blank_reasons()`) derives the flag from the *final* row_data at insert/update time — if any of the 3 critical columns (Document ID/Amount/Date) is still blank there, the row is flagged `'incomplete'`. This is safe because normal validation already guarantees a non-force-included row can never reach insertion with a blank critical field, so a blank critical field surviving to this point is only possible via an explicit override — no new row-identity tracking was needed, and `compare_transactions()` itself was not touched. `validate_and_import()`'s row-exclusion step changed from unconditionally excluding every `rejected_rows` entry to only excluding those *not* in a new `force_include_set` (built from `ImportRequest.force_include_rows`, same row-number scheme as `excluded_rows`/`rejected_rows[].row_number`) — a force-included row stays in `rows` with its cell genuinely blank, no default ever inserted. All three places a row reaches `client_data` (the "new" and "changed" branches of the change-detection path, and the "first-time upload" insert loop) now compute and persist `data_quality_flag` via this same helper; the "unchanged"/"missing" branches are untouched (no row content changes there). New `client_data.data_quality_flag TEXT DEFAULT NULL` column (database.py) added via the same idempotent `CREATE TABLE` column + `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` upgrade-block pattern already used for `document_group_id`/`change_detection_status`/`session_type`. Response: a new `force_included_count` field sits alongside the existing `rejected_count`/`rejected_rows` on `validate_and_import()`'s success response — `rejected_count` keeps its pre-existing meaning (total rows identified as rejected this run, force-included or not), so the frontend derives "truly excluded" as `rejected_count - force_included_count` rather than the backend inventing a third overlapping field. `validate_only()` (the `/validate` preview endpoint) was deliberately left untouched — force-inclusion only matters at actual import time. `showImportSummary()` (static/upload.js) gained a new conditional "Row Exceptions" stat block (same visual pattern as the existing "Change Detection" block, rendered only when `rejected_count > 0`) showing "Rejected (excluded)" and "Imported with missing data" as two explicitly separate tiles — never lumped into one number, per the locked requirement. Verified end-to-end against the live `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using a disposable test client + a 4-row Gate Pass test file (one row each: fully valid, blank Quantity/Amount, blank Transaction Date, blank GP no/Document ID) with `force_include_rows` naming only the blank-Quantity row: `/api/upload/import` correctly inserted 2 rows (the valid one plus the force-included one), left the other two genuinely excluded, returned `rejected_count: 3`/`force_included_count: 1`, and a direct DB query confirmed the force-included row has `Quantity: null` (not a default) and `data_quality_flag: 'incomplete'`, while the fully-valid row has `data_quality_flag: null`. Test client, its `client_data` row, and the uploaded file were deleted afterward. `python -m py_compile`/`node --check` both pass. **Surfacing `data_quality_flag` in Data Bank (icon + All/Complete/Incomplete filter dropdown) is a separate, not-yet-started follow-up phase** — this phase only persists and reports the flag at import time.

- **Row-level blank-field rejection, Phase 3 of 4 (exceptions list UI, `static/upload.html` + `static/upload.js` only)**: `rejectedRowsData` (`Map<excelRowNumber, reasons[]>`) and `rejectedRowOverrides` (`Set<excelRowNumber>`) are the frontend's mirror of a validate/import response's `rejected_rows` field (Phase 2, above) — populated/redrawn by `setRejectedRows(rejectedRowsList)`/`renderRejectedRowsList()`, rendered into `#rowRejectionContainer` (a panel deliberately separate from `#rowExclusionContainer`'s grid — different container, different CSS namespace `.row-rejection-*`, not reusing `.row-flagged`/`.row-validation-failed`/`.row-excluded`). `setRejectedRows()` is called from both places a validate/import response is handled (the `importBtn` click handler's validate branch, `performImport()`'s response handler) exactly the way `setValidationFailedRows()` already is — extend that same pair of call sites, not a new one, if a future phase adds another response-handling path. `rejectedRowOverrides` is **state only as of Phase 3** — nothing yet reads it when building the validate/import payload; Phase 4 is expected to fold `Array.from(rejectedRowOverrides)` into the request payload (mirroring how `excludedRowNumbers` already is) and must also decide what happens to `excludedRowNumbers`/the row-selection grid's own checkbox for a row that's both rejected and overridden. The three reset points (`renderRowExclusionGrid()`, `resetRowExclusionSelections()`, `resetUpload()`) that already clear `validationFailedRows` now also clear `rejectedRowsData`/`rejectedRowOverrides` in lockstep — keep all three in sync if any of these reset points are ever restructured.

- **Row-level blank-field rejection (Phase 2 of 4, `routers/import_export.py`)**: `validate_only()`/`validate_and_import()` no longer flag *any* blank mapped cell as a blocking `"required"` error — only a blank **Document ID**, **Amount**, or **Date** now causes a row-level rejection; a blank value in any other mapped column imports fine (as `None`), same as any other value. Since this schema has no explicit "Document ID"/"Amount"/"Date" column names, the 3 critical roles are identified positionally by new `get_critical_field_columns(template_cols)`: Document ID = the first template column by `sort_order` (same rule `get_document_group_id()` already uses), Amount = the first `Numeric`-typed column, Date = the first `Date`-typed column (both matching `extract_columns_from_row()`'s existing "take first numeric"/"take first date" rules) — a role with no matching column in a given template is simply skipped. New `find_critical_blank_reasons(row, critical_cols, mapping_dict)` (same file, same "blank" test as `apply_edited_cell_values()`) computes per-row rejection reasons, reported in a new, distinct `rejected_rows` field on both endpoints' responses — kept separate from `errors`/`validation_errors`, which now only ever contain genuine data-type mismatches (bad Numeric/Date *format* on a non-blank value) and still block the entire `/api/upload/import` call exactly as before. Blank-critical-field rejections do **not** block the whole import: in `validate_and_import()`, rejected rows are excluded from insertion (reusing the existing `filter_excluded_rows()` helper with the rejected rows' own row numbers — no new filtering logic needed) while every other row in the same file still imports normally. A row can independently appear in both `errors` and `rejected_rows` (e.g. a blank Date in one column plus a bad Numeric format in another) — if `errors` is non-empty the whole import still blocks regardless of `rejected_rows`. Phase 3 (exceptions list UI + override toggle) and Phase 4 (wire overrides through + data quality flag + import summary) are not started — do not assume an override mechanism exists yet; today a critical-field-blank row is unconditionally excluded, no way to force-include it.

## Upload Reliability & Blank-Field Handling (4 entries)


- 2026-07-21: Upload reliability & blank-field handling Phase 2 of 4 (stop the `/api/upload/validate` 500, `routers/import_export.py` only) done — root cause found via the now-working Error Dashboard (Phase 1): ERR-UNK-001 `Object of type time is not JSON serializable`, logged repeatedly against Upload. A Date-typed column's cell (most likely a trailing totals/subtotal row's oddly-formatted Date cell) can come back from pandas as a bare `datetime.time`, which the old `pd.isna()`/`isinstance(value, datetime)` pattern didn't catch (neither flags it), so it fell through into a row_data dict untouched and crashed the first `json.dumps()` call to see it, uncaught. Fixed at the source with a new shared `json_safe_cell_value()` helper (see new Convention note above) used by all four places in this file that build a row_data dict from a raw Excel row; also wrapped `validate_only()`'s and `validate_and_import()`'s per-row validation loops in `try/except`, so any row-level parsing failure — this one or an unforeseen future one — becomes a graceful `parse_error` validation entry for that row instead of crashing the whole request. `check_duplicates()` still has the old unfixed pattern (out of this phase's confirmed scope, flagged for later). Verified: `python -m py_compile` passes; confirmed via `curl` against the user's already-running dev server (port 5000, checked via `netstat` first, not restarted) that it auto-reloaded cleanly and `/api/clients` still responds 200. No Playwright/browser tool available this session, so an actual re-upload of the file that previously 500'd was not click-through confirmed — worth a manual pass. Next: Phase 3 (inline editing for blank cells in the Row Selection/Preview grid).

## Client Data Availability & Coverage Redesign (10 entries)


- **Client Data Availability & Coverage Redesign Phase 3 of 6 (Availability calendar backend, `routers/data.py` only)**: new `GET /api/data/availability/calendar` (`client_id`, one-or-more `template_ids`, `year`, `month`) returns, for each requested template, a per-day status array covering the full month: `present` (client_data exists for that template/date — highest priority, so real data on a Sunday/holiday still counts as present), `sunday` (hardcoded day-of-week check via `datetime(...).strftime('%w') == '0'`, same convention as this file's existing SQL-side `strftime('%w', ...) = '0'` checks — Sundays are never stored in the `holidays` table, per Phase 1's design), `holiday` (resolved via new `_resolve_holidays_for_month(year, month)`, which builds a `{date_str: label}` lookup from the Phase 1 `holidays` table — non-repeating holidays kept only if their stored date falls in the requested year/month; `repeats_yearly` holidays have their month/day projected onto the requested year, so a holiday configured in any past year resolves correctly going forward), or `missing` (none of the above). Each template's response also carries `present_count`/`missing_count`/`sunday_count`/`holiday_count` (always summing to the number of days in the month) so Phase 4's calendar UI doesn't need to re-derive them client-side. This is deliberately a new, additive endpoint, not a modification of the existing `GET /api/data/availability` (which answers a coarser "any data in this date range" question for the still-in-use date-picker/buttons UI) — that endpoint, `database.py`, and `routers/settings.py` were all left completely untouched; holidays are read-only from this endpoint's perspective. Backend-only per the confirmed brief — no frontend changes yet (Phase 4 is the template multi-select + calendar UI that will consume this). Verified end-to-end against the live `--reload` dev server (port 5000, `netstat`-checked first, not restarted) using real ACME data (client 1, July 2026): template 1 (Transaction Report, real data 07-01 to 07-06) correctly returned `present_count: 5` (07-05 is a Sunday, so it's `sunday` not `present`) / `missing_count: 22` / `sunday_count: 4` / `holiday_count: 0`, summing to 31; template 2 (Purchase Demand, no data) correctly returned all-missing/Sunday with `present_count: 0`; temporarily added one one-off holiday (07-14) and one `repeats_yearly` holiday (stored as 2025-07-21) via the existing Phase 1 API and confirmed both resolved correctly as `holiday`-status days for July **2026** (the repeating one correctly projected forward a year) with counts still summing to 31; confirmed 404 on an inactive/nonexistent client or template (naming the specific bad template id) and a clean 422 on `month=13`; confirmed `GET /api/data/availability` and `GET /api/data/preview` are unaffected (regression spot-check). Both test holidays deleted afterward. `python -m py_compile routers/data.py` passes.

Untracked via `git rm --cached` — 41 files removed from tracking, zero removed from disk (`.db`/`.bak`/`uploads/*.xlsx`/`__pycache__`/logs). Deliberately no history rewrite — scoped to `main` only, existing bulk stays until a separate decision.

Plain `git gc` compacted `.git` 513 MB → 28 MB with zero commit-hash changes across all 424 commits/4 branches, confirmed via `git fsck` and unchanged upstream tracking.

No backend change — confirmed by reading `save_line_items()` (`routers/verification.py`) directly: it already calls `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()` (default live/persisting) on every save and returns the fresh result in its response; the staleness was entirely a client-side caching gap, not a stale server value. ## Audit Workbook Module (28 entries)


- 2026-08-12: **Audit Workbook (new, confirmed 5-phase requirement) — Phase 1 of 5 (backend, `routers/verification.py` only)** done. New read-only `GET /api/verification/session/{session_id}/audit_workbook` returns one row per voucher (not per line) — `voucher_no`/`date`/`description`/`amount`/`status` — for a session, feeding a later "Audit Workbook" list view distinct from the existing Cashbook selection screen. ## Generic Voucher-Level Checks (6 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-6 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/verification.html`/`.js`, `static/style.css`)**: replaced the hardcoded Prepared/Checked/Approved-By voucher-level approval concept with a data-driven, extensible list of global checks. Phase 1: schema — `audit_rule_voucher_checks` (name/sort_order/is_active), `audit_rule_voucher_check_auth_roles` (per-check role gating, modelled on `audit_rule_document_auth_roles`), `voucher_check_status` (per-voucher tick + inline performed-by name, keyed by `client_id`+`transaction_ref` — deliberately not `session_id`+`transaction_ref`, to avoid the sibling-session orphaning bug already fixed three times elsewhere in this module, since reopening a cashbook creates a fresh `verification_sessions` row every time). The old `voucher_approvals` table was left in place, untouched, not dropped/migrated. Phase 2: full soft-delete/restore CRUD in routers/audit_rules.py (`GET/POST /api/audit-rules/voucher-checks`, `GET/PUT .../{id}`, `DELETE .../{id}` + `POST .../{id}/restore`, `POST .../reorder`), mirroring Documents' 6-endpoint pattern; `auth_roles` originally an embedded `List[str]`, delete-then-reinsert on save. Phase 3: a 5th Audit Rules rail entity, ordered by `sort_order` (not alphabetical) with Sortable.js drag-to-reorder POSTing live to the reorder endpoint. Phase 4: `GET /api/verification/voucher_checks` / `POST /api/verification/save_voucher_check` (upsert, no role-based access enforcement — `auth_roles` are informational only, matching the existing Audit Procedures checklist convention) — purely additive alongside the still-live `voucher_approvals` gate, cutover deferred to Phase 5. Phase 5: a persistent voucher-level checks bar (`#procedureVoucherChecksBar`) above the Supporting Documents modal's document rail; `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()`'s voucher-level gate cut over from `voucher_approvals` to "every active check ticked" in `voucher_check_status`; the old `GET/POST /api/verification/voucher_approval`/`save_voucher_approval` endpoints were **deleted** (the `voucher_approvals` table itself stays in the schema, unread/unwritten); the old Voucher Line tab's Prepared/Checked/Approved-By fields were removed. Phase 6: styling — indigo-tinted accent card, compact white pills, a shared custom tick-icon rule applied to both this bar and the per-document Audit Procedures checklist.

- **Voucher-level Checks simplified to name-only + 3-state model (new, confirmed 4-phase follow-up requirement, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `database.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/verification.js`/`.html`, `static/style.css`)**: Phase 1 — removed the Authorisation Roles field from Voucher-level Checks entirely (`VoucherCheckCreate`/`VoucherCheckUpdate` no longer accept `auth_roles`; `audit_rule_voucher_check_auth_roles` left in place, unread/unwritten). Phase 2 — `voucher_check_status` gained `state` (`'untouched'|'done'|'not_done'`, backfilled once from the old boolean `ticked`) and `flagged_in_observations` (written only by a new `POST /api/verification/verify_voucher_checks`, never by an ordinary tick); `GET/POST voucher_checks`/`save_voucher_check` now read/write `state` instead of `ticked`/`performed_by_name`; the new `verify_voucher_checks` endpoint 400s if any active check is still `untouched`, otherwise flags every `not_done` check and re-syncs the voucher's Observations. Phase 3 — the bar's checkboxes became tick/cross toggle-pill pairs; a warning line names any check currently `not_done`; a new voucher-scoped "✅ Verify & Next/Close" footer button (`.btn-verify`) replaced the old per-line Next button (← Back stays line-scoped, a locked scope decision). Phase 4 — a subsequent fix made "✅ Verify & Next" step through unverified lines (`cleared_status !== 'Cleared'` and a Category is assigned) within the same voucher before advancing to the next voucher, forward-only, never wrapping.

## Validation Rules Module (7 phases + Account Head recommendation + Category Cleared Requirements summary)

- **Full build, Phases 1-7 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/verification.js`/`.html`, `static/style.css`)**: adds a Cleared-vs-Query status engine per voucher line. Phase 1 schema: `approval_required` on `audit_rule_category_documents` (**since hard-removed, see the follow-up fix below**), `matrix_version` on `audit_rule_categories` (bumped whenever a Category's document/approval requirements change), `signature_specimens` (client_id+document_id+role_name → expected_signatory_name), `signature_exception` on `voucher_line_documents` (default OK, UI control since hidden — see Conventions note), `cleared_status`/`matrix_version_applied` on `verification_details`. Addendum: `voucher_approvals` (client_id+transaction_ref → prepared_by/checked_by/approved_by) — **since superseded and left dead by Generic Voucher-Level Checks Phase 5** (its endpoints deleted, table unread/unwritten). Phase 2 (Audit Rules backend): approval-toggle endpoint + `matrix_version` bump logic; Signature Specimens 5-endpoint CRUD. Phase 3 (Audit Rules frontend): approval checkboxes, matrix-version display, Signature Specimens as a standalone rail entity (later reworked, see "Signature Specimens Soft-Delete Conversion"). Phase 4 (Verification backend): `compute_and_persist_cleared_status(voucher_line_id)` — four AND'ed checks (later expanded, see below): required documents present (`get_category_documents()`), each `approval_required` document has an approver role ticked (**since removed**), `voucher_approvals` complete (**since replaced by the Generic Voucher-Level Checks gate**), no `signature_exception` flagged; called from `save_line_items()`. Phase 5 (Verification frontend): the Cleared/Query badge (`.voucher-line-cleared-badge-slot`, an independent sibling of the validation-status pill so `validateTransaction()`'s innerHTML rewrite can't wipe it), the Sig. Exc. checkbox (**UI since hidden**), the synthetic Voucher Line tab (**since replaced**, see Generic Voucher-Level Checks). Phase 6 (backend): `GET /api/verification/suggest-account-head` — fuzzy-matches (rapidfuzz `WRatio`) a line's description against the client's latest parsed Trial Balance leaf accounts, Category-alignment bonus, keyword-match reason, score band, top 2 results above `ACCOUNT_HEAD_MATCH_THRESHOLD=55`. Phase 7 (frontend): the Account Head Recommendation card in the Voucher Line tab (search-select over `latestTbAccountsCache`, "Use" button, no-match note via a reserved sentinel `document_id=-1` reusing the observation-sync machinery) — later repositioned above Voucher Approval with a TB search-select replacing free text (confirmed fix, same day).

- **Hard-remove Category "Approved" checkbox (confirmed requirement, `database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `static/audit_rules.js`, `routers/verification.py`)**: approval is now decided entirely at Document level via the "Approved by" role's Required Authority field (below), not per-Category — `audit_rule_category_documents.approval_required` was hard-removed via a full table rebuild (rename→recreate→copy→drop, same convention as the `comparison_type` CHECK-expansion), keeping only `is_required`. `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()`'s old approval-required check was stripped from `all_ok` entirely (no replacement landed yet at the time).

- **Document-level Approved-by authority gate (new, confirmed requirement, `routers/audit_rules.py` + `routers/verification.py`)**: the real replacement for the removed Category-level approval check — for every Category-required Document whose "Approved by"-type role has a Required Authority set, `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()` (check #6) now requires an ACTIVE Signature Specimen on file for that client+document+role whose `authority` matches (case/whitespace-insensitive). This is an **existence check** ("is a qualified signatory on file"), not a per-voucher recorded-signer match — no field anywhere records who actually signed a specific voucher's document, confirmed before designing.

- **Category "Cleared Requirements" summary (new, confirmed requirement, 3 phases, `routers/audit_rules.py` + `static/audit_rules.js` + `static/style.css`)**: read-only `GET /api/audit-rules/categories/{category_id}/cleared-requirements` reports, with no manual toggles, what a Category actually requires — `voucher_level_checks_required`/`account_head_required` always true (global gates), `cross_checks_required` true only if ≥1 active attached Cross-check, `required_documents` filtered to `is_required=1` — same data the real gate reads, not re-derived. Rendered as a "What Cleared Requires" plain-language bullet subsection at the top of each Category's "⚠️ Validation Rules" box.

## Automated Cross-Document Validation Engine (10 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-10 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/verification.js`, `static/style.css`)**: lets a Cross-check's configured document chain be evaluated against real linked evidence, not just displayed as guidance text. Phase 1 schema: `is_required` on `audit_rule_category_documents`; `comparison_type` CHECK expanded to 6 values (added `'Must be equal'`/`'May be less, never more'`); `compare_to_voucher_line` on `audit_rule_cross_checks`. Phase 2: `get_document_field_value(client_data_id, field_name)` (routers/verification.py) resolves a named field from linked evidence's `row_data`, validated against the Document's real template columns — dead code until Phase 6 wires it in. Phase 3: the Cross-checks "Field to Compare" dropdown now visibly flags (⚠, amber) a saved value that no longer matches any current option, instead of silently clearing it. Phase 4: a "Required" checkbox alongside the existing "Approved" checkbox on a Category's attached-Documents list, backed by `is_required`; `PUT .../categories/{id}/documents/{doc_id}/required`. Phase 5: 2 new comparison types wired into the config UI plus a "compare to voucher line amount" checkbox (anchor = the last document in chain order, resolved live, never manually picked). Phase 6: `evaluate_cross_checks_for_line(voucher_line_id, category_id)` — chain-aware evaluator: anchor = last **linked** document walked backwards; `May be less, never more` is directional (later ≤ earlier; strictly less = soft "shortfall", strictly more = hard "fail"); `Within tolerance %` uses a placeholder `CROSS_CHECK_DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_PCT=5.0` (no per-rule column exists yet); a Document with multiple linked evidence rows sums the field. Phase 7: wired into `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()` as check #5 — only a `"fail"` blocks Cleared, `"shortfall"`/`"not_evaluated"` do not. Phase 8: `_write_shortfall_observations()` auto-logs a shortfall as a reserved-sentinel observation (`CROSS_CHECK_SHORTFALL_DOC_ID_BASE = -1000` range, one sentinel per Cross-check) that self-clears once the shortfall resolves. Phase 9: `GET /api/verification/cross_check_results/{voucher_line_id}` exposes the evaluator read-only; the Supporting Documents modal's Data Table segment renders a per-document pass/fail/shortfall/not-evaluated rollup with click-to-expand chain detail. Phase 10/FINAL: a live document-chain preview on the Category detail screen — one row of connected pills per attached Cross-check, dimmed pill for a not-required document, "(anchor)" tag on the last pill.

- **"Field to Compare" dropdown / "Amount"→"Rate" — 2 confirmed data-only fixes (no code changes, `static/audit_rules.js` design already correct)**: the dropdown appeared stuck on "Add a document first" because none of the 7 active Documents actually had `cross_check_fields` configured (all prior test rows were soft-deleted) — fixed by setting real `cross_check_fields` (Quantity/Amount, later also Rate) on the 5 template-linked Documents via the existing API, plus a small empty-state message fix distinguishing "no documents added" from "no field common to all selected documents". A follow-up rename request ("Amount"→"Rate") was investigated and **deferred** — none of the 3 templates has a real "Rate" column at the time (Rate as a derived value came later via the Rate-Derivation Requirement).

## Physical Bill Evidence Type (8 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-8 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/verification.js`/`.html`, `static/style.css`)**: lets a Category require a manually-keyed "Physical Bill" (Bill No/Date/Amount/Vendor name) instead of a Data Bank template-linked Document. Phase 1 schema: `evidence_type` on `audit_rule_categories` (`'billable'`/`'non_billable'`, nullable with no default — every existing Category needs manual classification before the gate activates), `document_type` on `audit_rule_documents` (`'linked_template'`/`'physical_bill'`, defaulted `'linked_template'` on the ALTER), `voucher_line_physical_bills` (`voucher_line_id`+`document_id` → `bill_no`/`bill_date`/`amount`/`vendor_name`, `UNIQUE(voucher_line_id, document_id)` — carries `document_id` since a Billable Category can attach more than one Physical Bill Document). Phase 2: Documents CRUD supports `document_type`, defaulting to `linked_template` when omitted (a stricter reject was considered and rejected, since the frontend didn't send the field until Phase 4); `apply_document_type_constraints()` forces a `physical_bill`'s `template_id`/`cross_check_fields` empty but leaves `auth_roles` alone (load-bearing at the time — a template-less Document was still satisfied via role ticks until Phase 6 intercepted it). Phase 3: Categories CRUD requires `evidence_type` on both create **and** update (a validator, not a resolver — the strictness asymmetry with Phase 2 is deliberate, since this field drives the gate). Phase 4: Audit Rules frontend pickers for both fields, forced choice with no default, a native `confirm()` guard when switching an existing Document away from `linked_template`. Phase 5: `POST /api/verification/save_physical_bill` (upsert) / `GET .../physical_bills/{voucher_line_id}` (sibling-session-resolved batch read) — plain CRUD, no matching logic yet. Phase 6: wired into `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()`'s check #1 — intercepts `document_type == 'physical_bill'` **before** the template/no-template branches (closing the exact trap Phase 2/3 flagged); `_physical_bill_satisfied()` requires Bill No/Date/Vendor non-blank AND Amount exactly matching `client_data.extract_amount` (epsilon 0.005) — any one gap fails the whole document. Phase 7: the Supporting Documents modal's Physical Bill tab — a dedicated 4-field form (no Audit Procedures segment, since roles no longer gate this doc type), live green ✓ tick beside Amount on an exact match. Phase 8/FINAL: confirmed the reason-popover/Validate-panel's existing generic gate-detail rendering already covers physical-bill outstanding text with no code change needed. **Real blocker found and fixed along the way**: `client_data.extract_amount` was NULL on every real row (see "Rate-Derivation Requirement" for the root cause/fix/backfill) — until that fix, this entire gate was untestable against real data.

- **"Populate Physical Bill from GRN/ERP Vendor Bill" — see the dedicated heading below** (a separate, later 4-phase requirement building on this one).

## Signature Specimens Soft-Delete Conversion (4 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-4 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`)**: converts hard-delete to soft-delete for a Document's signatory records. Phase 1: `signature_specimens` gained `is_active INTEGER DEFAULT 1`; `DELETE .../{id}` now soft-deletes (404 if already inactive), `POST .../{id}/restore` added, plus a separate low-visibility `DELETE .../{id}/hard-delete` for genuine data-entry corrections. Phase 2: the old table-level `UNIQUE(client_id, document_id, role_name)` (which blocked reusing a deactivated slot) was removed via a schema-driven rebuild, replaced by `validate_no_duplicate_active_signatory()` — blocks only a literal duplicate ACTIVE entry for the *same person* (case-insensitive name match); multiple different people can be concurrently active for the same role. Phase 3: confirmed no-op — Verification's signature check (`signature_exception`) is a manual auditor toggle, never queries `signature_specimens` at all. Phase 4/FINAL: moved out of its own standalone rail entity into each Document's own detail view — a per-Role grouped person list with Deactivate/Reactivate + a separate low-visibility hard-delete link; inactive people stay visible, greyed/struck-through, never hidden (a historical record).

- **Authority field on Signature Specimens (new, confirmed requirement, `database.py` + `routers/audit_rules.py` + `static/audit_rules.js` + `static/style.css`)**: `signature_specimens` gained a nullable `authority TEXT`, unconditional on every specimen — the field the Document-level Approved-by authority gate (Validation Rules Module) matches against.

## ID-based Cross-check-eligible Fields (4 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-4 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/columns.html`/`.js`)**: moves a Document's "Cross-check-eligible Fields" toward referencing real `master_columns` IDs, without breaking the existing free-text `cross_check_fields: List[str]` contract. Phase 1: `audit_rule_document_fields` gained a nullable `master_column_id INTEGER`, best-effort backfilled by name-matching each field against its Document's template's mapped columns; `resolve_field_name_to_master_column_id()` (routers/audit_rules.py) also resolves on every future save. Phase 2: the free-text chip input on the Documents detail form became a `<select>` scoped to the Document's linked template's real columns, with an amber-flagged chip for any entry that wouldn't resolve. Phase 3: narrowed a reported "stays empty" bug to a real but different gap — a Document with zero configured fields showed the generic "no common field" message instead of naming the actual cause; fixed the message only. Phase 4/FINAL: `GET /api/columns/{column_id}/usage` — a read-only rename/edit dependency preview (`documents_count`/`cross_checks_count`/`templates_count`) shown in the Add/Edit Column modal.

- **Full build, Phases 1-3 (`static/audit_rules.js` + `static/style.css`)**: groups a Category's validation-related config into one visually distinct box. Phase 2: the Voucher-level Checks rail entity's list+detail panels were also reparented into this box (**later reverted, see below**). - **Full build, Phases 1-4 (`database.py`, `routers/audit_rules.py`, `static/audit_rules.html`/`.js`, `static/verification.js`)**: a per-Document flag gating a line's Supporting Documents completion on the (then-current) Voucher Line approval fields being filled. Phase 1: `audit_rule_documents.transaction_level_approval INTEGER DEFAULT 0`. Phase 2: `PUT /api/audit-rules/documents/{id}/transaction-level-approval`. Phase 3: a checkbox on the Documents detail form, disabled until the Document is saved. ## Inactive Items Excluded From Selection Contexts (5 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-5 (`routers/audit_rules.py`, `routers/verification.py`, `routers/trial_balance.py`, `static/audit_rules.js`)**: an inactive (soft-deleted) Document/Cross-check/Category must not appear as a *pickable* option anywhere it's actually selected during live audit work, while staying visible (greyed) in admin/historical displays. Phase 1: `get_category_guidance_documents()`/`get_category_guidance_cross_checks()` (feed Verification's live procedure-modal tabs) gained `is_active` filters — the one real gap found. Phase 2: confirmed no-op — Audit Rules' own Category-builder pickers already defaulted `include_inactive=false`. Phase 3: the Supporting Documents modal now synthesizes a locked, dimmed tab (`__inactive: true`) for a Document that already has linked evidence/ticks/an observation but was since deactivated — frozen/read-only, never gates completion, evidence stays unassignable but existing links stay visible and unassign still works. Phase 4: `get_category_for_account()` (Verification's Type auto-fill) and the Trial Balance smart-fill cascade both stopped over-filtering an inactive-but-assigned Category out of a read-only display; the Assign Categories dropdown gained a synthetic "(inactive)" option so a frozen assignment doesn't silently show "-- Not assigned --". Phase 5/FINAL: `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()`'s check #1 (`required_doc_ids`) and the Document-level Approved-by authority gate's document lookup both gained `is_active` filters — without these, a Document deactivated after being attached-but-never-linked could permanently block Cleared with no way to ever satisfy it.

## Shared Procedure Modal Extraction (procedure_modal.js)

- **Full build, 3 phases (`static/verification.js`/`.html`, new `static/procedure_modal.js`, `static/audit_workbook.js`/`.html`, `routers/verification.py`)**: extracts the entire `#procedureModal`/`#procedureBrowseModal`/`#voucherVerifyToast` subsystem out of `verification.js` into a shared, self-installing classic `<script>` so it can be reused by a second host page without duplicating ~3,500 lines. Phase 1 (relocation only): pure move via a scripted line-range extraction (byte-for-byte fidelity, verified via `node --check` + a top-level-identifier collision scan), zero behavior change — `verification.js` shrank 7373→3947 lines. Phase 1b (adapter refactor): replaced bare shared-global-scope reliance (~20 identifiers) with an explicit `hostAdapter` object passed into `openProcedureModal(uid, initialDocId, adapter)`; functions are plain property refs, live/reassignable state (`currentVoucherId`, `voucherLineState`, etc.) are `get` accessor properties so the adapter's view stays live rather than a stale snapshot; `verification.js` gained `buildProcedureModalAdapter()`, called at its 4 real `openProcedureModal()` sites. Phase 2 (Audit Workbook wiring): `static/audit_workbook.js` built its own lean `buildAuditWorkbookAdapter(voucherGroup)` — a direct-to-backend equivalent of `saveLineItems()`, not a reuse of Verification's — required `GET .../audit_workbook` to additionally surface each line's resolved Category *name* and the session's `client_id` (both genuinely needed by the modal, purely additive to the endpoint).

## Supporting Documents Modal Redesign (6 phases)

- **Full build, Phases 1-6 (`routers/audit_rules.py`, `static/verification.js`/`.html`, `static/style.css`)**: reworks `#procedureModal`'s visual structure. Phase 1: the top tab bar became a left-side vertical document rail (`.procedure-doc-rail`), auto-opening the first incomplete document by default (falling back to the first document if all are complete); a shared `isProcedureDocumentComplete(uid, doc)` helper replaced an inline per-branch completion check. Phase 2: each document panel's Data Table / Audit Procedures / Observation zones wrapped in a tinted `.procedure-segment` card (blue/amber/violet headers). Phase 3: removed the per-tab "💾 Save Observation" button — observations now flush automatically at the existing `saveLineItems()` chokepoint and on modal close, via a new `flushProcedureObservations(uid)`. Phase 4: the Linked Evidence table's dynamic (union-of-`row_data`-keys) column set was tried as a fixed Description/Quantity/Rate/Amount set, then reverted back to a per-template dynamic set (`fetchTemplateColumns()`, ordered by the template's real `sort_order`) once real template schemas turned out to have no Description/Rate columns at all. Phase 5: confirmed/fixed a caching bug — `fetchAuditGuidanceData()` was serving a stale cached Category's Documents/roles across a modal reopen; a new `forceRefresh` param bypasses the cache specifically on `openProcedureModal()`. Phase 6/FINAL: a **Risk** column on the main voucher table (between Supporting and Observations) — `computeLineRiskData()` takes the highest `risk_rating` among the line's Category's Documents (unrated ignored), rendered read-only with a hover tooltip listing each Document's `auth_roles`.

## Rate-Derivation Requirement (9 phases + backfill + follow-up fixes)

- **Full build, Phases 1-9 (`database.py`, `routers/settings.py`, `routers/templates.py`, `routers/import_export.py`)**: a 9-phase requirement letting Purchase Order/Store Receiving/Vendor Bill either import a Rate column as-is or derive it as Amount ÷ Quantity at import time. Phase 1: new `rate_precision` `app_settings` seed key (0/2/4 decimals), independent of `decimal_precision`, exposed automatically via the existing generic settings routes. Phase 2: `rate_precision` added to `static/settings.js`'s `SETTINGS_DEF`, same pattern as `decimal_precision`, no HTML change needed. Phase 3: `master_columns` gained a nullable `notes TEXT` ("Notes / Interpretation") field, editable in both the canonical Add/Edit Column modal and the Templates page's Quick Add modal. Phase 4: that Notes text surfaces as an "ℹ️" tooltip icon wherever a column is picked/listed in Template setup (search results, Selected Columns, Preview modal) — since `GET /api/templates` doesn't carry `notes` on its `columns[]`, the frontend cross-references the already-loaded `allMasterColumns` cache by id instead of extending that endpoint. Phase 5: `templates` gained a nullable `rate_source TEXT` (`'imported'`/`'derived'`), restricted server-side via `resolve_rate_source()` (routers/templates.py) to Purchase Order/Store Receiving/Vendor Bill only (matched case-insensitively) — any other template's value is always forced `NULL` regardless of payload, and an eligible template with no explicit value defaults to `'imported'` (the safe default). Phase 5a: a "Rate Source" dropdown in the Template setup modal, shown only when the typed Template Name matches an eligible template. Phase 6: import-time derivation lives in `get_rate_precision()`/`find_named_column()`/`apply_rate_derivation(row_data, template_cols, rate_source, rate_precision)` (routers/import_export.py) — computes `row_data['Rate']` as Amount ÷ Quantity when `rate_source='derived'` (Qty missing/blank/0 leaves Rate as `None`, a normal outcome, never an error) or rounds an already-imported Rate column when `rate_source='imported'`; called in `compare_transactions()`'s incoming-row loop and `validate_and_import()`'s first-time-upload branch — deliberately *before* change-detection's diff runs, since applying it after would make every re-upload of an already-imported row look artificially "changed" (a stored row already has a Rate value; a freshly-rebuilt comparison row without one injected first would never match). `validate_only()` is untouched (import-only scope). Phase 7: `client_data` gained a nullable `rate_source TEXT` — a per-row audit trail of how *that row's* Rate was actually obtained, distinct from `templates.rate_source` (the config knob, which can change later while historic rows must still show what was used at the time); set at all 3 write points (first-time insert, re-upload new-document insert, re-upload changed-row update) from the already-resolved `rate_source` variable, never re-derived; recorded even when Rate itself is null (Qty=0 case) — provenance of the attempt, not the result. A changed-row re-upload re-stamps `rate_source` to whatever's currently effective. Phase 8: Rate was retroactively attached as a real `master_columns`/`template_column_mappings` row on all 3 eligible templates (positioned between Quantity and Amount) via an idempotent `init_db()` block — needed since nothing had ever declared Rate as a formal template column despite Phases 6-7 already writing/stamping it. Phase 9: standalone `backfill_rate.py` (dry-run by default, `--run` to write) derives Rate for every eligible historical row still missing it, reusing `get_rate_precision()`/`find_named_column()`/`apply_rate_derivation()`'s exact logic; run for real against production data 2026-08-01 (11 rows backfilled: 2 PO, 3 Store Receiving, 6 Vendor Bill). Phase 10/FINAL: UI provenance indicator — `GET /api/data/preview` and `get_voucher_line_documents()` (routers/verification.py) both now return `rate_source` per row; `static/databank.js`'s `renderPreviewRows()` and `static/verification.js`'s `buildSelectedLinesTable()` render a 📥 (imported) / 🧮 (derived) icon next to a non-blank Rate cell.

- **Rate column display/storage order fix (confirmed fix, `routers/import_export.py` + `static/databank.js` + `static/verification.js` + `static/template-viewer.js`)**: the backfill surfaced that Rate rendered last in the Data Bank preview instead of between Quantity and Amount — for all 3 eligible templates Rate is `rate_source='derived'` (no native Excel column), so `apply_rate_derivation()` appends it to `row_data` *after* the initial column-assembly loop, and since dict/JSON insertion order is preserved, every import (not just the backfill) stored Rate last in the JSON. Purely cosmetic — every backend consumer reads `row_data` by field name, never by position. Fixed with new `reorder_row_data_by_template(row_data, template_cols)`, called right after both `apply_rate_derivation()` call sites so all future imports store fields in the template's real `sort_order`. Frontend: 4 render points that built column order from `Object.keys(row_data)` now read from the template's own `sort_order`-ordered `columns[]` instead (`static/databank.js`'s `renderPreviewRows()`/`exportDataset()`, `static/verification.js`'s `buildProcedureBrowseTableHtml()`, `static/template-viewer.js`'s `renderTemplateData()`), falling back to the old key-order behavior only if the template lookup fails. `renderCashbookTable()` (Cashbook Preview) deliberately excluded — its query has no `template_id` and Rate never appears there.

- **`client_data.extract_amount` permanently NULL on every real row (confirmed fix + backfill, `routers/import_export.py` + new `backfill_extract_amount.py`)**: found while chasing the Physical Bill Amount-match gate never triggering — `extract_columns_from_row()` used one shared `break` for both its Numeric and Date branches, and since every real template lists Date before Amount in `sort_order`, the loop always found the date first and exited before ever reaching a Numeric column, leaving `extract_amount` NULL on all 6,369 rows while `extract_date` was correctly populated. Fixed with independent found-flags per branch; also fixed the changed-row re-upload UPDATE path, which never recomputed either extracted field at all. Two related gotchas fixed at the same time: (1) the cashbook template stores both Debit and Credit Amount as real numbers (never blank), so a literal `0` must be treated as "no value here" or a Debit-side `0` on a receipt-type voucher permanently wins over the real Credit Amount; (2) Purchase Order/Store Receiving/Vendor Bill list Quantity (also Numeric) before Amount, so "first Numeric column" must yield to a column literally named "Amount" (via `find_named_column()`) when one exists — otherwise the Data Bank preview's `amount_min`/`amount_max` filter silently resolves to Quantity. New `backfill_extract_amount.py` (dry-run default, `--run` to write) backfilled all 6,369 real rows, deliberately scoped to every row regardless of `is_deleted`/`change_detection_status` (unlike `backfill_rate.py`'s live-dataset-only scope), since a voucher line's `client_data` FK target routinely has `is_deleted=1` after a later whole-dataset re-import.

## Multi-Bill/Multi-Line Physical Bill (6-phase requirement, complete)

- **Phase 1 of 6 (schema, `database.py` only)**: replaces the earlier flat Physical Bill shape (one `voucher_line_physical_bills` row = one bill, `quantity`/`rate`/`amount`/`vendor_name`/`source_document_row_id`/`source_template` all on that single row, `UNIQUE(voucher_line_id, document_id)` limiting a line to one bill per Document) with a header/items split: `voucher_line_physical_bills` keeps only `bill_no`/`bill_date`/`vendor_name` plus a new `sort_order`, and drops the UNIQUE constraint (a line can now carry several bills against the same Document). A new `voucher_line_physical_bill_items` table (`bill_id` FK, `item_name`/`quantity`/`rate`/`amount`, `source_document_row_id`/`source_template` — moved down from the header since "copy from lines" will seed one item per source Store Receiving row, each individually traceable) holds one or more item lines per bill; `amount` is stored per item (Qty × Rate, rounded to `rate_precision`), not derived live, matching the table's pre-existing convention. Upgraded via this file's established full-table-rebuild idiom (detect the old shape by the `quantity` column still living on the header table, rename→recreate both tables→copy header rows across with ids preserved→fold each old row's quantity/rate/amount/source_* into exactly one new item row keyed to that same id as `bill_id`→drop the renamed table); verified idempotent (a second `init_db()` call is a no-op) and, incidentally, exercised for real against the live dev database via an auto-reloading dev server picking up the file edit — all 9 existing bills were preserved with matching headers, each correctly folded into one item row. `routers/verification.py` (save/read endpoints, the Cleared/Query amount-match gate) and every frontend file were deliberately left untouched this phase and will not work against the new shape until Phase 2 (backend) lands.

- **Phase 2 of 6 (backend API + Cleared/Query gate, `routers/verification.py` only)**: `save_physical_bill` changed from flat `Body(..., embed=True)` fields to a nested `bills: List[Dict[str, Any]] = Body(..., embed=True)` payload (same no-Pydantic-model, typed-list idiom `save_line_items()` already established) — a full-replace upsert of a Document's *entire* bill set per save (delete-then-insert inside one `get_raw_conn()` transaction, mirroring `start_verification_session()`'s own multi-statement-write idiom), not a per-field merge. An item's Amount is now always derived (Qty × Rate, rounded to `rate_precision`) — no more standalone manual Amount input, per the confirmed "Amount (derived)" field design. An entirely-blank bill (no header data and every item itself blank) is silently dropped rather than persisted, so an unused trailing "Add Bill"/"Add line" UI placeholder never becomes a permanent phantom row on every auto-save tick. `get_voucher_line_physical_bills` now returns a nested `bills[].items[]` shape (plus a convenience `bill_total` per bill); its sibling-session dedup generalized from "latest-updated row wins per document" to "latest-touched bill SET wins per document" — the single sibling session whose bills for a document were most recently touched wins wholesale, never a mix of two sessions' bills under one document. New shared `_evaluate_physical_bill_completion(bills, voucher_amount)` (placed by `_cross_check_values_equal()`) is the one hard-lock rule now used by both `compute_and_persist_cleared_status()`'s `_physical_bill_satisfied()` (per-line) and `get_audit_workbook()`'s pre-batched `_compute_line_procedures()` (whole-session, previously a broken direct `vpb.amount` query — that column no longer exists post-Phase-1, would have errored on first real use) — every bill's header non-blank and ≥1 item, every item's amount resolvable, and the SUM of every item's amount across every bill exactly equal to the voucher line's amount, no partial credit and no rounding tolerance (only `CROSS_CHECK_FLOAT_EPSILON`). Verified against the live dev DB: `GET` on one of Phase 1's 9 migrated bills round-trips correctly (`bill_total` matches the old flat `amount`); a 2-bill/3-item `POST` round-trips via `GET`; re-`POST`ing with 1 bill leaves zero orphaned rows from the previous 2-bill save (both header and item tables); `GET .../line_status_reason/{id}` on the same line still reports its Physical-Bill-gated Document as satisfied ("documents" gate: pass).

- **Phase 3 of 6 (frontend multi-bill card UI, `static/procedure_modal.js` only)**: replaced the old one-bill-per-Document 4-field flat form (Bill No/Date/Vendor/Amount + a Quantity×Rate tap-to-calculate popover + a single-source "Copy from lines" button, all built against Phase-1's now-gone flat shape) with a card-per-bill layout matching the new nested contract. `getProcedureTabState()`'s default tab object now carries `physicalBills: []` (array of `{bill_no, bill_date, vendor_name, items: [{item_name, quantity, rate, amount}]}`, `amount` a client-cached qty×rate) in place of the old single `physicalBill`/`physicalBillErrors`/`physicalBillSourceDocumentRowId`/`physicalBillSourceTemplate` fields; `physicalBillSaved` kept as-is. Each card: Bill No/Vendor/Date header fields + a remove-bill button, an editable Item/Rate/Qty/Amount(derived)/remove-line items table, a per-card "Add line" button, and a dimmed Subtotal row; an "Add Bill" button below all cards (no bill auto-seeded on first open — an empty tab shows just the button); a Grand Total footer with a `Reconciled`/`Over by X`/`Short by X` pill vs. the voucher line's own amount, epsilon 0.005 matching `_cross_check_values_equal`, computed by the new `computePhysicalBillCompletion()`/`buildPhysicalBillReconciliationStatus()` (client mirrors of `_evaluate_physical_bill_completion()`). Rate/Qty edits are handled by a targeted DOM update (`updatePhysicalBillTotals()` repaints just that row's Amount cell + its bill's Subtotal + the Grand Total/pill) rather than a full re-render, so typing never loses focus; Add/Remove Bill/line (structural changes, not text entry) do a full `renderPhysicalBillDocumentPanel()` re-render, safe since tabState is already the source of truth for typed values. The mandatory-field red-border/tooltip cue (Bill No/Date/Vendor blank) is ported as `refreshPhysicalBillMandatoryIndicators()`, now walking every rendered bill card via `data-bill-idx`/`data-field` instead of the old fixed-id design, called at render and after a save completes — not live-per-keystroke, preserving the original intent. `isProcedureDocumentComplete()`'s `physical_bill` branch and `savePhysicalBillEntry()`/`flushPhysicalBillEntries()` (now POSTing the full `bills[]` array) were updated to match; `openProcedureModal()`'s seeding block now `.filter()`s the batch-fetched bills by `document_id` (was `.find()`, single-bill assumption) and maps each into the lean editable shape. Removed as dead/incompatible-with-the-new-shape: `validatePhysicalBillFields()` (defined but never called), the entire Quantity/Rate calculator popover subsystem, and the old single-source Copy-from-lines button/picker (Phase 5 rebuilds this against the new per-item array shape). Verified via Playwright against the live dev server (client_id 1, physical_bill Document id 19 "Vendor Bill"): page loads with zero console/page errors; the new pure functions (`recomputePhysicalBillItemAmount`, `computePhysicalBillGrandTotal`, `buildPhysicalBillReconciliationStatus`, `computePhysicalBillCompletion`) return correct values for a 2-bill/2-item scenario (grand total 120, Reconciled/Over by 20/Short by 30 for voucher amounts 120/100/150, completion correctly false for a blank bill_no or an item-less bill); a full DOM interaction simulation (Add Bill → Add line → type Rate 50/Qty 2 → Amount cell "100.00", Subtotal "100.00", Grand Total "100.00", pill "Short by 20.00" against a 120 voucher amount; blank Bill No shows the mandatory-missing class; Remove line → 0 rows; Remove bill → 0 cards, empty state shown) all passed with no page errors. **Known pre-existing gap noticed, not fixed this phase** (outside the confirmed file list): `static/verification.js`'s `updateProceduresCellForLine()` still reads a flat `bill.amount` field from the batch bills fetch for its Procedures-badge amount-match check — that field doesn't exist on the new nested shape (replaced by `items[]`/`bill_total`), so that badge's amount-match check is currently silently broken for any physical_bill Document; needs a follow-up fix touching `verification.js`.

- **Follow-up fix (`static/verification.js` only)**: fixed the gap noted above. `updateProceduresCellForLine()`'s `isDocDone` physical_bill branch now `.filter()`s `physicalBills` by `document_id` (was `.find()`, a single-bill assumption) and uses each matching bill's server-computed `bill_total` (null whenever that bill has zero items or any item's amount doesn't resolve numeric, from `_shape_physical_bill()`) instead of the no-longer-existent flat `bill.amount` — every matching bill needs non-blank bill_no/bill_date/vendor_name and a non-null `bill_total`, and the SUM of every matching bill's `bill_total` must equal the voucher line's amount within the same `0.005` epsilon, mirroring `_evaluate_physical_bill_completion()` without re-deriving item sums client-side. Kept as a small self-contained inline check in this file rather than calling into `static/procedure_modal.js`'s `computePhysicalBillCompletion()`, matching the code's existing per-file duplication convention. Verified via Playwright (live dev server): the exact replacement logic run against fixtures — no bills (incomplete), one bill matching the voucher amount (complete), two bills whose `bill_total`s sum to the voucher amount (complete, proving multi-bill summing), a bill with `bill_total: null` (incomplete), a bill with a non-matching total (incomplete), and a bill with a blank vendor_name (incomplete) — all returned the expected result with zero console/page errors.

- **Phase 4 of 6 (Enter-key field navigation, `static/procedure_modal.js` only)**: added left-to-right Enter navigation across Phase 3's multi-bill card fields (Bill No → Vendor Name → Date → each line's Item → Rate → Qty, card after card). All and only these fields already share the class `.procedure-bill-input` and are emitted in exactly this order by HTML source order, so `renderPhysicalBillDocumentPanel()`'s new `keydown` listener (wired alongside its existing `input`/`click` listeners) just walks the flat `form.querySelectorAll('.procedure-bill-input')` list on Enter and focuses the next element — no manual bill/item index arithmetic, and it flows into the next bill card automatically since cards are DOM siblings in that same order. Tab is untouched (only `Enter` is intercepted). Pressing Enter on the last field of the last line of the last bill (detected as: last in the flat list *and* `data-field === 'quantity'` — the only field that can simultaneously be true for) appends a new item to *that field's own bill* (`this.dataset.billIdx`, not an assumed "last bill index") via the same `renderPhysicalBillDocumentPanel()` re-render Add/Remove Bill/Line already use, then focuses the new line's Item field. Deliberately narrow, undocumented-by-the-brief edge case: if the last bill card currently has zero item rows, its last field is Date (not Qty), so Enter there does nothing further — the brief's trigger is specifically "last line," and a bill with no lines has none to be last; "Add line" remains how that bill's first row gets added. Verified via Playwright (live dev server, 2-bill/3-item fixture): a 10-step Enter walk from the first field produced the exact expected sequence (Bill No → Vendor → Date → item 1 → item 2 → next bill's Bill No → Vendor); a Tab keydown dispatch confirmed the handler doesn't intercept it; a separate 1-bill/1-item fixture confirmed Enter on the final Qty field grows that bill's items from 1 to 2 and moves focus to the new item's Item field — zero page errors in either run.

- **Phase 5 of 6 (Copy from lines rebuilt, `static/procedure_modal.js` only)**: rebuilt against the new nested `bills[].items[]` shape after Phase 3 removed the old single-bill version. Two open questions from the brief resolved with the user before implementing: (1) **Item Name** — neither the "Store Receiving" nor "Vendor Bill" template actually has an Item/Item Name column (confirmed by inspecting `template_column_mappings` for both — only GRN no/Bill no/Vendor/Quantity/Rate/Amount/dates), so each copied item's Item Name is left blank, same treatment as the bill's own Vendor Name/Bill No, rather than inventing a stand-in value; (2) **existing bills** — Copy from lines is only available while the Document has zero bills (the brief's own stated default), never a repeatable append. New `resolvePhysicalBillSourceType(templateId)`/`getEligiblePhysicalBillCopySourceRows(uid)` (reintroducing the Phase-3-removed pattern, adapted from a single-row picker to a batch) gather every GRN/Vendor Bill row currently linked as evidence anywhere on the line, reading Quantity/Rate straight out of the already-loaded `tabState.selections[].row_data` via the existing `getRowFieldCaseInsensitive()` helper — no new network call, since `openProcedureModal()` already warms `templateNameCache`/loads every document's selections before any tab renders, and the existing `physical_bill_source_preview` endpoint wouldn't add anything for Quantity/Rate (and doesn't resolve Item Name either). `copyPhysicalBillFromLines()` builds one new bill (blank header fields) with one item per eligible row (Quantity/Rate carried over, Amount derived via the existing `recomputePhysicalBillItemAmount()`), pushes it, and re-renders. The Copy from lines button itself is rendered only inside `renderPhysicalBillDocumentPanel()`'s empty-state branch (`bills.length === 0`) and only when at least one eligible row exists, showing the row count (e.g. "Copy from lines (2)") — the "only when empty" rule falls out for free with no extra flag, since pushing a bill flips the panel to the cards branch on its very next render, the same mechanism Add Bill/Add Line already rely on. Verified via Playwright (live dev server): a fixture with one GRN-templated Document holding 2 linked selections showed the button as "Copy from lines (2)"; clicking it produced exactly one bill with 2 items (blank Item Name, Quantity/Rate carried over as "5"/"100" and "2"/"50", Amount correctly derived as 500/100) and the button was gone on the next render; a separate fixture with zero eligible rows rendered the empty state with no Copy from lines control at all — zero page errors in either run.

- **Phase 6 of 6, FINAL (styling, `static/style.css` only)**: added CSS for the multi-bill card UI built in Phases 3-5 — none of its markup (`.procedure-bill-card`/`-card-header`, `.procedure-bill-items-table`, `.procedure-bill-item-amount`, `.procedure-bill-subtotal-row/-label/-value`, `.procedure-bill-grand-total-row/-label/-value`, `.procedure-bill-recon-pill` + `-reconciled`/`-over`/`-short` state modifiers, `.procedure-bill-empty-state`, `.procedure-bill-add-bill-btn`/`-add-line-btn`/`-remove-bill-btn`/`-remove-line-btn`) had any CSS before this phase. Bill cards match `.procedure-segment-data`'s existing border/header-bg convention so each reads as a nested mini-card; item table has a bordered header row and a muted read-only look on the derived Amount cell; each card's Subtotal row is deliberately dimmed (`#94a3b8` on `#fafbfc`) to sit visually below the bolder Grand Total footer; the reconciliation pill reuses the app's existing 3-state green/red/amber palette verbatim (`#dcfce7`/`#166534` reconciled, `#fee2e2`/`#991b1b` short, `#fef3c7`/`#92400e` over — same values as `.status-badge.pending`/`.aw-status-badge` elsewhere in this file, not new colors). All new rules scoped `#procedureModal .procedure-bill-...` per this app's per-modal CSS convention; the pre-existing `.procedure-bill-input-mandatory-missing` red-border rule (from the old single-bill design) needed no changes — confirmed it already fires correctly on a Copy-from-lines-created bill's blank Vendor Name, since `refreshPhysicalBillMandatoryIndicators()` runs at the end of every `renderPhysicalBillDocumentPanel()` call including the one `copyPhysicalBillFromLines()` triggers right after pushing the new bill, no live-as-you-type behavior needed. Old single-bill-design rules (`.procedure-bill-section*`, `.procedure-bill-grid*`, `.procedure-bill-total-row*`, `.procedure-amount-match-tick`, etc.) were left in place, unused/orphaned but harmless, since removing them was out of scope for a styling-only phase. Verified via Playwright screenshot of the new markup rendered standalone against the live `style.css` (mandatory-missing Vendor Name red border, dimmed Subtotal row, Grand Total footer with a red "Short by" pill, and the empty state with its Copy-from-lines button all rendered as designed) — completes the 6-phase requirement.

## Global Header Nav Rebuild (6-phase requirement, in progress)

- **Phase A of 6 (Up + Back core logic, `static/client_context.js` + `static/style.css` only)**: split the single ← icon (which had conflated "go to a static structural parent" and "go to whatever I was just looking at, cross-module") into two permanent icons. **Up** (`.nav-up-arrow`, "↑") reuses the old `getBackTarget()`'s exact priority chain (`<body data-nav-parent>` → `NAV_PARENT_MAP` → `index.html`), renamed `getUpTarget()`, plus a new `window.setUpOverride(fn)` hook (parallel to the pre-existing `setBackOverride` pattern) for a page with in-page views to declare a dynamic Up target. **Back** (`.nav-back-arrow`, "←") is an entirely new mechanism: a `sessionStorage`-backed chronological history stack (`navHistoryStack` key, JSON array of `{url, viewKey, label}`, capped at 20 entries, oldest trimmed first) — backed by `sessionStorage` rather than a plain JS variable because a real page navigation (e.g. Verification → Audit Workbook) reloads the whole `client_context.js` module, wiping any in-memory-only state; follows this project's established try/catch + warn-only + clear-on-parse-error sessionStorage convention. `pushCurrentPageToHistory()` pushes one entry per page load (skipping a duplicate push on a plain refresh); a new page-facing `window.pushInPageNavEntry(viewKey, label)` lets a multi-view page (Verification/Audit Workbook/Audit Rules — not yet wired, that's Phase B) push an entry for an in-page view change with no navigation. Back's click handler (`handleBackArrowClick()`) pops the stack's current entry and either calls a page's registered `window.setInPageRestoreHandler(fn)` if the new top's `url` matches the current page (same-page in-page restore) or navigates to a different page's URL — stashing the target's `viewKey` (if any) under a transient `navPendingRestore` sessionStorage key first, which the destination page's `initClientContext()` consumes via `consumePendingNavRestore()` before it does its own history push, so the restored entry isn't duplicated. Handler-registration ordering (a page must call `setInPageRestoreHandler()` before `client_context.js`'s own DOMContentLoaded-deferred restore-consumption runs) is safe because `client_context.js` is always the first `<script>` tag on every page and its auto-init defers to `DOMContentLoaded`, which fires only after every synchronous page-specific `<script>` (including any registration call) has already executed. The Back button renders `disabled` when the stack has ≤1 entry (nothing to go back to). Both icons are now `<button type="button">` elements (not anchors with a static `href`) since their destinations are resolved dynamically at click time — CSS reset their default button chrome to match the old plain-arrow-link look, plus a `:disabled` state for Back. Legacy `window.setBackOverride()` is kept defined (verification.js's `exitSession()` override still calls it) so nothing throws, but its stored value is no longer consulted by the new Back click handler — Verification's Back arrow this phase falls back to plain page-level granularity (e.g. lands on the Dashboard) instead of calling `exitSession()`, expected and temporary until Phase B ("Wire Up + Back into Verification/Audit Workbook/Audit Rules") migrates it onto `setUpOverride()`/`pushInPageNavEntry()`/`setInPageRestoreHandler()`. `NAV_PARENT_MAP` deliberately left empty this phase (population is Phase B/E's job, not Phase A's). Full 6-phase list: A (this phase, core logic) → B (wire Up+Back into Verification/Audit Workbook/Audit Rules) → C (Home icon audit) → D (merge `NAV_MANIFEST`/`FEATURE_SEARCH_INDEX` into the `⊞` grid + Search field) → E (populate remaining modules' ground-level entries) → F (tooltips/hover states + CLAUDE.md convention). Verified via `node --check` (syntax) — full browser verification deferred to a later phase once real pages are wired, since Phase A alone has no in-page-view pushes yet to meaningfully exercise the viewKey path.

- **Phase B of 6 (wire Up + Back into Verification/Audit Workbook/Audit Rules, `static/verification.js` + `static/audit_workbook.js` + `static/audit_rules.js` only)**: key finding that shaped this phase — Verification and Audit Rules both already persist their entire in-page view state in the URL (`setVerificationUrl()`/`updateAuditRulesUrl()`, both via `history.replaceState`, built originally for hard-refresh restore), so each of their in-page views has a genuinely different URL. Phase A's Back click handler detects "same page" by exact URL string match, so between these views it will always (correctly) take the "different page" branch and do a real `window.location.href` navigation — which their own pre-existing `window.onload` restore logic already resolves perfectly. This meant `viewKey`/`setInPageRestoreHandler()` reduce to handling only the narrow edge case where the popped stack entry's URL happens to exactly match the current URL (e.g. Back landing on the module's own untouched entry state) — both pages got a lightweight `restoreVerificationViewFromUrl()`/`restoreAuditRulesViewFromUrl()` (each factored out of that page's own pre-existing `window.onload` restore branches, so there's exactly one URL-to-view dispatch per page, not a duplicate) registered via `setInPageRestoreHandler()` for that case, and reused as-is for the page's own initial-load restore. **Verification**: replaced all 3 `setBackOverride()` call sites with `setUpOverride()`, and changed Up's target semantics — Up from the Cashbook view now always goes to the dashboard hub (`exitCashbookView()`) regardless of whether a session is active in the background (the old code branched on `currentSessionId` to instead resume the session; that "return to where I actually was" behavior is now Back's job, not Up's, so the branch was removed and replaced with an unconditional target), and Up from the Session view goes to the Cashbook view (`returnToCashbookFromSession()`, renamed hook, same target as before). `exitCashbookView()` now also clears Up's override (`setUpOverride(null)`) once back at the hub, so Up correctly falls back to the static default there. `pushInPageNavEntry(null, label)` calls were added inside `activateCashbookView()`/`activateSessionView()`, timed *after* their own `setVerificationUrl()` call so the pushed entry's URL matches what should be restored — placed inside the shared functions (not their individual callers) so both a fresh transition and a hard-refresh restore hit the same call, with Phase A's own dedup silently no-op'ing the restore-path case (the page's own load-time push already recorded that exact URL). Deliberately NOT pushed inside `returnToCashbookFromSession()`/`returnToSessionFromCashbook()`/`exitCashbookView()` — these are Up-equivalent "retreat" actions, not new forward progress, mirroring why Up-target functions shouldn't grow the Back stack. **Audit Workbook**: had zero `setBackOverride()` calls to begin with (confirmed via grep) and has no in-page views (one table, one screen) — only `setUpOverride()` was added, inside `window.onload`'s valid-session branch, targeting the exact same URL the existing `awVerificationBtn` peer-nav button already navigates to (`/static/verification.html?state=session&id=<id>`) — this page's structural parent is the Verification session it was opened from. `pushInPageNavEntry()`/`setInPageRestoreHandler()` were deliberately left unwired here — there's no second in-page view for them to distinguish. **Audit Rules**: also had zero `setBackOverride()` calls (confirmed via grep). Added `setUpOverride(closeAssignCategoriesView)` in `openAssignCategoriesView()` (reusing the view's own pre-existing in-page "⬅ Back" button's function as Up's target, since it already does exactly "return to the rail" correctly) and `setUpOverride(null)` in `closeAssignCategoriesView()` (now back on the rail, static default). `pushInPageNavEntry(null, ...)` calls were added in `switchEntityType()` (after its own `updateAuditRulesUrl()` call — pushes one entry per rail-tab switch, e.g. Documents → Categories) and in `openAssignCategoriesView()` (after its own `updateAuditRulesUrl()` call) — not in `closeAssignCategoriesView()`, same Up-equivalent-retreat reasoning as Verification. Every stale in-file comment referencing `setBackOverride()`/`getBackTarget()`/"back-arrow" by its old name was updated to Up/Back terminology in the same pass. Verified via `node --check` on all three files and a `grep -n setBackOverride` across all three confirming zero remaining references (exit code 1/no matches).

## Import Progress Tracking (multi-phase requirement, in progress)

- **Phase 1 of 3 (backend counter + status endpoint, `routers/import_export.py` only)**: import stays a single synchronous `POST /api/upload/import` request — no background job/queue. A new module-level `IMPORT_PROGRESS: dict` keyed by `file_id` (known to the frontend before it fires the POST, unlike any id the response itself would return) tracks `{"current": int, "total": int, "status": "processing"|"complete"}` for the in-flight import's row-write phase only — deliberately not the earlier validation loop, since that's not what's slow/worth showing progress for. Initialized right after `change_detection = compare_transactions(...)` is computed, with `total` set to the number of rows about to actually be written (`changed`+`new`+`missing` counts on a re-upload, or `len(rows)` on a first-time upload); incremented by one at the end of each iteration of all 4 write loops (changed/new/missing/first-time-insert), next to each loop's existing `inserted_count`/`updated_count`/`deleted_count` bump; flipped to `"complete"` right before the success response returns. The early `validation_failed` return path never touches it (no entry exists yet for that call). New `GET /api/upload/import-status/{file_id}` returns the dict entry or `{"current": 0, "total": 0, "status": "idle"}` if none exists (e.g. unknown file_id, or import not yet reached its write phase). No locking — a simple dict under FastAPI's threadpool is enough for this single-in-flight-import-per-file_id use case. Verified via the existing test suite (`pytest tests/ -v`, all 4 passing, no regressions).

## Client Cards Landing Page (User module, Phase 5 of 7, complete)

- New `static/client_select.html` + `static/client_select.js`, reached after login (also updated `static/login.js`'s post-login redirect from its `index.html` placeholder to `client_select.html`, closing that loop). Standalone page like `login.html` — deliberately omits `client_context.js`/the navbar, since that file's `isDashboardPage()` doesn't recognize this page and would fall into the non-dashboard branch, whose `enforceClientSelection()` would immediately redirect away because no client is selected yet — exactly the thing this page exists to let the user do. Fetches `GET /api/clients` (routers/clients.py, no backend changes needed) once into an in-memory array, mirroring `static/clients.js`'s `window.clientData` pattern. Cards reuse the existing `.module-card`/`.module-grid` classes from `style.css` verbatim (same visual language as the dashboard's module cards, per the confirmed brief) for the shell/hover/shadow behavior; card *content* (a colored avatar-initial circle, client_code badge, client_name, industry line) is page-specific markup styled via `client_select.html`'s own inline `<style>` block, the same "own `<style>` block instead of touching `style.css`" approach `login.html` already established — `style.css` itself was not touched this phase. Search bar filters the in-memory array on every `input` event against `client_name`/`client_code`/`industry` (lowercase substring match, no debounce, no backend call) — the same pattern as `clients.js`'s `filterClients()`, just reimplemented locally since this page has no shared JS with the Manage Clients admin page. Card click writes the clicked client's `id`/`client_name`/`client_code` into `localStorage` under the exact same keys `client_context.js` already reads/writes (`selectedClientId`/`selectedClientName`/`selectedClientCode`, confirmed by reading `client_context.js` directly rather than assuming) then navigates to `index.html` — deliberately `localStorage`, not `sessionStorage` (the brief's own wording), to match what `client_context.js` actually uses. This makes the dashboard and every other client_context.js-driven page recognize the selection immediately with zero changes on their end, and is explicitly a temporary client-side handoff pending Phase 6's real session-backed selection. No login-session guard on this page yet (Phase 7). Verified end-to-end via Playwright against the user's already-running dev server (port 5000, confirmed via `netstat` first, not restarted): logged in as the seeded admin, confirmed redirect landed on `client_select.html` with both seeded clients rendered as cards matching the dashboard's card visual style; typed "leather" into the search box and confirmed the grid filtered to 1 matching card with no network call; clicked a card and confirmed navigation to `index.html` with `localStorage`'s `selectedClientId`/`selectedClientName`/`selectedClientCode` correctly populated from the clicked client.
