## Client Context Load-Order Race (confirmed fix, single phase, complete)

**Reported symptom**: Client Data (Data Bank) and Trial Balance showed "no client selected" despite a valid session with a client selected. The brief's initial diagnosis was a stale-source read — a direct `localStorage` read, or a locally-declared `getSelectedClientId()`/`getSelectedClientName()` shadowing `client_context.js`'s canonical versions, the exact bug already fixed once in `databank.js` on 2026-08-22.

**That diagnosis was wrong, and was corrected before any code was touched.** Investigation found `static/databank.js` has no local shadow helpers left (the earlier fix is complete and deployed) and `static/trial_balance.js` reads the client only via `window.getSelectedClientId()`, with no `localStorage` access anywhere in the file.

**Actual root cause — a load-order race.** `initClientContext()` (static/client_context.js) is `async` and `await`s `loadSessionClient()`, a real network fetch to `GET /api/auth/current-client`, kicked off at `DOMContentLoaded`. Each page then gates its UI from `window.onload` and calls `getSelectedClientId()` *synchronously*. `window.onload` waits on subresources, which says nothing about an in-flight `fetch()` — on a light page (scripts at the end of `<body>`, no images) `onload` fires first, `sessionClientCache.id` is still `null`, and the page renders its no-client state. The file's own comment at the `await loadSessionClient()` call ("Every page's own init runs from `window.onload`, well after `DOMContentLoaded`, so this has ample time to resolve first") stated exactly this wrong assumption and has been corrected in place.

Per-page consequences: `trial_balance.js` showed its client-selection warning with Upload permanently disabled; `databank.js` reset its tables and **hard-redirected to `index.html` after 3 seconds**; `verification.js` ran `loadVerificationStats()`/`loadDataLinksCards()` with a null client id.

**Fix.** `client_context.js` had no ready signal of any kind — no event, no flag, no promise (confirmed by reading the file end to end). Added `window.clientContextReady`, a promise created at *module parse time* (not inside `initClientContext()`, so it exists before any page script's `onload` can run — `client_context.js` is loaded first on every page) and resolved at the very end of `initClientContext()`, after `loadSessionClient()`, `renderClientControl()` and `renderNavLeft()` have all completed, so an awaiting page gets both a populated cache and a rendered navbar. It always resolves and never rejects: `loadSessionClient()` already swallows its own errors and leaves the cache null, so a rejection would hang every page rather than letting it render its no-client state; a 401 inside it redirects to login and returns early, and the promise still resolving there is correct since the page is being torn down anyway.

The three reported pages then gate on it — `window.onload` stays the entry point, it just awaits first: `if (window.clientContextReady) await window.clientContextReady;` as the first statement (guarded, matching the defensive `typeof window.getSelectedClientId === 'function'` style already used across these files). `trial_balance.js` and `verification.js` became `async`; `databank.js` already was, and the await went ahead of its `initUtils()` call. `verification.js`'s `window.onload` has early `return`s (the `?state=` restore branch) — awaiting at the top is unaffected by those.

Also removed `verification.js`'s `getClientId()` fallback to `localStorage.getItem('selectedClientId')`: nothing writes that key since session-backed selection landed, so it could only ever return `null` or a stale pre-migration value. `upload.js` has two identical dead fallbacks (~lines 475 and 1748) — deliberately left, logged in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`.

**Cache-bust**: `client_context.js?v=2` → `?v=3` on all 15 HTML pages together (per this project's style.css convention — never bump only some pages, which reintroduces the split "some pages live, others stale" state), plus the three edited page scripts on their own pages (`trial_balance.js` v4→v5, `databank.js` v3→v4, `verification.js` v6→v7).

**Scope deliberately held**: `upload.js`, `audit_rules.js` and `template-viewer.js` all read the client id at `window.onload` and have the same race. Confirmed with the user as a separate follow-up phase, logged in `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`.

**Verification.** Backend suite (`pytest tests/ -v`) 4 passed, unchanged as expected for a frontend-only change. Playwright against the user's already-running dev server (port 5000, confirmed via `netstat` first and deliberately not restarted — a `--reload` server was already live in the user's own terminal): logged in as the seeded admin, selected a client, then hard-loaded all three pages twice — once normally, once with `GET /api/auth/current-client` artificially delayed ~2s via `page.route()`, which is what makes the race deterministic rather than machine-dependent. All six checks passed with no page errors: Trial Balance's warning hidden and navbar client correct, Data Bank still on `databank.html` after waiting past its 3-second redirect window, Verification rendering all 6 Client Data Links cards.

A **control run** was added specifically to prove the test could actually fail rather than being vacuously green: an init script recorded `window.getSelectedClientId()` at the exact moment the `load` event fired versus after `window.clientContextReady` resolved. Result on all three pages, under the same 2s delay — `None` at the load event, `1` after the signal. That is the race reproduced directly, and confirms the await is what closes it.

## User Module — Auth Backend (routers/auth.py, all 7 phases complete)

`POST /api/auth/login` verifies username/`bcrypt` password against `users`, 401s on bad credentials or unknown user (same message either way), 403s if `is_active=0`, logs every failed attempt to `error_log` (`module='Auth'`) via the existing `log_error()`. On success: creates a `sessions` row (`secrets.token_hex(32)` token, ~10h expiry), updates `users.last_login`, sets an HttpOnly `session_token` cookie (`samesite=lax`, `max_age`-based — not `expires`, which requires a UTC-aware datetime `Response.set_cookie` doesn't get from a naive `datetime.now()`).

`POST /api/auth/logout` deletes the session row matching the cookie's token and clears the cookie; idempotent if no session exists — this also naturally clears `selected_client_id` since the whole row is gone, no explicit clearing needed; called by `client_context.js`'s `logoutUser()` (navbar Logout button) with no request body, always 200.

`get_current_user(request)` is the reusable guard — reads the cookie, joins `sessions`+`users` on token (now also selecting `u.role`, added for the Admin role foundation phase below), raises 401 if missing/invalid, 401 "Session expired" if `expiry` (naive local time, matching `login()`'s own writes) has passed; no active purge of expired rows. Used both as a route `Depends()` (`select-client`/`current-client`) and called directly (not via `Depends()`) by `main.py`'s root route and `client_context.js`'s `loadSessionClient()`/`client_select.js`'s `guardSession()` (via the `current-client` endpoint's 401) to gate every page.

`PUT /api/auth/select-client` (body `{client_id}`) validates the client exists then writes `sessions.selected_client_id`; `GET /api/auth/current-client` reads it back — the session-backed client handoff. Registered in main.py alongside the other 10 routers.

## Admin Role Foundation (8-phase requirement, complete)

Confirmed requirement to build a firm-level Admin area (Settings tabs: App Settings | Manage Clients | Manage Users), reachable via an admin-only gear icon on the Client Select page. Originally scoped as 7 phases; renumbered to 8 after Phase 3 verification found that `client_context.js`'s `enforceClientSelection()` blocks every non-dashboard page (including the new admin pages) unless a client is selected — a new phase (6) was inserted to fix that, pushing the old Phase 6/7 to 7/8.

**Phase 1 (role foundation, complete)**: single two-tier role model (`admin` vs everything else), no third-party RBAC library, consistent with the auth module's plain `secrets`/`bcrypt` approach. `database.py`'s seed-admin block now inserts `role="admin"` (was `None`) for the placeholder `admin`/`admin123` user. `get_current_user`'s session+user join query (`routers/auth.py`) now also selects `u.role`, and a new `require_admin(session=Depends(get_current_user))` dependency raises 403 if `session["role"] != "admin"` — additive only. Verified via `pytest tests/ -v` (4 passed).

**Phase 2 (Manage Users backend, complete)**: new `routers/users.py`, mirroring `routers/clients.py`'s CRUD shape, every endpoint behind `Depends(require_admin)` — `GET /api/users` (active-only by default), `POST /api/users` (bcrypt-hash password, reject duplicate username), `PUT /api/users/{id}` (edit username/role), `POST .../deactivate`/`.../reactivate`, `PUT .../reset-password`. Audit-logs each mutation with the acting admin's real username (`session["username"]`), a small accuracy improvement over `clients.py`'s hardcoded `"Admin"` string. No self-deactivation/last-admin safeguard — deliberately deferred. `main.py` registers the new router (12 total). Verified with `pytest` plus a scripted `TestClient` run against an isolated temp DB (create/update/reset-password/deactivate/reactivate/duplicate-check/403-for-non-admin all passed).

**Phase 3 (Manage Users frontend, complete)**: new `static/users.html`/`.js`, mirroring `clients.html`/`.js`'s CRUD-page structure — sortable/searchable table (username/role/active/last login), add/edit modal (role dropdown Admin/Standard User, password field shown only on create), deactivate/reactivate toggle, and a separate Reset Password modal. `loadUsers()` treats a `403` specially (shows "Admin access required", redirects to `index.html`) as a friendlier layer over the backend's `require_admin` gate. Standalone page, no real nav entry point yet (Phase 4/7 land those) and not yet in `NAV_MANIFEST`.

**Verification finding, Phase 3**: the real dev `test.db`'s admin user still had `role=None` — Phase 1's seed logic only fires on an empty `users` table, so a pre-existing install's admin row never got backfilled. Fixed live with a one-time `UPDATE users SET role='admin' WHERE username='admin'` (confirmed with the user first). Full CRUD flow then verified end-to-end via Playwright against the live dev server (create/edit/reset-password/deactivate/reactivate/search, zero console errors), test user cleaned up afterward.

**Verification finding, Phase 3 (carried into Phase 6)**: `client_context.js`'s `enforceClientSelection()` redirects any non-dashboard page to `index.html` (with a "please select a client" alert) unless a client is selected — confirmed this is pre-existing, app-wide behavior (even `settings.html` hits it today), not specific to `users.html`. Since Manage Users/Settings are firm-level pages with no real reason to need a client selected, this blocks direct/bookmarked access to the admin area today. Flagged, not fixed this phase (out of the confirmed file list) — a new Phase 6 was inserted specifically to exempt these firm-level pages.

**Phase 4 (Settings page restructure into tabs, complete)**: `static/settings.html`/`.js` restructured into a 3-tab shell. Only "App Settings" is a real in-page panel (existing `SETTINGS_DEF` form + firm-wide Holidays, now wrapped in `#tabPanelAppSettings`, unchanged otherwise); "Manage Clients"/"Manage Users" tabs navigate via `window.location.href` to `clients.html`/`users.html` rather than rendering embedded content, since that content doesn't live here yet (Manage Clients' actual relocation is Phase 5). Tab bar styled in `settings.html`'s own `<style>` block — no shared tab pattern existed anywhere else in the codebase to reuse. `checkAdminAndShowTabs()` reuses the exact `GET /api/users` 403-probe pattern `users.js` established in Phase 3 (no dedicated "am I admin" endpoint) to reveal the two admin tabs only for an admin session. Verified via Playwright against the live dev server: admin session sees both extra tabs and both navigate correctly; a scripted non-admin test user (created and deleted for this check) sees neither tab; existing App Settings content still renders/saves correctly under the new wrapper.

**Phase 5 (Protect + relocate Manage Clients, complete)**: `routers/clients.py` gets `Depends(require_admin)` on every route except the bare `GET /api/clients` list — that one stays deliberately open since `static/client_select.js` (the Client Cards page every logged-in user, not just admins, uses right after login) depends on it; every other route (`GET/POST/PUT/DELETE` by id, `.../restore`, `GET/PUT .../voucher-prefixes`) has no caller besides `clients.js`/`client_settings.js`, both only reachable through the now-gated `clients.html`. `log_audit()` calls keep their existing hardcoded `"Admin"` string — protection only, no CRUD-logic changes this phase, so aligning with Phase 2's `session["username"]` improvement was deliberately left out. `static/clients.js` can't use its own `GET /api/clients` as a 403-probe anymore (it stayed open), so a new `checkAdminAccess()` probes `GET /api/users` instead — the same de facto "am I admin" endpoint `settings.js`'s `checkAdminAndShowTabs()` already reuses — redirecting a non-admin to `index.html` before `loadClients()` ever runs. Verified via Playwright against the live dev server: a scripted non-admin test user (created and deleted for the check) still sees the client-card grid on `client_select.html` (proving the list endpoint truly stayed open) but gets redirected off `clients.html` on direct navigation; the admin session's full CRUD flow (list of 20 real clients, add/edit/deactivate/restore icons) rendered with zero console errors.

**Phase 6 (Exempt firm-level pages from `enforceClientSelection()`, complete)**: `client_context.js` gets a narrow, named exemption — `FIRM_LEVEL_PAGES = ['settings.html', 'users.html', 'clients.html']` + `isFirmLevelPage()`, matched by pathname the same way `isDashboardPage()` already is. `enforceClientSelection()`'s guard condition became `if (!isDashboardPage() && !isFirmLevelPage())` — a one-line change, not a general opt-out mechanism. Only one call site existed (`renderClientControl()`, return value already ignored) and no other file called `enforceClientSelection()`/`window.enforceClientSelection` directly (confirmed via grep), so despite living in a globally-loaded file this was fully contained. Existing admin-role guards (Phases 3/5's `GET /api/users` 403-probes) are untouched and layer on top unchanged. Verified via Playwright against the live dev server: an admin session with no client selected loaded all three firm-level pages cleanly (no alert, content rendered normally, "Client: None selected" pill shown gracefully) while a real client-scoped page (`databank.html`) still correctly redirected; a scripted non-admin test user (created and deleted for the check) was still redirected off `users.html`/`clients.html` by the untouched 403-probe guards — `settings.html` correctly did NOT redirect it, since only that page's two admin tabs are role-gated, not the page itself (Phase 4's design).

**Phase 7 (Admin gear icon on Client Select page, complete)**: `client_select.html` gets an `⚙️` gear icon in its header, hidden by default, positioned alongside the title in a flex row. `client_select.js` adds `checkAdminAndShowGear()` — the same `GET /api/users` 403-probe pattern reused for the 4th time now (`settings.js`/`clients.js`), revealing the icon on `200`. Since this page is standalone (no `client_context.js`/`API_BASE`), the probe uses a plain relative fetch, matching this file's existing `fetch('/api/clients')`/`fetch('/api/auth/select-client')` convention. Clicking the icon navigates to `settings.html`, the Admin area's tab hub. Called from the existing `guardSession()` IIFE right after `loadClients()`, so a user about to be bounced to login never triggers the extra probe. No further changes to `settings.html`/`users.html`/`clients.html` — already firm-level-accessible since Phase 6. Verified via Playwright against the live dev server: admin session sees the gear icon and it navigates correctly to `settings.html`; a scripted non-admin test user (created and deleted for the check) sees no icon and no visual gap — screenshots pixel-identical to the standard layout aside from the icon's absence.

**Phase 8 (Remove admin links from client-scoped navbar, complete, FINAL)**: pure markup/data removal, no logic or backend changes — every route stays live, just unlinked from client-scoped surfaces now that the Phase 7 gear icon is the Admin area's sole entry point. `static/index.html`: removed the `#manageClientsCard` card and the inert "Settings"/"Users" `coming-soon` cards from the Administration `hub-group` (Setup/Audit Rules/Audit Log untouched). `static/script.js`: removed `manageClientsCard: '/static/clients.html'` from `MODULE_CARD_DESTINATIONS` (Settings/Users were never wired there, always inert). `static/client_context.js`: removed the top-level `Manage Clients` (ready) and `Settings`/`Users` (coming-soon) entries from `NAV_MANIFEST`'s Administration group — `flattenNavManifest()`/`renderNavMenuPanel()`/`renderNavSearchResults()` needed no code changes, since they all read the array generically. **Confirmed with the user and deliberately left untouched**: `Setup`'s own nested `App Settings` child link — pre-existing Setup-hub internal navigation, unrelated to this Admin-area initiative, and `setup.html` was never in this phase's file list. Verified via Playwright against the live dev server: dashboard's Administration section shows only Setup/Audit Log/Audit Rules with no visual gap; the ⊞ quick-nav dropdown and search field no longer surface Manage Clients/Settings/Users while still correctly finding Setup's own "App Settings" child; the Phase 7 gear icon still reaches `settings.html` end-to-end, proving the underlying pages/routes remain fully functional.

**All 8 phases of the Admin Role Foundation requirement are now complete.**

## Global Header Client Area Redesign (4-phase requirement, in progress)

**Goal.** Replace the leftover pre-session `🏢 Client` dropdown in the navbar with a fixed,
read-only `Client: [Name]` display on every protected page; move Logout to an icon-only control
beside the Welcome text; and make switching clients an explicit confirm-then-go-to-Client-Selection
action. No backend or schema changes anywhere in the requirement — session-overwrite on client
selection already works via `PUT /api/auth/select-client`.

Phases: **1** fixed client display (this entry) · **2** JS-owned Welcome text + icon-only Logout ·
**3** click-to-switch flow, then the `?v=N` cache-bust across all 15 pages · **4** cleanup of the
now-stale `renderClientBadge()`/`goToDashboard()`/`enforceClientSelection()`/`updateClientDependentUI()`.

### Phase 1 of 4 — fixed read-only client display (`static/client_context.js` + `static/style.css`)

**Why the dropdown was wrong, not merely redundant.** Before the User module landed, the
dashboard's `<select>` *was* client selection, and every other page rendered a read-only badge of
whatever it had set. Selection now happens on `static/client_select.html` and persists on the
session row, so the dropdown had become a second, competing writer of the same session value —
and it existed only on the dashboard, so the header read differently page to page.

**Removed** (all dropdown-only, all unreachable once the `<select>` goes): the `clientList`/
`selectedClientId`/`clientSelectElement` module state, `getClientSelect()`, `loadClientDropdown()`,
and `updateSelectedClient()`. This also drops a `GET /api/clients` fetch from every dashboard load
— `clientList` had no other consumer. `updateSelectedClient()`'s own `PUT /api/auth/select-client`
is superseded by `client_select.js`'s call, so no write path is lost.

**`renderClientControl()` rewritten.** It no longer branches on `isDashboardPage()` for *what kind
of control* to render — both paths now render the same `<span class="nav-client-display">Client:
<strong>NAME</strong></span>`. The dashboard gets that alone; non-dashboard pages keep their
existing `AREA: <module>` and `#navStats` spans, inline styles untouched, exactly as before. A
session with no client resolved (`GET /api/auth/current-client` returns nulls when
`selected_client_id` is unset) renders an explicit `Client: None selected` in the amber
`.client-none` variant rather than a blank pill.

Rendered as a `<span>`, not a `<button>`: this phase's display is genuinely read-only, and Phase 3
is what adds interactivity with its own delegated click handler. Landing a clickable-looking
element a phase early would have been a dead control in the interim.

**No new readiness gating was needed** — a point worth recording, since the brief asked for
`window.clientContextReady` gating here. `renderClientControl()` is already called from *inside*
`initClientContext()`, after `await loadSessionClient()`, so the cache is populated before it
renders; `clientContextReady` resolves after both. The load-order race that signal exists for only
affects page scripts reading the client from their own `window.onload` (see "Client Context
Load-Order Race" above). Nothing in this phase touches `window.onload`.

**`window.updateNavClientName()` retargeted, not deleted.** Its only caller was the removed
`updateSelectedClient()`, so it is now uncalled — the client can no longer change without a page
navigation, which re-renders the display anyway. But it is a `window.*` export, so rather than
leave it silently querying the now-nonexistent `.nav-client-name`, its selector was repointed at
`.nav-client-display` and it was flagged in-comment for removal in Phase 4.

**CSS.** Removed the `.nav-client select` rules and the `.nav-client label` that titled the
dropdown. Also collapsed a pre-existing duplicate: `.nav-client`/`.nav-client label` were declared
twice, identically, under two different section headings (`CLIENT DROPDOWN IN NAVBAR` and
`CLIENT CONTROLS`) — one copy kept, since `.nav-client` is still the `#clientControl` container
class in all 15 pages' HTML. Added `.nav-client-display` carrying the pill styling that previously
lived as an inline `style="…"` on the old `.nav-client-name` span — *moved* out of JS into CSS
rather than restyled, so the header looks identical to before; plus `.nav-client-display.client-none`
reusing `.client-badge.client-none`'s existing amber tokens (`#fbbf24`/`#f59e0b`) rather than
introducing new colours. `.client-badge`'s own rules were kept — `renderClientBadge()` still
references them until Phase 4 removes both together.

**Verification.** Playwright against the user's already-running dev server (port 5000, confirmed
via `netstat` first and deliberately not restarted — a `--reload` server was live in the user's own
terminal). Logged in as the seeded admin, selected a client from the Client Cards page, then
inspected the header on three pages: `index.html` (dashboard), `databank.html` (non-dashboard), and
`verification.html` (which re-renders the navbar at runtime via `setNavModule()`, so it proves the
display survives a re-render). On all three: `.nav-client-display` present reading `Client: ACME`,
computed style confirming the pill rendered from the new CSS (`rgb(30, 41, 59)` background, 16px
radius), `#globalClientSelect` absent, the old `.nav-client-name` absent, and `AREA:` correct on
the two non-dashboard pages. Zero console errors and zero page errors across the run. The single
`GET /api/clients` observed was `client_select.js`'s own card-loading call, not a dashboard one.

**Cache-bust deliberately deferred.** Per the user's instruction the `?v=N` bump happens once, at
the end of Phase 3 (the last CSS-touching phase), rather than per phase — so reviewing Phases 1–2
in a real browser needs a hard refresh (Ctrl+F5). Playwright starts with an empty cache, which is
why the verification above saw the new CSS without a bump.

---

### Phase 2 of 4 — JS-owned Welcome text + icon-only Logout (`static/client_context.js`, `static/style.css`, all 15 HTML pages)

**Two problems, one container.** The navbar's right-hand `.nav-user` div was page-owned markup, and
it had drifted: the hardcoded `👤 Welcome, …` span said **"Admin" on 8 pages** (clients,
client_settings, columns, templates, settings, setup, audit_rules, error_dashboard) and
**"Analyst" on 7** (index, verification, audit_workbook, databank, upload, trial_balance,
template-viewer). Confirmed with the user as meaningless copy drift rather than a real distinction —
`users.role` exists in the schema but is nullable and unread, and there is one seeded account.
Separately, Logout was a text button (`🚪 Logout`) rendered by `renderNavLeft()` into the *left*
group beside the brand, search and nav icons — an odd home for a session action, and it had **no CSS
rules of its own at all**, so it rendered as raw default browser-button chrome against the dark
navbar (plainly visible in the Phase 1 screenshot).

**`renderNavUser()`** is the new sibling to `renderClientControl()`/`renderNavLeft()`, following
their exact shape (look up container, guard if absent, single `innerHTML` write). It fills
`.nav-user` with a `.nav-user-name` span plus the icon-only logout button. Selected via
`document.querySelector('.nav-user')` — a *class*, unlike the id-based `#navLeft`/`#clientControl` —
because it is unique per page and adding an id would have meant a second, unrelated edit to all 15
files for no benefit. Called from `initClientContext()` after `renderNavLeft()`: it reads no session
state, so its position relative to `await loadSessionClient()` is irrelevant, but keeping all three
renders together preserves what the Phase 1 comment on `clientContextReady` already claims — that
the promise means the *whole* navbar is ready. Deliberately not called from `setNavModule()`/
`setNavStats()`, which re-render only the client control; this content is static for the page's life.

**`NAV_USER_LABEL`** holds the greeting as a module-level constant rather than inline in the
template, so there is one obvious place to change when a future roles/permissions module renders a
real username — `GET /api/auth/current-client` returns no user fields today, only client
id/name/code, so nothing dynamic was available to wire here.

**Logout button.** `title` *and* `aria-label` both set: with the text label gone the emoji is the
button's only content, and an emoji alone is not a reliable accessible name. **Its click handler
needed no change** — it is a document-level delegated listener on `.nav-logout-btn` at the bottom of
the file, the same delegation pattern the Back/Up arrows use, so moving the button between
containers was invisible to it. This was verified by actually clicking it, not assumed.

**CSS.** `.nav-user` gained `display:flex`/`align-items:center`/`gap:10px` (existing font-size/colour
untouched). New `.nav-logout-btn` rules reset the button chrome and size the icon. The hover and
active feedback was added by **extending the existing shared selector groups**
(`.nav-home-icon:hover, .nav-back-arrow:hover, .nav-up-arrow:hover` and the `:active` group below
it) rather than writing a fourth near-duplicate block — that comment block already states its intent
is that "all header icon-buttons read as one consistent set", so this honours it. `:focus-visible`
reuses `.nav-menu-toggle`'s existing `2px solid #4fc3f7`.

**The 15 pages.** 14 carried a byte-identical 3-line block (only the Admin/Analyst word differing),
collapsed to `<div class="nav-user"></div>` — the div stays as the container JS writes into, only
the inner span was deleted. `templates.html` was the exception, a single-line variant, identified
up front and edited individually so a uniform pattern couldn't silently skip it. A first pass using
a `\x{1F464}` emoji escape in perl matched nothing (byte-vs-character semantics on a UTF-8 file);
rewritten to match on surrounding structure (`<span>[^<]*Welcome,[^<]*</span>`) instead. A
follow-up grep confirmed zero `Welcome,` occurrences remain in any HTML file. `login.html`/
`client_select.html` are correctly untouched — pre-session pages with no navbar and no such span.

**Verification.** Playwright against the user's already-running dev server (port 5000, `netstat`
checked first, not restarted). Five pages covered deliberately: `index.html` and `verification.html`
(formerly "Analyst"), `clients.html` and `settings.html` (formerly **"Admin"** — where the
standardisation is actually visible), and `templates.html` (the one-line markup variant). Per page:
greeting reads exactly `👤 Welcome, Analyst`; `.nav-user`'s full text contains exactly **one**
"Welcome" (a missed span would surface as two) and no stale "Admin"; exactly one `.nav-logout-btn`
whose text is `🚪` with no "Logout" word; the button resolves inside `.nav-user` and *not* inside
`#navLeft`; both `title` and `aria-label` present; computed style confirming the chrome reset
(`rgba(0,0,0,0)` background, `border none`, `50%` radius). Then the button was clicked and the run
followed the redirect to `login.html`, proving the delegated listener survived the container move.
All checks passed on all five pages with zero console and zero page errors.

**Cache-bust still deferred** to the end of Phase 3 per the user's standing instruction, so browser
review of this phase needs a hard refresh (Ctrl+F5). Playwright starts cache-empty.

## Status Log Compression (CLAUDE.md maintenance, 2026-08-22)

**Trigger.** The Status log's own budget rule caps it at ~80 lines, with a documented drift trigger:
"if the Status log exceeds ~80 lines, stop before starting new work and flag it." It had reached
**408 entries** — 5× over — because each phase of every multi-phase requirement had been appended as
its own line, which is precisely the phase-by-phase trail `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md` exists to hold.
This is the second such compression (the first was August 2026); the Conventions note predicting
recurrence was correct.

**A second, structural problem found while doing it.** 44 entries (2026-08-16 onward) had been
appended *below* the `## Self-maintenance` section rather than under `## Status log` — so the log
was silently split in two, with the newest entries outside it. Anything counting or reading "the
Status log" would have missed the most recent third of it. Those were moved back under the heading.

**Method.** Grouped by requirement rather than by phase: a finished multi-phase requirement is now
one line ("Audit Rules module, 9 phases", "Automated cross-document validation engine, 10 phases")
instead of 9 or 10. Chronological order preserved; no requirement dropped. 408 → 73 entries.
A short preamble was added at the top of the section stating that full detail lives in the archive,
which let every individual line drop its repetitive "Full detail: CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md." suffix —
that phrase alone accounted for roughly four words on a large share of the old entries. The preamble
also states the go-forward rule explicitly: one line per *requirement*, roll a finished multi-phase
requirement up rather than appending each phase.

**Verification.** A pre-edit backup was taken to scratchpad. Afterwards: section headings unchanged
in count and order (10, same list); `git diff -U0` hunks confirmed to start at line 164 or later, so
Architecture / Conventions / Workflow rules / Dev tooling / Code Health Review are provably
untouched; `git diff` shows no `## ` heading added or removed; zero dated entries remain below
`## Self-maintenance`; the Self-maintenance block itself diffs identically; and every one of the 73
entries was word-counted programmatically against the ~25-word rule — none over. Net file size
645 → 252 lines.

---

### Phase 3 of 4 — click-to-switch flow + cache-bust (`static/client_context.js`, `static/style.css`, all 17 pages)

**The old switch flow was stale on two counts.** `confirmSwitchClient()` navigated to `index.html`,
which stopped being a client picker the moment Phase 1 removed the dashboard dropdown — so the one
surviving "switch client" path led somewhere with no way to switch. It also fired a *second*
`alert()` after the confirm, warning that "all client-related data visible on current pages will be
cleared". That was never accurate under the session-backed design: every query is `client_id`-scoped,
so switching mixes nothing and discards nothing. Two stacked dialogs for one action, the second of
them misinformation.

**Now:** the `.nav-client-display` pill is a `<button type="button">` (Phase 1 deliberately rendered
it as an inert `<span>` rather than land a clickable-looking control a phase before it did
anything). One `confirm('Switch client? Any unsaved work on this page may be lost.')` → on OK,
`client_select.html`. Cancel does nothing at all. The `alert()` is gone.

**Both states are clickable**, per the user's call. The no-client (`client-none`) state goes
*straight* to the picker with no confirm — there is nothing to lose, and it is precisely the state
where the user most needs to get there. The two are told apart at click time by reading the
button's own `client-none` class rather than re-querying session state, so what is rendered is the
single source of truth for what the click does.

**The listener is delegated by necessity, not style.** `renderClientControl()` rebuilds this
element via `innerHTML` on every `setNavModule()`/`setNavStats()` call, so a directly-bound listener
would be silently discarded on the first runtime re-render — which happens on `verification.html`
during normal use. It follows the same `e.target.closest()` shape as the existing Back/Up/Logout
handlers, bound once at module load. A dedicated test case covers exactly this (see below).

**CSS.** `cursor: pointer`, a hover that lightens against the dark navbar (`#334155`, the same
"subtle lift" language as `.nav-home-icon:hover` rather than a new colour), and a `:focus-visible`
outline reusing the existing `2px solid #4fc3f7`. Also `font-family: inherit` + `text-align: left`
— converting `<span>` to `<button>` otherwise picks up browser button defaults and visibly changes
the pill even though nothing else was restyled. The `client-none` variant keeps its amber on hover
rather than falling through to the grey one.

**Cache-bust: 17 pages, not 15, and two assets, not one.** Two corrections surfaced here, both
found by grepping rather than trusting the convention's prose:

1. The convention text said "all 15 pages", but **17** pages load `style.css` — `login.html` and
   `client_select.html` were added after that note was written. All 17 were in lockstep at `?v=8`;
   bumping only 15 would have stranded those two and recreated the exact split "some pages live,
   others stale" state the rule exists to prevent. All 17 → `?v=9` (confirmed with the user).
2. **`client_context.js` was still at `?v=3` on the 15 navbar pages** — and that file was modified in
   all three phases. Bumping the stylesheet alone would have shipped a half-applied change: the new
   CSS lands, but the JS that renders the markup it styles does not, so none of Phases 1–3 would
   appear on a normal refresh. Bumped to `?v=4`. This is now written into the convention explicitly,
   since the rule previously only described the stylesheet.

`CLAUDE.md`'s convention text was corrected for both — and now says to re-check the real page count
with a grep rather than trusting a number in prose, which is what let "15" go stale in the first
place.

**Verification.** Playwright against the already-running dev server (`netstat` checked, not
restarted), five cases, all passing with zero page errors — then re-run after the cache-bump to
confirm the bump changed nothing behavioural: (1) the display is a real `BUTTON` with
`cursor: pointer` and the right `title`; (2) Cancel fires **exactly one** dialog, of type `confirm`,
whose message contains no "cleared" wording, and the URL does not change — that single-dialog
assertion is the regression this phase removes, so it is checked directly rather than assumed;
(3) OK lands on `client_select.html`; (4) on `verification.html`, after forcing an extra
`setNavModule()` re-render on top of the page's own, the click still works — proving the delegated
listener survives the `innerHTML` rebuild; (5) with `GET /api/auth/current-client` stubbed via
`page.route()` to return nulls, the button renders `client-none` and clicking it reaches the picker
with **zero** dialogs. Also confirmed the bumped URLs return 200 and that the served files actually
contain the new rules (`nav-client-display:hover`, `goToClientSelect`) — a version bump that serves
stale content would otherwise look identical. Backend suite: 4 passed, unaffected as expected.

## Firm-Level Header for the Admin Pages (confirmed fix, 2026-08-22)

**Problem.** `settings.html`, `users.html` and `clients.html` are firm-level pages (already exempted
from client selection by Admin area Phase 6's `isFirmLevelPage()`), but they still inherited the
shared *client-scoped* header rendered by `client_context.js`. That header showed a "Client: None
selected" pill, a 🏢 dashboard icon, the ⊞ quick-nav dropdown and the search field — all routes back
into a client workspace these pages have nothing to do with. On top of that, `settings.html` and
`clients.html` carried a stray "← Back to Setup" link and `users.html` a "← Back to Dashboard" link,
each a dead-end into client territory. Net effect: a confusing flow with a permanently empty client
pill and links that led nowhere useful.

**Decision on mechanism.** The header is defined once inside `client_context.js` and selected by the
existing `isFirmLevelPage()`/`FIRM_LEVEL_PAGES` list, rather than hardcoded into the three HTML
pages. Per-page navbar markup has already drifted apart once in this app — the "Welcome, Admin" vs
"Welcome, Analyst" split across 15 pages that `NAV_USER_LABEL` was introduced to end — and one
renderer cannot drift. Keeping `client_context.js` loaded on all three also means the 401 session
guard, `API_BASE` and `logoutUser()` are reused as-is with no duplication, unlike `client_select.js`,
which had to grow its own `guardSession()` because it is a genuinely pre-session page.

### Phase 1 — Foundation (`static/client_context.js`, `static/style.css`)

- New `renderFirmLevelNav()` renders into a single `#firmNav` container: brand text, an
  "AREA: Administration" label, the `NAV_USER_LABEL` greeting, and Logout.
- **Deliberately absent, do not restore:** the client pill (`.nav-client-display`), the 🏢 home icon,
  the Back and Up arrows, the ⊞ dropdown (`initNavMenu`) and the search field (`initNavSearch`).
- The brand text is an anchor to `client_select.html` — firm-level, and the Admin area's own
  sanctioned entry point (its gear icon) — so it is a non-destructive way out that never enters
  client territory. Confirmed with the user after the brief was found to leave `clients.html` and
  `users.html` with Logout as their only exit.
- Logout reuses the existing `.nav-logout-btn` class, so the document-level delegated listener at the
  bottom of the file already handles the click; no new listener was bound.
- `initClientContext()` branches on `isFirmLevelPage()` *after* `loadSessionClient()` and its 401
  early-return, so session-expiry handling is identical on both paths.
- `pushCurrentPageToHistory()` is now skipped for firm-level pages, so an Admin page can never become
  the Back-arrow destination of a client-scoped page later in the session.
- `style.css` gained `.firm-navbar`/`.firm-nav-brand`/`.firm-nav-area`, reusing the existing dark
  navbar palette rather than new one-off colours. `.nav-user-name` had no rules of its own — on the
  client-scoped navbar it inherits font-size/colour from its `.nav-user` parent, which this header
  does not use — so those two values are restated under `.firm-nav-right .nav-user-name`.

### Phase 2 — The three Admin pages

- Each page's `<nav>` now holds a single `#firmNav` container carrying a `firm-navbar` class, in
  place of the `#navLeft`/`#clientControl`/`.nav-user` trio.
- The `back-link` anchors were deleted, and the now-dead `data-nav-parent` attributes removed (the
  Up arrow no longer renders, and both values pointed into client territory).
- **Prediction that proved wrong:** the plan stated the three page scripts would need no changes. A
  grep for remaining navigation targets found that `users.js`'s and `clients.js`'s "Admin access
  required" 403 handlers redirected a non-admin to `index.html` — the *client* dashboard, and a page
  they have no selected client for. Both now redirect to `client_select.html`. Lesson: the "no links
  into client-scoped pages" rule has to be checked against JS `location.href` assignments, not just
  HTML `href` attributes.
- **Deliberately left alone:** `clients.js`'s ⚙️ cogwheel still links to `client_settings.html`, a
  client-scoped page. Confirmed with the user: `client_settings.html` keeps its client-scoped header,
  because a separate later piece of work will reach it from inside the client dashboard instead. The
  cogwheel is removed then, once its replacement exists — not as part of this fix.
- Also left alone per the brief: `setup.html`'s "App Settings" card still links to `settings.html`.

### Phase 3 — Cache-bust bumps

`style.css?v=9` → `?v=10` on all **18** pages that load it; `client_context.js?v=5` → `?v=6` on all
**16** pages that load it; plus `clients.js?v=2`→`v=3` and `users.js?v=1`→`v=2` (both changed in
Phase 2). `settings.js` was not changed and carries no version string, so it was left as-is.

**Count correction:** CLAUDE.md's prose said "17 pages"/"15 pages" for these two figures. A grep
shows the real counts are 18 and 16 — `login.html`/`client_select.html` load `style.css` but not
`client_context.js`. The prose has been corrected. Re-check these with a grep, never from prose.

### Verification (Playwright against the already-running dev server on port 5000)

- On all three pages: `.nav-client-display`, `.nav-home-icon`, `#navMenuToggle`, `#navSearchInput`,
  `.nav-back-arrow`, `.nav-up-arrow`, `.back-link`, `#navLeft` and `#clientControl` all absent;
  `#firmNav`, `.firm-nav-brand`, `.firm-nav-area`, `.nav-logout-btn` all present. Navbar computed
  background `rgb(26, 26, 46)`, proving `style.css?v=10` actually reached the browser.
- Regression: `setup.html` (client-scoped) still renders the full client header, with no `#firmNav`.
- Back-stack: visiting `users.html` left `navHistoryStack` unchanged at the `setup.html` entry.
- Logout from `settings.html` → `login.html`; brand link from `clients.html` → `client_select.html`;
  `settings.html` with no session → `login.html` (session guard intact).
- With a client actually selected, the firm header still shows no client text.
- Backend suite: 4 passed.

**Testing note for future sessions:** the first behavioural run reported two apparent failures
(logout not navigating, client selection not taking) that were both artifacts of
`wait_for_load_state("networkidle")` returning before a *JS-initiated* navigation began. Use
`page.wait_for_url(...)` when the navigation comes from `window.location.href`, not networkidle.
Also set `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` when printing page text — this environment's cp1252 console throws
on emoji, the same quirk that breaks `python main.py` from a bash tool here.

## Shared Admin Tab Strip

**Date:** 2026-08-22 · **Type:** Fix Mode, single phase · **Scope:** frontend only (no backend,
router or schema changes)

### The problem

The three firm-level Admin pages (`settings.html`, `clients.html`, `users.html`) were supposed to
read as one Administration area, but the tab strip appeared on Settings alone. Clicking
"🏢 Manage Clients" or "👥 Manage Users" landed the user on a page with no tab strip, no way back to
the other two, and no indication of where they were. The tabs behaved as a one-way menu.

### Root cause (diagnosed before fixing)

The brief allowed for two possibilities — (a) the markup only exists on `settings.html`, or (b) it
exists everywhere but loses its active styling on navigation. **It was (a), conclusively:**

- `settings.html:175-179` held the only `.settings-tabs` markup in the entire app.
- `clients.html` and `users.html` had no tab markup at all (both read end to end to confirm).
- The `.settings-tabs`/`.settings-tab` CSS lived in `settings.html`'s own inline `<style>` block
  (lines 121-148), so copying the markup elsewhere would have rendered it unstyled anyway.
- The `active` class was a hardcoded HTML attribute plus a click-time toggle in
  `setupSettingsTabs()` that was effectively dead code — it only ran for the one tab that never
  navigated away.

### The fix

Extracted into a single shared component owned by `static/client_context.js`, following the exact
precedent `renderFirmLevelNav()` already set for the Admin navbar — that file already owned the
firm-level header, already knew which pages were firm-level (`FIRM_LEVEL_PAGES`/`isFirmLevelPage()`),
and already had a firm-level branch in `initClientContext()`.

- **`FIRM_LEVEL_TABS`** — a hand-maintained data array (`{file, label, adminOnly}`), the same
  data-not-DOM-scrape convention `NAV_MANIFEST` follows. `file` doubles as navigation target and
  active-state key.
- **`renderFirmLevelTabs()`** — fills each page's empty `#firmTabs` container. Active state is
  derived from `window.location.pathname.split('/').pop()`, the same read `isFirmLevelPage()` uses,
  so "you are here" always comes from the URL and can never go stale the way a hardcoded class did.
- **`isAdminUser()`** — a **memoised** promise around the existing `GET /api/users` 403-probe (there
  is still no dedicated "am I admin" endpoint). Memoising means the guard and the tab strip on a
  given page share one request instead of firing two. Fails closed on any error.
- **Delegated click listener**, bound once at module load (same pattern as the nav-menu document
  listeners). Clicking the already-active tab is a deliberate no-op.
- The three HTML pages each carry only `<div class="firm-tabs" id="firmTabs"></div>` after their
  `</header>` — no tab markup of their own, by design.
- `.settings-tabs`/`.settings-tab` moved out of `settings.html`'s inline block into `style.css` as
  `.firm-tabs`/`.firm-tab`/`.firm-tab.active`, in the existing firm-level section. Renamed because
  they are no longer settings-specific; all values carried over unchanged (no new colours). The old
  class names were confirmed to appear nowhere else before renaming.
- `settings.js` lost `checkAdminAndShowTabs()` and `setupSettingsTabs()` entirely.
- `clients.js`'s `checkAdminAccess()` kept its name, redirect behaviour and call site, but now
  delegates to `window.isAdminUser()` instead of issuing its own fetch.
- **`users.js` deliberately untouched** — it was on the confirmed file list, but its guard is
  `loadUsers()`'s real `GET /api/users?include_inactive=true` data call, not a separate probe, so
  there was nothing to consolidate.

**One deliberate behavioural narrowing:** `clients.js`'s old guard returned `true` for any non-403
response, so a `401` (expired session) would have passed the admin check. The shared probe requires
`res.ok`, so a 401 now fails closed. `loadSessionClient()` already redirects to `login.html` in that
case, so this is strictly a tightening with no user-visible change.

### Cache-busting

Per the standing convention that a partial bump reintroduces the "some pages live, others stale" bug
it exists to prevent: `style.css?v=10` → `?v=11` on all **18** pages, `client_context.js?v=6` →
`?v=7` on the **16** that load it. Both counts verified by grep, not taken from prose — the count in
`CLAUDE.md` has been wrong twice historically. Additionally `clients.js?v=3` → `?v=4`, and
`settings.js` was given a `?v=2` (it had never carried a version string at all, against convention,
which would have left its deletions stale in browsers).

### Verification (Playwright, headless Chromium against the live dev server)

A dev server was already listening on port 5000 (PID 12712) and was deliberately reused, not killed,
per the standing rule about persistent `--reload` servers.

As **admin**, on all three pages: 3 tabs rendered and visible; exactly one active tab and it matched
the current page; active tab computed `border-bottom-color: rgb(37, 99, 235)` and `cursor: default`;
inactive tabs computed `rgb(100, 116, 139)`. Navigation between tabs worked and the strip survived
it with the right tab active. Clicking the active tab left the URL unchanged. No console errors.

As **non-admin** — simulated by intercepting `GET /api/users` to return the same 403
`require_admin()` raises, deliberately **not** by creating a throwaway user in the live database:
only "⚙️ App Settings" visible on `settings.html` with its content still loading normally;
`clients.html` still showed "⛔ Admin access required" and redirected to `client_select.html`,
proving the shared probe did not weaken that guard.

Regression: `index.html` and `databank.html` still render the client pill, carry no `#firmTabs`, and
log no console errors — `client_context.js` is shared by every page, so this mattered. Backend suite:
4 passed.

**Testing note:** `browser.new_page()` creates a *fresh context* with no session cookie, so a
regression check written that way silently bounces to `login.html` rather than testing anything.
Reuse the already-logged-in page. Also confirmed again: this console is cp1252 and throws on emoji
in `print()` — encode to ASCII with `errors="replace"` when echoing page text back.

## Client Settings Card on the Dashboard

**Date:** 2026-08-22 | **Files:** `static/index.html`, `static/script.js`, `static/client_context.js`,
plus a `client_context.js?v=8` cache-bust bump on the other 15 pages that load it.
Phase 2 of a 3-phase requirement (Phase 1: admin tab-strip stabilisation, already landed; Phase 3:
`client_settings.html`'s own Up/Back navigation, not started).

**Why:** the only route into `client_settings.html` (per-client voucher prefix config) was the ⚙️
cogwheel on `clients.html`, which now sits behind the firm-level Admin area. Someone already working
inside a client's workspace had no direct way there. This adds a second, contextual entry point on
the dashboard. The `clients.html` cogwheel is untouched.

**The constraint that shaped the design:** `client_settings.js`'s `loadClientSettings()` reads
`?client_id=N` straight off the URL and hard-errors ("No client_id was provided in the page URL")
without one. So the card could not be a static link — the id has to be resolved from the session at
click time. `client_settings.html` itself was not modified.

**What was built:**

1. **`getClientSettingsUrl()`** (`client_context.js`, next to the other client getters, exported on
   `window`) — the single source of truth for "where does Client Settings go?", shared by the
   dashboard card and the nav manifest so the rule lives in exactly one place. Returns
   `/static/client_settings.html?client_id=<id>` when a client is selected, `/static/client_select.html`
   (the picker) when none is — the confirmed choice over dimming the card or alerting. Deliberately
   synchronous: every caller resolves it on a real click/render, long after `loadSessionClient()` has
   populated the cache, so there is no `clientContextReady` race here; the null branch means an early
   read degrades to the picker rather than to a broken page.

2. **The card** (`index.html`) — `#clientSettingsCard`, second in the Administration group between
   Setup and Audit Log, reusing `.module-card.admin-card` as-is (quieter styling, no status badge).
   **No `style.css` change was needed**, so no stylesheet `?v=` bump was involved.

3. **Function-valued destinations.** `MODULE_CARD_DESTINATIONS` (`script.js`) now accepts either a
   URL string or a function returning one; the existing listener loop resolves it at click time.
   `NAV_MANIFEST` got the same treatment via a new shared `resolveNavItemUrl(item)` helper, called at
   the two places an `href` is built from an item — `renderNavMenuPanel()`'s `renderItem()` and
   `renderNavSearchResults()`'s ready-row branch. Both run on demand (dropdown open / keystroke), well
   after the session cache is populated, so the resolved href is always current. Every existing string
   `url` passes through untouched.

4. **NAV_MANIFEST entry** — "Client Settings" under Administration, `module: 'Client Settings'`, with
   `keywords: ['voucher prefix', 'prefixes', 'cash payment', 'bank receipt', 'client config']`. It is
   client-scoped, not firm-level, so it sits in every logged-in user's Administration group alongside
   Setup rather than behind the Admin gear.

**Pre-existing bug found and fixed while verifying:** `flattenNavManifest()` carried `keywords`
through for **children only** — the top-level push omitted the field entirely. Until now no top-level
item had declared any, so nothing had ever surfaced it. Live proof: searching "prefix" returned zero
matches even though the entry declared that keyword, while "Client Settings" (a label match) worked.
Fixed by adding `keywords: item.keywords || []` to the top-level push, symmetric with the child push
and inert for every item that declares none.

**Verified live** (Playwright, headless Chromium against the running dev server on :5000, logged in
as `admin`, client "ACME" selected):
1. Card renders in the Administration group, no status badge, correct label/description.
2. `getClientSettingsUrl()` evaluated in-page → `/static/client_settings.html?client_id=1`.
3. ⊞ dropdown's "Client Settings" href → same resolved URL, not a bare `client_settings.html`.
4. Nav search "prefix" → matched via keywords **after** the flatten fix (empty before it).
5. Card click → landed on `client_settings.html?client_id=1`, heading read "Voucher prefix
   configuration for ACME", prefixes loaded.
6. `performance.getEntriesByType('resource')` on a fresh dashboard load confirmed
   `client_context.js?v=8` and `script.js?v=3` were actually fetched, not stale cached copies.
7. Backend suite: 4 passed. `node --check` clean on both changed JS files.

**Testing note (again):** this console is cp1252 and throws `UnicodeEncodeError` on emoji in
`print()` — `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` on the Playwright invocation is the fix used here, an
alternative to the `errors="replace"` encode noted in the previous entry.

## Entry-Aware Up/Back Navigation for Client Settings

**Date:** 2026-08-22 | **Files:** `static/client_context.js`, `static/client_settings.html`,
`static/clients.js`, plus a `client_context.js?v=9` bump on the other 15 pages that load it.
Phase 3 of 3 (FINAL) — after the admin tab-strip stabilisation and the dashboard Client Settings card.

**Why:** the previous phase gave `client_settings.html` a second door (the dashboard card and the ⊞
nav entry, both via `getClientSettingsUrl()`), but the page still declared
`<body data-nav-parent="clients.html">` and shipped a fixed `← Back to Manage Clients` header link.
A user arriving from the dashboard was pointed back at an admin-gated page they might have no rights
to. The way out now depends on the way in.

**Read-only check (per the brief's "grep JS redirects, not just HTML hrefs" note, which caught two
missed redirects in an earlier Admin phase):** `client_settings.js` contains **no** `location.href`,
redirect, or guard logic at all — its only navigation-relevant read is `?client_id=` in
`loadClientSettings()`. `client_settings.html` has no inline script. Nothing hidden was found; that
file was not edited.

**Back was deliberately left alone.** The ← arrow is already the chronological sessionStorage stack,
which returns to whatever page you actually came from. One nuance recorded rather than "fixed":
`clients.html` is a firm-level page and `initClientContext()` deliberately keeps firm-level pages out
of that stack, so Back will never return to the cogwheel. Up is precisely the mechanism that covers
that door — which is why the fix belongs in `getUpTarget()` and not in the history stack.

**Mechanism chosen: an explicit `&from=` stamp, over inferring the door from the history stack.**
Both were compared; the param wins on three counts, not just the obvious one:
1. It is part of the URL, so it survives a refresh, a restored or duplicated tab, and a pasted link.
   `sessionStorage` is per-tab and empty in a new one.
2. Inference is *structurally* unable to detect the admin door at all — the stack excludes firm-level
   pages by design, so `clients.html` is never in it. The door that most needs distinguishing is the
   one inference cannot see.
3. Each door declares its own identity at its own call site, greppable, rather than depending on
   stack-shape assumptions a later nav change could silently invalidate.
Cost: every door must remember to stamp. Mitigated by there being exactly two call sites and a safe
fallback.

**What was built** (all in `client_context.js` unless noted):

1. **`NAV_ENTRY_SOURCES`** — whitelist table beside `NAV_PARENT_MAP`, mapping a `from` key to
   `{file, label}`: `clients` → `clients.html` / "Manage Clients", `dashboard` → `index.html` /
   "Dashboard". **A lookup, never `'/static/' + fromParam`** — concatenating the raw param would be
   an open redirect. Unknown or absent keys fall through.
2. **`getNavEntrySource()`** — reads `?from=`, returns the whitelisted entry or null. Shared by the
   two consumers below so the arrow and the link cannot disagree, which is exactly how they drifted
   apart originally.
3. **`getUpTarget()`** — one new highest-priority step ahead of `data-nav-parent`. The original
   `data-nav-parent` → `NAV_PARENT_MAP` → `index.html` chain is untouched beneath it, so every other
   page resolves exactly as before (verified: `columns.html` still → `setup.html`).
4. **`renderUpLinks()`** — points any anchor marked `data-nav-up-link` at `getUpTarget()`'s result
   and relabels it from the same table. Opt-in per anchor, so no other `.back-link` in the app is
   affected. Called from `initClientContext()`'s client-scoped branch. With no recognised `from`, it
   labels whatever `getUpTarget()` actually resolved (looked up by filename) rather than trusting the
   HTML's shipped text.
5. **`getClientSettingsUrl()`** now appends `&from=dashboard`, covering both the card and the nav
   entry in one edit. The no-client branch (→ `client_select.html`) is unchanged.
6. **`client_settings.html`** — `data-nav-parent` removed (the hardcoded assumption being fixed); the
   header link marked `data-nav-up-link` with a dashboard-pointing pre-JS default. Navigation
   attributes only; no content, styling, form or explainer changes.
7. **`clients.js`** — one line: `&from=clients` on the cogwheel redirect.

**Fallback choice (confirmed with the user):** with no `from` at all — a hand-typed URL, an old
bookmark, a pre-change saved link — Up goes to the **dashboard**, not `clients.html`. A Standard User
is then never sent by a nav control to a page `clients.js` would bounce them off with "Admin access
required".

**Verified live** (Playwright, headless Chromium, logged in as `admin`, client "ACME"):
1. Dashboard card → `?client_id=1&from=dashboard`; `getUpTarget()` = `/static/index.html`; link read
   "← Back to Dashboard"; clicking Up actually landed on `index.html`.
2. ⊞ nav entry → identical stamped URL and Up behaviour.
3. `clients.html` cogwheel → `&from=clients`; `getUpTarget()` = `/static/clients.html`; link read
   "← Back to Manage Clients"; Up landed on `clients.html`.
4. Hard reload on a `from=clients` URL → resolution survived intact (the case inference fails).
5. No `from` → `/static/index.html` + "← Back to Dashboard", prefixes still loaded ("Voucher prefix
   configuration for ACME").
6. Injection guard: `from=https://evil.com`, `from=nonsense`, `from=../../etc/passwd` — all three
   fell through to `/static/index.html`, no attacker-controlled target.
7. Regressions: `columns.html` still → `setup.html` (its `data-nav-parent`), `databank.html`/
   `upload.html` still → `index.html`, and none of the three carries a `data-nav-up-link` anchor, so
   `renderUpLinks()` is a no-op there. `client_context.js?v=9` confirmed actually fetched.
8. Backend suite: 4 passed. `node --check` clean on both changed JS files.

## Lightweight Header on the Client Cards Page (2026-08-22)

**Requirement (single phase).** `static/client_select.html` — the landing page reached straight
after login — was the only post-login page in the app with no header at all: no app identity, no
indication of who was logged in, and **no way to log out without first selecting a client**. Added a
minimal header showing `System Analyst` / `Module: Client` / `👤 Welcome, <username>` / 🚪 logout.

### Gate check: is there a shared header component to reuse?

The brief gated this phase on the Admin tab-bar work being complete, so it would be known whether a
genuinely shared header existed. It does — `renderFirmLevelNav()` plus the `.firm-nav-*` CSS family,
both in `client_context.js`/`style.css`. **But it is not reusable as a renderer here, and this is the
one design decision worth recording:**

`client_select.html` cannot load `client_context.js` at all. `initClientContext()` runs on
`DOMContentLoaded`; this page is neither the dashboard nor a member of `FIRM_LEVEL_PAGES`, so
`enforceClientSelection()` would fire its "⚠️ Please select a client from the Dashboard first" alert
and redirect to `index.html` — bouncing the user off the very page whose job is selecting a client.

So the brief's stated fallback was taken: **reuse the shared CSS classes verbatim, render the ~10
lines of markup from this page's own script.** No CSS was duplicated — `style.css` needed no change
whatsoever, which was the check confirming the classes really are shared rather than settings-specific.

Two deliberate differences from `renderFirmLevelNav()`'s output:
1. The brand `System Analyst` is a plain `<span>`, not an `<a>` — on the three Admin pages that
   brand links *to* `client_select.html`, so here it would be a self-link to nowhere.
2. The area label reads `Module: Client`, not `AREA: Administration` — this is the client picker,
   not the Admin area.

### The username was not available (decision point)

The app had no real username anywhere: every header rendered the hardcoded constant
`NAV_USER_LABEL = '👤 Welcome, Analyst'` (`client_context.js:83`), and `GET /api/auth/current-client`
returned only `client_id`/`client_name`/`client_code`. Two options were put to the user — hardcode a
fourth copy of the greeting (no backend change, but not the real name, and planting exactly the
per-page drift `NAV_USER_LABEL` was created to end), or make it real. The user chose to make it real.

`current_client()` now returns `username` on **all three** of its return points — including the two
"no client selected" null branches, which is the branch this page actually hits (a session that has
not picked a client yet is this page's normal state; adding the field only to the success branch
would have shipped a header that never showed a name). `get_current_user()` already selects
`u.username` in its existing join, so this costs no extra query and no schema change. Purely
additive: the endpoint's only two callers (`client_context.js`'s `loadSessionClient()` and
`client_select.js`'s `guardSession()`) read named fields.

### Other changes

- **Page padding moved off `<body>`.** `body { padding: 40px 24px }` would have inset the navbar
  from the window edges, which no other page does. Body padding is now `0`, with the equivalent
  padding moved onto `.client-select-header`/`.client-select-grid-wrap`. Their `max-width` went
  `900px → 948px` to compensate: `box-sizing: border-box` is global (style.css reset), so without
  that the content column would have silently narrowed by the 48px of new padding.
- **`logout()` is a local copy** of `client_context.js`'s `logoutUser()`. Required, not laziness:
  the delegated document-level `.nav-logout-btn` listener also lives in `client_context.js`, which
  this page does not load. Same contract — POST, then redirect to login regardless of the response,
  so a failed request can never leave the user stuck.
- `guardSession()` previously discarded the response body and checked only `res.ok`; it now parses
  the JSON, since that body is the greeting's only source.
- Script tag bumped to `client_select.js?v=1` per the per-script cache-bust convention.

### Verification (live, not inferred)

Backend suite: 4 passed. A dev server was already listening on port 5000 (PID 9444, the user's own
`--reload` process — checked with `netstat` before doing anything, per convention, and not killed);
it picked the change up on its own.

`GET /api/auth/current-client` with a real logged-in cookie returned
`{"client_id":null,...,"username":"admin"}` — confirming the null branch, the one that matters here,
carries the name.

Playwright headless Chromium, full login→logout round trip:
1. Header text: brand `System Analyst`, area `Module: Client`, greeting `👤 Welcome, admin` (the real
   username, not the `Analyst` constant), logout button `🚪` with `aria-label="Log out"`.
2. Navbar geometry `{x:0, y:0, width:1280, height:70}` — full-bleed and flush to the top, i.e. the
   body-padding move worked.
3. Content below starts at exactly `y:70` with a `948px` box → `900px` content column, unchanged
   from before the header existed. No horizontal page scroll.
4. Client cards still render (2 clients), and the admin `⚙️` gear is still visible and unmoved.
5. Clicking 🚪 → redirected to `login.html`; navigating back to `client_select.html` bounced
   straight to `login.html` again, proving the session was genuinely destroyed, not just navigated
   away from.

### Left deliberately out of scope

`client_context.js:82`'s comment ("`GET /api/auth/current-client` returns no user fields today") is
now stale. Fixing a comment would require bumping `client_context.js?v=N` across 16 pages, so it was
logged to `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` instead, to be corrected when `NAV_USER_LABEL` is next touched to render
the real username app-wide. That app-wide change is itself a separate requirement, not this one.

## Fix: clients.html Cogwheel Blocked Despite a URL client_id (2026-08-22)

**Phase 1 of a 2-phase Fix Mode requirement.** Preceded by a read-only investigation (see the
Status log entry) that reproduced both faults live before any code was touched.

### The bug

The Admin-area cogwheel on `clients.html` builds a fully-resolved
`client_settings.html?client_id=1&from=clients` — the destination's client id is right there in the
URL. But `enforceClientSelection()` (`static/client_context.js`) decided whether a page could load
by checking **only** the session's `selected_client_id`, never the URL. In the normal Admin flow
(client picker → gear → Settings → Manage Clients) no client is ever selected, so the cogwheel
navigated correctly and was then immediately evicted with "⚠️ Please select a client from the
Dashboard first" and bounced to `index.html`.

`client_settings.js`'s `loadClientSettings()` reads `?client_id=` straight off the URL and hard-errors
without one — the page is *designed* to be URL-driven. The guard was the piece out of step, which is
why the fix is scoped to `client_context.js` and `clients.js` was left untouched.

### Why the exemption is a named whitelist, not "any page with a client_id param"

The obvious fix — let any page through if the URL carries a `client_id` — would have been wrong, not
merely broad. Every other client-scoped page (`databank.html`, `verification.html`, `upload.html`, …)
resolves its client from `getSelectedClientId()` (the session cache), **not** from the URL. Exempting
those on the strength of a param they never read would let them load with a null client and render a
broken page — trading a clear message for silent breakage.

So the fix adds `URL_CLIENT_SCOPED_PAGES` (currently `['client_settings.html']`), deliberately
mirroring the two lookup-table conventions already in this same file — `FIRM_LEVEL_PAGES` and
`NAV_ENTRY_SOURCES` (which CLAUDE.md states is a lookup table *on purpose*, for the open-redirect
reason). The rule for adding to it is stated in the code comment: a page belongs there only if its
own loader actually reads `?client_id=` off the URL.

Supporting helpers, both new:
- `getUrlClientId()` — parses `?client_id=` using the **same** validation `loadClientSettings()`
  applies (`!idParam || isNaN(parseInt(idParam, 10))`, else `parseInt(idParam, 10)`). Deliberately
  the same shape so the guard and the loader can never disagree about what counts as a valid id: a
  value the guard accepted but the loader rejected would wave a page through only for it to
  hard-error on arrival.
- `hasUrlSuppliedClient()` — requires **both** that the current file is whitelisted and that the id
  is valid. A stray `?client_id=` anywhere else grants nothing.

`enforceClientSelection()` gained a single early `if (hasUrlSuppliedClient()) return true;` inside its
existing no-client branch; the alert/redirect path is otherwise unchanged.

### Not a security regression

Verified rather than assumed: every endpoint `client_settings.js` calls — `GET /api/clients/{id}`,
`GET`/`PUT /api/clients/{id}/voucher-prefixes` (`routers/clients.py`) — sits behind
`Depends(require_admin)`. This guard is UX, not authorization; a non-admin crafting the URL gets 403s
and an error message, never data.

### Explicitly not touched

`NAV_ENTRY_SOURCES`/`getUpTarget()`/the `?from=` whitelist from the immediately-prior phase (a
different parameter, no interaction — and regression-tested below); `clients.js` (its URL building was
already correct); `getClientSettingsUrl()` (Phase 2's subject — touching it here would have blurred
the two faults together).

### Fault A is NOT fixed by this — confirmed before scoping, as the brief required

The dashboard card / ⊞ nav landing on `client_select.html` fails at a different point: it fails
*before navigation*. `getClientSettingsUrl()` resolves to `/static/client_select.html` at click time,
so `client_settings.html` never loads and this guard never runs. The two faults share a symptom and a
file, not a mechanism. Phase 2 stays necessary and does not shrink — though it may change shape, since
`client_settings.html?client_id=N` is now genuinely reachable with no session client, making "pass the
id in the URL" a Phase 2 option that did not exist before this fix.

### Verification (live)

`node --check` clean. Backend suite 4 passed (no backend change; run as a guard).

1. **The fix** — fresh login, no client selected, `clients.html` → cogwheel: landed on
   `client_settings.html?client_id=1&from=clients`, **zero alerts**, and the page rendered real data
   ("Voucher prefix configuration for ACME", 6 prefix chips) rather than the "No client specified" error.
2. **Guard still fires where it should** — `databank.html` with no client → alert + redirect to
   `index.html`, as before. Crucially, `databank.html?client_id=1` *also* still alerts and redirects,
   proving it is the whitelist and not the bare param that grants entry.
3. **Invalid id still blocked** — `client_settings.html?client_id=abc` → alert + redirect.
4. **`?from=` navigation intact** — with a client selected, dashboard card → `from=dashboard`,
   "← Back to Dashboard", Up `/static/index.html`; cogwheel → `from=clients`, "← Back to Manage
   Clients", Up `/static/clients.html`. Injection guard held: `from=https://evil.com` fell through to
   `/static/index.html`.
5. `client_context.js?v=10` confirmed actually fetched by the browser (bumped from `v=9` across all
   16 pages that load it — verified by grep, not by trusting the count in prose; `client_select.html`
   correctly does not load it and was rightly excluded).

### Known cosmetic side effect (flagged, not fixed — logged to KNOWN_ISSUES.md)

On `client_settings.html` reached with no session client, the navbar pill reads "Client: None
selected" while the page heading reads "Voucher prefix configuration for ACME" — confirmed live.
Cosmetic only; fixing it means touching `renderClientControl()`, outside this brief's scope.

## Fix: Dashboard Card Loses Intent When No Client Is Selected (2026-08-22)

**Phase 2 of 2 (Fix Mode), completing the pair opened by the read-only investigation.** Phase 1 fixed
the `clients.html` cogwheel; this fixes "Fault A", the other half.

### The bug

Clicking the dashboard's "⚙️ Client Settings" card — or the ⊞ nav entry — with no client selected sent
the user to `client_select.html`, and after they picked a client they landed on the **dashboard**, not
Client Settings. Their original intent was silently discarded.

Phase 1 could not have fixed this, and this is worth recording because the two faults share a symptom
and a file: this redirect happens **at click time**, inside `getClientSettingsUrl()`, *before* any
navigation occurs — so `client_settings.html` never loads and Phase 1's `enforceClientSelection()`
guard never runs on this path. Confirmed before scoping, at the user's explicit request.

The "pass `client_id` in the address" alternative was considered and rejected upstream: in the
no-client state there is no id to pass. That is the whole problem.

### The fix

`getClientSettingsUrl()`'s no-client branch now returns `/static/client_select.html?next=client_settings`.
`client_select.js`'s `selectClient()` resolves that key after a successful selection and routes to
`/static/client_settings.html?client_id=<just-selected-id>&from=dashboard`.

One change covers **both** entry points, because the dashboard card (`script.js`'s
`MODULE_CARD_DESTINATIONS`) and the ⊞ nav entry (`NAV_MANIFEST`) already resolve through that single
shared helper.

### Where the whitelist lives, and why (the one real design decision)

`NEXT_DESTINATIONS` lives in **`client_select.js`**, not beside `NAV_ENTRY_SOURCES` in
`client_context.js`, for a structural reason: `client_select.html` is a standalone pre-session page
that **cannot load `client_context.js` at all** (loading it would trip `enforceClientSelection()` and
bounce the user off the very page whose job is selecting a client — the same constraint that shaped
the lightweight-header phase). So the consumer cannot read a table defined in the stamper.

This is also the better placement on its own merits: the security-critical resolution sits at the
point of use, and there is exactly one copy rather than two that can drift.

`client_context.js` writes only a bare key (`client_settings`) that means nothing on its own — never a
path or URL.

```js
const NEXT_DESTINATIONS = {
    client_settings: { file: 'client_settings.html', from: 'dashboard' },
};
```

`from` is carried as data on the destination rather than hardcoded where the URL is built, so the
arriving page's Up arrow/back-link resolve through `NAV_ENTRY_SOURCES` to the door the user actually
came through. `from=dashboard` is correct here because both stamping entry points are the
client-scoped door — matching what `getClientSettingsUrl()`'s *other* branch already stamps when a
client is selected. The Admin door keeps its own `from=clients` at its own call site, untouched.

**SECURITY:** `resolveNextUrl()` is a whitelist lookup, never concatenation. `'/static/' + nextParam`
would be an open redirect — the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md already calls out for `NAV_ENTRY_SOURCES`.
An unknown or absent key returns `null` and `selectClient()` falls back to `/static/index.html`, i.e.
precisely the previous behaviour.

### Dependency on Phase 1 worth noting

This phase *relies* on Phase 1: the destination now loads with no session client only because Phase 1
taught `enforceClientSelection()` to accept a URL-supplied `client_id`. Without it, the `?next=` hop
would have delivered the user to a page that immediately evicted them — the two fixes compose.

### Verification (live)

`node --check` clean on both changed files. Backend suite 4 passed (no backend change; run as a guard).

1. **The fix** — fresh login, no client picked, dashboard → Client Settings card:
   step 1 → `client_select.html?next=client_settings`; after clicking a client card, step 2 →
   `client_settings.html?client_id=1&from=dashboard`, rendering real data ("Voucher prefix
   configuration for ACME"), zero alerts, Up arrow/back-link reading "← Back to Dashboard" →
   `/static/index.html`.
2. **⊞ nav entry** — `getClientSettingsUrl()` resolved to the same stamped picker URL, confirming both
   doors are covered by the one helper.
3. **Open-redirect regression** — `?next=https://evil.com`, `?next=../../etc/passwd`, `?next=nonsense`
   and `?next=//evil.com` (protocol-relative, the one most likely to slip past a naive check): all four
   fell through to `/static/index.html` after selection. No attacker-controlled destination.
4. **No-regression** — a plain login with no `?next=` still lands on the dashboard after selection.
5. **Phase 1 still holds** — cogwheel with no client selected still reaches
   `client_settings.html?client_id=1&from=clients` with "← Back to Manage Clients" and no alert;
   `databank.html?client_id=1` still blocked (1 alert, redirected to `index.html`).
6. **Client already selected** — dashboard card still goes straight to Client Settings, no picker hop.
7. `client_context.js?v=11` and `client_select.js?v=2` both confirmed actually fetched. Both files
   changed, so both were bumped — bumping one and not the other would ship a half-applied change.

`client_select.html` needed no markup change; its only edit was the `client_select.js?v=` bump.

### Also in this commit

`NAV_USER_LABEL`'s comment in `client_context.js` corrected — it claimed
`GET /api/auth/current-client` "returns no user fields today", untrue since that endpoint gained
`username`. Deferred one phase earlier purely because it would have cost an app-wide cache-bump; this
phase needed that bump anyway, so it came free. Its `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` row stays in place per that
file's own append-only rule.

### Known limitation (flagged, logged, not fixed)

If the session expires mid-flow, `guardSession()` bounces to `login.html`, and `login.js` returns to
`client_select.html` **without** the `?next=` — intent is lost. Rare, and the outcome is safe (picker,
then dashboard). Logged to `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` rather than widening this phase's scope.
